metadata.title: Uniform stratified vanishing and equidistribution on $\mathbb{G}_m^d$

extraction_notes.note: The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal on sketch proofs, but rigor is not allowed on proofs (the finishing step warns); the four outline sketches keep alternative proves edges and carry no rigor.
The paper recalls cited properties as labelled lists (C1)-(C7), (GL1)-(GL6), (T1)-(T5); each item is one external node (definition or theorem) so that the \ref{item:..} citations resolve to it.

T5 mixes the FFK definition of unramified characters with the paper's own identification alpha_m = phi_{mu_m}, a cited inclusion and the Frobenius trace identity; typed definition. T1 also introduces <M> and the tannakian groups but is typed theorem.

The outline (Section 1.2) sketches the proofs in running text; each sketch paragraph was taken as a proof node, and the definitions it restates are recorded as also_stated_at of the later definitions.

Historical discussion in the introduction (Katz, Zurbuchen, Bonolis-Kowalski-Woo, the FFK conditional horizontal theorem) only cites results without stating them and gets no nodes; the leitfaden figure is omitted in the source.

nodes.name: Finite field, prime l and split torus
nodes.statement: Let \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\) be a finite field of characteristic \(p\), let \(\bar k\) be a fixed algebraic closure of \(k\), let \(\ell\neq p\) be a prime, and let \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) be the split \(d\)-dimensional torus.
also_stated_at: Throughout, \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\) is a finite field of characteristic \(p\), \(k_n=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\), and \(\bar k\) is a fixed algebraic closure of \(k\). We fix a prime \(\ell\neq p\) and an algebraic closure \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) of \(\mathbb Q_\ell\).

nodes.name: Geometric torus
nodes.statement: We write \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\bar k\) for its geometric base change and use unadorned \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) for this geometric torus.
also_stated_at: We write \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) for the split \(d\)-dimensional torus and \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\bar k\) for its geometric base change.

nodes.name: Degree-n extension k_n
nodes.statement: For \(n\ge1\), \(k_n=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\) denotes the extension of \(k\) of degree \(n\) inside \(\bar k\).

nodes.name: Kummer local system attached to a character
nodes.statement: Through the Lang isogeny, a character \(\chi:\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)\to\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}^\times\) determines a rank-one Kummer local system \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\).

nodes.name: Twist M_chi
nodes.statement: If \(M_0\) is perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) and \(M\) is its geometric base change, we set \(M_\chi=M\otimes\mathcal{L}_\chi\).

nodes.name: Character sum S(M_0;k_n,chi)
nodes.statement: To this we can associate a character sum \[ S(M_0;k_n,\chi)=\sum_{x\in \mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}t_{M_0}(x;k_n)\,\chi(x), \] where \(t_{M_0}\) is the trace function of \(M_0\).
nodes.statement_short: The character sum of the trace function of M_0 against a multiplicative character chi of G_m^d(k_n).

nodes.name: Gabber-Loeser generic vanishing on tori
nodes.statement: Assuming resolution of singularities and simplification of ideals for varieties of dimension \(<d\), they proved that the locus where the forget-supports morphism \(R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,M_\chi)\to R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,M_\chi)\) is \emph{not} an isomorphism is contained in a finite union of translated algebraic cotori of the character scheme \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) \cite[Th.~4.1.1']{GabberLoeser1996}.
assumptions: Assuming resolution of singularities and simplification of ideals for varieties of dimension \(<d\)
conclusions: the locus where the forget-supports morphism \(R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,M_\chi)\to R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,M_\chi)\) is \emph{not} an isomorphism is contained in a finite union of translated algebraic cotori of the character scheme \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\)
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally, the characters where forget-supports fails to be an isomorphism lie in finitely many translated cotori.

nodes.name: Forey-Fresan-Kowalski equidistribution on average
nodes.statement: For a fixed generically unramified, arithmetically semisimple\footnote{A perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) is \emph{arithmetically semisimple} if it is semisimple as a perverse sheaf over \(k\) \cite[\S1.12]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. On a torus every arithmetically semisimple object is generically unramified \cite[Th.~3.27]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, and Zurbuchen \cite{Zurbuchen2026} has recently proved generic unramifiedness for every perverse sheaf on a connected commutative algebraic group.} object \(M_0\) pure of weight zero, they proved that the classes \(\Theta_{M_0,k_n}(\chi)\) attached to the unramified characters equidistribute on average as \(n\to\infty\) \cite[Th.~4.11]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.
nodes.statement_short: For a fixed generically unramified arithmetically semisimple weight-zero object, Frobenius classes of unramified characters equidistribute on average as n grows.

nodes.name: Arithmetically semisimple perverse sheaf
nodes.statement: A perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) is \emph{arithmetically semisimple} if it is semisimple as a perverse sheaf over \(k\) \cite[\S1.12]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.
differentia: it is semisimple as a perverse sheaf over \(k\)

nodes.name: Horizontal equidistribution on tori of dimension at least two
nodes.statement: Forey--Fres\'an--Kowalski developed the corresponding theory for multiplicative characters of connected commutative algebraic groups, including their horizontal equidistribution theorem \cite[Th.~4.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. For tori of dimension at least two, this theorem was left open \cite[Rem.~4.20(2)]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.
nodes.statement_short: The horizontal equidistribution theorem of FFK was left open for tori of dimension at least two.

nodes.name: Sawin complexity c_u
nodes.statement: For \(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), \(c_u(K)\) denotes Sawin's complexity relative to the embedding \(u_d\) fixed in \S\ref{sec:embeddings} and recalled in \S\ref{sec:complexity}.

nodes.name: Gabber-Loeser character scheme
nodes.statement: We denote by \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) the Gabber--Loeser scheme of \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}^{\times}\)-characters of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) (\S\ref{sec:characters}).

nodes.name: Kummer twist K_chi
nodes.statement: Its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points parametrize the Kummer sheaves \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\), and we put \(K_\chi=K\otimes\mathcal{L}_\chi\).

nodes.name: Forget-supports morphism phi_{K,chi}
nodes.statement: Applied to the structure morphism of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and the complex \(K_\chi\), the transformation \eqref{eq:forget-supports} gives the morphism \[ R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi) \xrightarrow{\varphi_{K,\chi}} R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi). \]

nodes.name: Gabber-Loeser locus Delta(K)
nodes.statement: Following Gabber--Loeser, let \(\Delta(K)\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) be the support of the cone of the comparison morphism between the two Mellin transforms of \(K\), as recalled in \ref{item:GL2} of \S\ref{sec:mellin}.
nodes.statement_short: Delta(K) is the support of the cone of the comparison morphism between the two Mellin transforms of K.

nodes.name: Points of Delta(K)
nodes.statement: By \cite[Prop.~3.3.4(i)]{GabberLoeser1996}, \[ \Delta(K)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}) =\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\varphi_{K,\chi}\text{ is \emph{not} an isomorphism}\}. \]
nodes.statement_short: The points of Delta(K) are the characters at which the forget-supports morphism is not an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Finite-field character groups and Z(k_n)
nodes.statement: For \(n\ge1\) we write \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}=\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n),\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}^{\times}\bigr)\), and for a subset \(Z\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) we put \(Z(k_n)=Z\cap\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}\).

nodes.name: Weakly unramified locus X_w(A)
nodes.statement: If \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), let \(X_w(A)\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) be the weakly unramified locus, defined by the conditions of \cite[Def.~3.1]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.\footnote{For the perverse sheaf \(A_\chi\) on the affine torus, Artin vanishing and its Verdier-dual form \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18} show that \(\varphi_{A,\chi}\) is an isomorphism exactly when the conditions of loc.~cit. hold. Thus \(\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) is the complement of the weakly unramified locus.} \begin{equation} X_w(A)=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: X_w(A) is the weakly unramified locus of FFK; by Artin vanishing it is the complement of Delta(A).

nodes.name: Weakly unramified locus as complement of Delta
nodes.statement: X_w(A)=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}).
nodes.label: eq:weak-locus

nodes.name: uniform point count for Delta(K)
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function \(\Phi^\Delta_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with the following property. For every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every \(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(K)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\), \[ |\Delta(K)(k_n)|\le \Phi^\Delta_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-1)} . \]
assumptions: every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every \(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(K)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\)
conclusions: there is a nondecreasing function \(\Phi^\Delta_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with the following property
nodes.statement_short: The number of k_n-characters in Delta(K) is at most Phi_d(C) q^{n(d-1)}, uniformly in the field, l and K of complexity <= C.
nodes.label: thm:delta-count

nodes.name: Cohomology-jump loci V_{d,i}(A)
nodes.statement:
For \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) and \(0\le i\le d\), put  egin{equation}  egin{aligned} \mathcal V_{d,i}(A)= igl\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):{}& \mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ &\mathrm{H}^{i}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0 igr\}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For \(i>d\), we use the convention \(\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)=\varnothing\).
nodes.statement_short: V_{d,i}(A) is the set of characters at which compactly supported or ordinary cohomology of A_chi is nonzero in degree +-i.

nodes.name: Cohomology-jump loci
nodes.statement:
egin{aligned} \mathcal V_{d,i}(A)= igl\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):{}& \mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ &\mathrm{H}^{i}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0\ 	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)
eq0 igr\}. \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:cohomology-jump-loci

nodes.name: bounded-complexity stratified point count
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function \(\Psi_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that for every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(A)\le C\), every \(0\le i\le d\), and every \(n\ge1\), \[ |\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)(k_n)|\le\Psi_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-i)} . \]
assumptions: every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(A)\le C\), every \(0\le i\le d\), and every \(n\ge1\)
nodes.statement_short: The k_n-points of the i-th cohomology-jump locus of a perverse sheaf of complexity <= C number at most Psi_d(C) q^{n(d-i)}.
nodes.label: thm:stratified

nodes.name: Bounded-complexity refinement proposed by FFK; case i=1
nodes.statement: Forey--Fres\'an--Kowalski propose this bounded-complexity refinement of their stratified vanishing theorem \cite[Th.~2.3, Rem.~2.4]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.\footnote{For tori, the non-uniform stratified vanishing theorem is \cite[Th.~3.4.1, Prop.~6.3.2, Th.~6.3.3]{GabberLoeser1996}, again conditional on the hypotheses recalled above, removed in \cite[Cor.~2.16]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.} Its case \(i=1\) bounds \(\mathcal V_{d,1}(A)\), a subset of \(\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and is subsumed by Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count}, which bounds the larger set \(\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\).
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.2 is the refinement proposed by FFK; its case i=1 is subsumed by Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: Unramified locus X(M_0)
nodes.statement: For \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\), with geometric base change \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\), let \(X(M_0)=X(M)\subseteq X_w(M)\) denote the unramified locus of \cite[Def.~3.25, \S3.8]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Generic subset of characters
nodes.statement: Following \cite[Def.~1.22]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, a subset \(X\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) is \emph{generic} if there exists a constant \(c(X)\ge0\) such that \[ |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X)(k_n)|\le c(X)q^{n(d-1)} \] for every \(n\ge1\).
differentia: there exists a constant \(c(X)\ge0\) such that

nodes.name: Generically unramified object
nodes.statement: The object \(M_0\) is \emph{generically unramified} if \(X(M_0)\) is generic.

nodes.name: unramified point count
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\) there is a nondecreasing function \(\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) with the following property. For every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every arithmetically semisimple object \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) whose geometric base change \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\) satisfies \(c_u(M)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\), \[ |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_0))(k_n)| \le \Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)\,q^{n(d-1)} . \]
assumptions: every \(C\ge0\), every finite field \(k=\mathbb{F}_q\), every prime \(\ell\neq\operatorname{char}k\), every arithmetically semisimple object \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) whose geometric base change \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\) satisfies \(c_u(M)\le C\), and every \(n\ge1\)
nodes.statement_short: The ramified k_n-characters of an arithmetically semisimple M_0 of complexity <= C number at most Phi^ur_d(C) q^{n(d-1)}.
nodes.label: thm:unram-count

nodes.name: Isomorphism iota and unitary Frobenius classes
nodes.statement: Fix a prime \(\ell\) and an isomorphism \(\iota\colon\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\to\mathbb{C}\), through which the unitary Frobenius conjugacy classes below are formed, as in \cite[\S3.9]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Maximal compact K_G, conjugacy classes and Haar measure
nodes.statement: For an integer \(r\ge1\) and a reductive subgroup \(G\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{r,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\), let \(K_G\) be a maximal compact subgroup of \(G(\mathbb{C})\), let \(K_G^\sharp\) be its space of conjugacy classes, and let \(\mu_G^\sharp\) be the pushforward of the normalized Haar probability measure on \(K_G\).

nodes.name: Sequence of finite fields k_j
nodes.statement: Let \((k_j)_{j\ge1}\) be a sequence of finite fields of characteristic \(\neq\ell\) with \(\#k_j\to\infty\).

nodes.name: Sequence of objects M_{j,0}
nodes.statement: For each \(j\), choose an algebraic closure \(\bar k_j\) of \(k_j\), and let \(M_{j,0}\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k_j)\) be arithmetically semisimple and pure of weight zero, with geometric base change \(M_j=M_{j,0,\bar k_j}\).

nodes.name: Tannakian groups G_j and sets X_j
nodes.statement: Let \(r_j\) be the tannakian dimension of \(M_j\), and put \[ G_j^{\mathrm{geo}}=G^{\mathrm{geo}}_{M_j},\qquad G_j^{\mathrm{ari}}=G^{\mathrm{ari}}_{M_j},\qquad X_j=X(M_{j,0})(k_j). \]

nodes.name: Horizontal equidistribution on G_m^d
nodes.statement: Assume that \(\sup_jc_u(M_j)<\infty\), that \(r_j=r\) for some integer \(r\), and that \(G_j^{\mathrm{ari}}=G_j^{\mathrm{geo}}\) for every \(j\). Suppose that these groups are conjugate in \(\operatorname{GL}_{r,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\) to a fixed reductive subgroup \(G\). After choosing such conjugacies, the unitary Frobenius conjugacy classes \(\Theta_{M_{j,0},k_j}(\chi)\), \(\chi\in X_j\), become \(\mu_G^\sharp\)-equidistributed in \(K_G^\sharp\) as \(j\to\infty\).
assumptions: these groups are conjugate in \(\operatorname{GL}_{r,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\) to a fixed reductive subgroup \(G\)
conclusions: the unitary Frobenius conjugacy classes \(\Theta_{M_{j,0},k_j}(\chi)\), \(\chi\in X_j\), become \(\mu_G^\sharp\)-equidistributed in \(K_G^\sharp\) as \(j\to\infty\)
nodes.statement_short: For bounded complexity and a common tannakian group G, Frobenius classes of unramified characters equidistribute in K_G^# as #k_j grows, with varying characteristic.
nodes.label: cor:equidistribution

nodes.name: Recovery of Katz's equidistribution theorem for d=1
nodes.statement: For \(d=1\), Corollary~\ref{cor:equidistribution} recovers Katz's equidistribution theorem \cite[Th.~28.1]{Katz2012} for \(\mathbb{G}_m\).\footnote{Katz assumes instead that the \(M_j\) have a common tannakian dimension and uniformly bounded generic rank, and these hypotheses already bound \(c_u(M_j)\) uniformly. For the degree-one embedding \(u_1\) of \(\mathbb{G}_m\) in \(\mathbb{P}^1\), the curve-complexity formula \cite[Th.~7.3(2)]{SFFK23} gives \(c_u(M_j)\le4\operatorname{rank}(M_j)+\operatorname{loc}(M_j)\), and \(\chi_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}[1])=0\) reduces the Grothendieck--Ogg--Shafarevich formula to \(\operatorname{loc}(M_j)=\chi_c(\mathbb{G}_m,M_j)\), which is the tannakian dimension of \(M_j\). We thank Emmanuel Kowalski for this observation.} Like Katz's theorem, it applies along arbitrary sequences of finite fields, covering the extension towers, the sequences of prime fields, and every amalgam of the two.
nodes.statement_short: For d=1 Corollary 1.4 recovers Katz's theorem, since Katz's hypotheses bound c_u(M_j).

nodes.name: Equidistribution of the character sums
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{cor:equidistribution} has a companion at the level of the sums, the analogue on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) along arbitrary sequences of finite fields of \cite[Th.~4.8]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. It is one of the variants that Forey--Fres\'an--Kowalski leave to the reader before \cite[Th.~4.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Let \(\nu\) be the direct image of \(\mu_G^\sharp\) under the trace of the standard representation \(K_G^\sharp\to\mathbb{C}\). For \(\chi\in X_j\), the Grothendieck--Lefschetz trace formula and \ref{item:T5} give \[ S(M_{j,0};k_j,\chi)=\operatorname{Tr}\Theta_{M_{j,0},k_j}(\chi). \] Since the trace is continuous on \(K_G^\sharp\), the sums \(S(M_{j,0};k_j,\chi)\), \(\chi\in X_j\), become \(\nu\)-equidistributed in \(\mathbb{C}\) as \(j\to\infty\). By Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count} the characters outside \(X_j\) make up a vanishing fraction of all characters of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_j)\), so the same holds for the sums indexed by the full character group.
nodes.statement_short: The sums S(M_{j,0};k_j,chi) become equidistributed for the image of Haar measure under the trace, also over the full character group.
nodes.label: rem:sum-equidistribution

nodes.name: Sketch of the exceptional-set estimate
nodes.statement: The estimate for \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) is a boundary calculation. Compactify the first factor to \(\mathbb{P}^1\). The localization triangle reduces the failure of \(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) to the boundary components \(\{0,\infty\}\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\). The Hochschild--Serre spectral sequence for nearby cycles \cite[\textit{Th\'eor\`emes de finitude}, Lem.~3.11]{SGA45} identifies the corresponding stalks with continuous inertia cohomology of the relative nearby-cycle complexes. By the prime-to-\(\ell\) vanishing of Appendix~\ref{app:boundary}, this cohomology is carried by the pro-\(\ell\) quotient of tame inertia. Twisting by \(\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) multiplies the tame inertia action at \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\) by the scalar \(\lambda_x(\tau_x)\), in the local monodromy notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer-local-monodromy}. Consequently, if \(\lambda\) is exceptional, then \(\lambda_x(\tau_x)^{-1}\) occurs as a monodromy eigenvalue on a relative nearby-cycle complex at one of the two boundary points. Since \[ \lambda\longmapsto\lambda_x(\tau_x) \] is injective, the exceptional characters are bounded by the number of such eigenvalues. The complexity estimates for nearby cycles and eigenvalue strata bound this number solely in terms of \(c_u(A)\) and \(d\), uniformly in the field and in \(\ell\). This is a relative and quantitative version of the mechanism in \cite[(6.5.1)]{KatzLaumon1985}. The finite exceptional set of the qualitative argument is replaced by a bound depending only on the complexity.
nodes.statement_short: Boundary calculation: exceptional characters give inertia eigenvalues on relative nearby cycles, counted by complexity.

nodes.name: Reduce to the boundary
nodes.statement: The estimate for \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) is a boundary calculation. Compactify the first factor to \(\mathbb{P}^1\). The localization triangle reduces the failure of \(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) to the boundary components \(\{0,\infty\}\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\).
nodes.statement_short: Compactify and reduce failure of forget-supports to the boundary

nodes.name: Stalks as inertia cohomology
nodes.statement: The Hochschild--Serre spectral sequence for nearby cycles \cite[\textit{Th\'eor\`emes de finitude}, Lem.~3.11]{SGA45} identifies the corresponding stalks with continuous inertia cohomology of the relative nearby-cycle complexes. By the prime-to-\(\ell\) vanishing of Appendix~\ref{app:boundary}, this cohomology is carried by the pro-\(\ell\) quotient of tame inertia.
nodes.statement_short: Identify boundary stalks with inertia cohomology carried by pro-l tame inertia

nodes.name: Twist gives an eigenvalue
nodes.statement: Twisting by \(\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) multiplies the tame inertia action at \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\) by the scalar \(\lambda_x(\tau_x)\), in the local monodromy notation of Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer-local-monodromy}. Consequently, if \(\lambda\) is exceptional, then \(\lambda_x(\tau_x)^{-1}\) occurs as a monodromy eigenvalue on a relative nearby-cycle complex at one of the two boundary points.
nodes.statement_short: Exceptional lambda yields a monodromy eigenvalue

nodes.name: Count eigenvalues
nodes.statement: Since \[ \lambda\longmapsto\lambda_x(\tau_x) \] is injective, the exceptional characters are bounded by the number of such eigenvalues. The complexity estimates for nearby cycles and eigenvalue strata bound this number solely in terms of \(c_u(A)\) and \(d\), uniformly in the field and in \(\ell\). This is a relative and quantitative version of the mechanism in \cite[(6.5.1)]{KatzLaumon1985}. The finite exceptional set of the qualitative argument is replaced by a bound depending only on the complexity.
nodes.statement_short: Injectivity bounds the exceptional set by complexity

nodes.name: Sketch of the proofs of Theorems 1.1 and 1.2
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} and the perverse case of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} are proved by separate inductions on \(d\), both starting from Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one} and both using the estimate above. By the projection formula, twisting \(B_\lambda\) by \(\eta\) computes the twisted cohomology of \(A\) at \((\lambda,\eta)\), with and without compact supports. For non-exceptional \(\lambda\), the counting problem for \(A\) at the characters \((\lambda,\eta)\) is therefore exactly the counting problem for \(B_\lambda\) in dimension \(d-1\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre}), and the inductive bound applies to each of the at most \(q^n\) such \(\lambda\). The exponent in Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} is preserved by \[ q^n\cdot q^{n((d-1)-i)}=q^{n(d-i)}. \] For the perverse case of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} the exceptional characters may be estimated trivially in the remaining \(d-1\) variables, contributing at most \(\#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\,|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}|\le F_d(c_u(A))\,q^{n(d-1)}\). For Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} in degree \(i>1\) this is too large, of order \(q^{n(d-1)}\) rather than \(q^{n(d-i)}\), and the exceptional fibres must enter the induction as well. Artin affine vanishing and the relative-dimension bound place \(B_{!,\lambda}\) in perverse degrees \([0,1]\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) in \([-1,0]\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-amplitude}). The perverse spectral sequence therefore converts a cohomology jump in degree \(\pm i\) at \((\lambda,\eta)\) into a jump in degree \(i\) or \(i-1\) at \(\eta\) for one of the at most four perverse cohomology sheaves of \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\), each of complexity at most \(F_d(c_u(A))\), and the induction applies to these. The term \(i-1\) gives \(q^{n((d-1)-(i-1))}=q^{n(d-i)}\), which closes the induction. The case of an arbitrary complex in Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} then follows from the perverse cohomology sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on d via the one-coordinate estimate; exceptional fibres enter through perverse amplitude [0,1] and [-1,0].

nodes.name: Induction structure
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} and the perverse case of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} are proved by separate inductions on \(d\), both starting from Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one} and both using the estimate above.
nodes.statement_short: Separate inductions on d starting from Corollary 3.5

nodes.name: Non-exceptional fibres
nodes.statement: By the projection formula, twisting \(B_\lambda\) by \(\eta\) computes the twisted cohomology of \(A\) at \((\lambda,\eta)\), with and without compact supports. For non-exceptional \(\lambda\), the counting problem for \(A\) at the characters \((\lambda,\eta)\) is therefore exactly the counting problem for \(B_\lambda\) in dimension \(d-1\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre}), and the inductive bound applies to each of the at most \(q^n\) such \(\lambda\). The exponent in Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} is preserved by \[ q^n\cdot q^{n((d-1)-i)}=q^{n(d-i)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Non-exceptional lambda reduce to dimension d-1

nodes.name: Trivial bound for exceptional characters
nodes.statement: For the perverse case of Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} the exceptional characters may be estimated trivially in the remaining \(d-1\) variables, contributing at most \(\#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\,|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}|\le F_d(c_u(A))\,q^{n(d-1)}\).
nodes.statement_short: Exceptional characters cost F_d q^{n(d-1)}

nodes.name: Exceptional fibres for Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement: For Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} in degree \(i>1\) this is too large, of order \(q^{n(d-1)}\) rather than \(q^{n(d-i)}\), and the exceptional fibres must enter the induction as well. Artin affine vanishing and the relative-dimension bound place \(B_{!,\lambda}\) in perverse degrees \([0,1]\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) in \([-1,0]\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:relative-amplitude}). The perverse spectral sequence therefore converts a cohomology jump in degree \(\pm i\) at \((\lambda,\eta)\) into a jump in degree \(i\) or \(i-1\) at \(\eta\) for one of the at most four perverse cohomology sheaves of \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\), each of complexity at most \(F_d(c_u(A))\), and the induction applies to these. The term \(i-1\) gives \(q^{n((d-1)-(i-1))}=q^{n(d-i)}\), which closes the induction.
nodes.statement_short: Perverse amplitude moves jumps to degree i or i-1

nodes.name: Arbitrary complexes
nodes.statement: The case of an arbitrary complex in Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} then follows from the perverse cohomology sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to perverse cohomology sheaves

nodes.name: Sketch of the proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count} requires no new boundary estimate. Unramifiedness follows from weak unramifiedness through the localization formalism of Gabber--Loeser. The canonical comparison morphisms \(\alpha_m\colon L^{\ast_!m}\to L^{\ast_*m}\), \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), have Mellin transforms with derived fibre \(\varphi_{L,\chi}^{\otimes m}\) at every character \(\chi\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-monoidal}). A Nakayama argument and \ref{item:GL5} invert them at every character outside the locus \(\Delta(L)\) defined in \ref{item:GL2} of \S\ref{sec:mellin}. The compact and ordinary cohomology of every perverse cohomology sheaf of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha_m)\) then vanishes at such characters, and \ref{item:T5} gives unramifiedness. This proves Lemma~\ref{lem:weakly-unramified-inclusion}, the inclusion \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\). The complement of \(X(M_0)\) is therefore contained in \(\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} applied to \(L\) bounds it.
nodes.statement_short: Weakly unramified implies unramified via localization and Nakayama; then Theorem 1.1 for L bounds the complement.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count} requires no new boundary estimate. Unramifiedness follows from weak unramifiedness through the localization formalism of Gabber--Loeser.
nodes.statement_short: Unramifiedness from weak unramifiedness by localization

nodes.name: Comparison morphisms
nodes.statement: The canonical comparison morphisms \(\alpha_m\colon L^{\ast_!m}\to L^{\ast_*m}\), \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), have Mellin transforms with derived fibre \(\varphi_{L,\chi}^{\otimes m}\) at every character \(\chi\) (Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-monoidal}). A Nakayama argument and \ref{item:GL5} invert them at every character outside the locus \(\Delta(L)\) defined in \ref{item:GL2} of \S\ref{sec:mellin}.
nodes.statement_short: Fibres of alpha_m are tensor powers; invert outside Delta(L)

nodes.name: Unramified inclusion
nodes.statement: The compact and ordinary cohomology of every perverse cohomology sheaf of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha_m)\) then vanishes at such characters, and \ref{item:T5} gives unramifiedness. This proves Lemma~\ref{lem:weakly-unramified-inclusion}, the inclusion \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: Cohomology of cones vanishes, giving X_w(L) in X(M_0)

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: The complement of \(X(M_0)\) is therefore contained in \(\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} applied to \(L\) bounds it.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 for L bounds the complement

nodes.name: Sketch of the proof of Corollary 1.4
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{cor:equidistribution} follows from the Weyl criterion and \ref{item:T5}. For every nontrivial irreducible representation \(\rho\) of the common tannakian group, Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} bounds the characters at which the associated object has cohomology outside degree zero, and Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count} bounds the characters omitted from the unramified averaging set. The weight bounds for the remaining Frobenius traces then force every nontrivial Weyl average to be \(O_\rho(q^{-1/2})\).
nodes.statement_short: Weyl criterion: Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 bound the bad characters and weights force O(q^{-1/2}) averages.

nodes.name: Weyl criterion
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{cor:equidistribution} follows from the Weyl criterion and \ref{item:T5}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to Weyl sums

nodes.name: Bound bad characters
nodes.statement: For every nontrivial irreducible representation \(\rho\) of the common tannakian group, Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} bounds the characters at which the associated object has cohomology outside degree zero, and Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count} bounds the characters omitted from the unramified averaging set.
nodes.statement_short: Theorems 1.2 and 1.3 bound the exceptional characters

nodes.name: Weight bounds
nodes.statement: The weight bounds for the remaining Frobenius traces then force every nontrivial Weyl average to be \(O_\rho(q^{-1/2})\).
nodes.statement_short: Weights force O(q^{-1/2})

nodes.name: Varying algebraically closed base field Omega
nodes.statement: When a statement allows the algebraically closed base field to vary, we denote it by \(\Omega\), and unadorned varieties in that statement and its proof are over \(\Omega\).

nodes.name: Segre embedding u_d
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\), we use the product compactification \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\hookrightarrow(\mathbb{P}^1_{\bar k})^d\), with boundary induced by \(\mathbb{G}_m\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\), and fix the locally closed immersion \[ u_d\colon \mathbb{G}_m^d\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2^d-1}_{\bar k} \] obtained by the Segre embedding.

nodes.name: Compatibility of the embeddings u_d
nodes.statement: For \(d\ge2\), these choices are compatible with the decomposition \(\mathbb{G}_m^d=\mathbb{G}_m\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\), in that the embedding induced by \(u_1\) and \(u_{d-1}\) is \(u_d\).
conclusions: the embedding induced by \(u_1\) and \(u_{d-1}\) is \(u_d\)

nodes.name: Charts U_x and coordinates t_x
nodes.statement: For \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), put \[ U_0=\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{\infty\},\quad t_0(z)=z, \qquad U_\infty=\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0\},\quad t_\infty(z)=z^{-1}. \] Each \(t_x\) is an isomorphism \(U_x\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\mathbb{A}^1\) carrying \(x\) to \(0\).

nodes.name: Standard immersion a
nodes.statement: We use the standard immersion \(a\colon\mathbb{A}^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\).

nodes.name: Standard embedded morphisms
nodes.statement: Products carry the corresponding Segre embeddings. The morphisms used below are products and compositions of coordinate projections, multiplication, inversion, the identity section, the open and closed immersions associated with \(\mathbb{G}_m\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\), the maps \(t_x\), and the Segre embeddings. We equip each graph with the induced locally closed immersion into the product of the projective ambient spaces. These embeddings and morphisms are fixed over \(\mathbb Z\), and will be used in Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}.
nodes.statement_short: The fixed morphisms are products and compositions of projections, multiplication, inversion, identity section, the P^1 immersions, t_x and Segre embeddings, with graph embeddings.

nodes.name: Schemes are noetherian
nodes.statement: All schemes in this paper are noetherian.

nodes.name: Constructible derived category via pro-etale site
nodes.statement: For a scheme \(Y\), we set \[ D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}), \] where the right-hand side is the constructible derived category of \cite[Defs.~6.8.6, 6.8.8]{BhattScholze2015}.

nodes.name: Perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: For \(Y\) of finite type over either \(k\) or \(\bar k\), we write \(\operatorname{Perv}(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\subset D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) for the abelian category of perverse sheaves with respect to the middle perversity of \cite{BBDG18}, with perverse \(t\)-structure \(({}^pD^{\le0},{}^pD^{\ge0})\).

nodes.name: Sheaf-theoretic notation
nodes.statement: We use \(D\) for Verdier duality, \(\boxtimes\) for the external tensor product, \(\mathcal{H}^i\) for the cohomology sheaves of a complex, \(\operatorname{Supp}\) for support, \(\operatorname{Cone}\) for the mapping cone, and \(\mathrm{H}^i\), \(\mathrm{H}^i_c\) for hypercohomology without and with compact supports.

nodes.name: Forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon X\to Y\) be a separated morphism of finite type. Then \(X\) and \(Y\) are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and \(f\) is finitely presented, as required in \cite[Def.~6.7.6]{BhattScholze2015}. By Nagata compactification, choose a factorization \(f=\bar f\circ j\), where \(j\colon X\hookrightarrow\bar X\) is an open immersion and \(\bar f\colon\bar X\to Y\) is proper \cite[Tag~0F41]{stacks-project}. For an open immersion \(j\), let \(\varphi_j\colon j_!\to Rj_*\) be the natural transformation whose value at \(K\) corresponds to \(\operatorname{id}_K\) under \[ \operatorname{Hom}(j_!K,Rj_*K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(K,K). \] The \emph{forget-supports transformation} for \(f\) is \begin{equation} \varphi_f=R\bar f_*(\varphi_j)\colon Rf_!=R\bar f_*\,j_!\longrightarrow R\bar f_*\,Rj_*=Rf_*. \end{equation} For \(K\in D^b_c(X,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), we write \[ \varphi_f(K)\colon Rf_!K\longrightarrow Rf_*K \] for the value of this natural transformation at \(K\). It is independent of the compactification.
nodes.statement_short: phi_f = Rbar f_*(phi_j): Rf_! -> Rf_* for a Nagata compactification f = bar f o j, with phi_j adjoint to id.

nodes.name: Forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement: \varphi_f=R\bar f_*(\varphi_j)\colon Rf_!=R\bar f_*\,j_!\longrightarrow R\bar f_*\,Rj_*=Rf_*.
nodes.label: eq:forget-supports

nodes.name: Forget-supports compatible with composition and lisse projection formula
nodes.statement: Let \(p\colon X\to Y\) and \(f\colon Y\to S\) be separated morphisms of finite type, let \(K\in D^b_c(X,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and let \(\mathcal{L}\) be lisse on \(Y\). For \(\star\in\{!,*\}\), let \[ \beta_\star\colon R(f\circ p)_\star(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } Rf_\star(Rp_\star K\otimes\mathcal{L}) \] be the composition and projection-formula isomorphism. For \(\star=!\), the formula used here is the projection formula \cite[Exp.~XVII, Prop.~5.2.9]{SGA4}, \cite[Prop.~A.1.5(ii)]{GabberLoeser1996}. For \(\star=*\), it is the universal coefficient formula for a lisse sheaf \cite[Prop.~A.1.5(i)]{GabberLoeser1996}. A direct proof of the latter is included in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(2). Then the following diagram commutes. \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] R(f\circ p)_!(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}) \arrow[rr,"\varphi_{f\circ p}"] \arrow[d,"\beta_!"',"\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"] && R(f\circ p)_*(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}) \arrow[d,"\beta_*","\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"'] \\ Rf_!(Rp_!K\otimes\mathcal{L}) \arrow[r,"Rf_!(\varphi_p(K)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{L}})"'] & Rf_!(Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}) \arrow[r,"\varphi_f"'] & Rf_*(Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}). \end{tikzcd} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: The forget-supports map of f o p twisted by a lisse sheaf factors through phi_p and phi_f under the projection-formula isomorphisms.

nodes.name: Combined composition and projection-formula diagram
nodes.statement: \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] R(f\circ p)_!(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}) \arrow[rr,"\varphi_{f\circ p}"] \arrow[d,"\beta_!"',"\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"] && R(f\circ p)_*(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}) \arrow[d,"\beta_*","\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"'] \\ Rf_!(Rp_!K\otimes\mathcal{L}) \arrow[r,"Rf_!(\varphi_p(K)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{L}})"'] & Rf_!(Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}) \arrow[r,"\varphi_f"'] & Rf_*(Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}). \end{tikzcd}
nodes.label: eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse

nodes.name: Proof of the combined compatibility
nodes.statement: The composition formula in Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports}(2) gives the lower composite. Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(2) identifies its first arrow under the projection-formula isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the composition formula of Lemma A.1(2) and Lemma A.2(2).

nodes.name: Bhatt-Scholze comparison for continuous etale cohomology
nodes.statement: For an inverse system of \'etale sheaves with surjective transition maps, Bhatt--Scholze identify Jannsen's continuous \'etale cohomology with the pro-\'etale cohomology of its inverse limit \cite[Prop.~5.6.2]{BhattScholze2015}.
nodes.statement_short: Jannsen's continuous etale cohomology agrees with pro-etale cohomology of the inverse limit.

nodes.name: Continuous group cohomology RGamma_cts
nodes.statement: For a profinite group \(G\), a finite extension \(E/\mathbb Q_\ell\), and a finite-dimensional continuous \(E\)-representation \(V\) with a \(G\)-stable \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice \(\Lambda\), choose a uniformizer \(\varpi\) of \(E\) and set \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V) =\left(R\varprojlim_nR\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)\right) \otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E. \] This is independent of \(\Lambda\) and \(\varpi\) and computes Tate's continuous-cochain cohomology \cite[(2.1),(2.2)]{Jannsen88}. For an \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-representation, choose an \(E\)-model and extend scalars from \(E\) to \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\). The result is independent of the model.
nodes.statement_short: Continuous cohomology of an l-adic representation defined via a stable lattice and derived inverse limit, then extension of scalars.

nodes.name: Existence of an E-model
nodes.statement: An \(E\)-model always exists.

nodes.name: Proof of existence of E-models
nodes.statement: The image of a continuous representation \(G\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) of a profinite group is compact, the finite subextensions of \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}/\mathbb Q_\ell\) are countably many, and the intersections of the image with the closed subgroups \(\operatorname{GL}_n(E)\) cover it. By the Baire category theorem, one such intersection is open in the image, and adjoining to \(E\) the entries of finitely many coset representatives gives a finite extension containing all matrix entries. A compact subgroup of \(\operatorname{GL}_n(E)\) moreover stabilizes an \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice.
nodes.statement_short: Compact image covered by countably many closed subgroups GL_n(E); Baire gives a finite extension.

nodes.name: Compact image covered
nodes.statement: The image of a continuous representation \(G\to\operatorname{GL}_n(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) of a profinite group is compact, the finite subextensions of \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}/\mathbb Q_\ell\) are countably many, and the intersections of the image with the closed subgroups \(\operatorname{GL}_n(E)\) cover it.
nodes.statement_short: The compact image is covered by countably many GL_n(E)

nodes.name: Baire category
nodes.statement: By the Baire category theorem, one such intersection is open in the image, and adjoining to \(E\) the entries of finitely many coset representatives gives a finite extension containing all matrix entries.
nodes.statement_short: Baire gives a finite extension with all entries

nodes.name: Stable lattice
nodes.statement: A compact subgroup of \(\operatorname{GL}_n(E)\) moreover stabilizes an \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice.
nodes.statement_short: Compact subgroups stabilize a lattice

nodes.name: Vinogradov notation
nodes.statement: For a complex valued function \(f\) and a nonnegative function \(g\), we write \(f\ll g\), or \(f=O(g)\), if \(|f|\le Kg\) for some constant \(K\ge0\).

nodes.name: Notation f asymp g
nodes.statement: For nonnegative \(f\) we write \(f\asymp g\) if both \(f\ll g\) and \(g\ll f\) hold.

nodes.name: Nondecreasing majorant f^uparrow
nodes.statement: If an estimate first produces a function \(f:\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), we replace it by the nondecreasing function \(f^\uparrow:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) defined by \[ f^\uparrow(C)=\max\{f(e)\mid e\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},\ e\le\lceil C\rceil\}. \] We retain the notation \(f\) after this replacement. Thus all functions used in upper bounds below are nondecreasing.

nodes.name: Sawin complexity
nodes.statement: \emph{Definition} \cite[Defs.~3.2, 6.3, 6.5, 6.6]{SFFK23}. For \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{P}^n_\Omega)\), \[ c(A)=\max_{0\le m\le n}\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z} h^i\bigl(\mathbb{P}^m_{\Omega'},l_{a_m}^*A\bigr), \] where \(a_m\) is a geometric generic point of the space of \((n+1)\times(m+1)\) matrices, defined over an algebraically closed extension \(\Omega'\) of \(\Omega\), and \(l_{a_m}:\mathbb{P}^m_{\Omega'}\to\mathbb{P}^n_{\Omega'}\) is the associated linear map. For an embedded quasi-projective variety \(u:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^n\) and \(A\in D^b_c(X)\), put \(c_u(A)=c(u_!A)\) and \(c(u)=c_u(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). For a morphism \(f:(X,u)\to(Y,v)\) with \(u:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^m\) and \(v:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^n\), let \(a_p\) and \(b_q\) be geometric generic points of the spaces of \((m+1)\times(p+1)\) and \((n+1)\times(q+1)\) matrices, defined over a common algebraically closed extension \(\Omega'\) of \(\Omega\). The complexity of \(f\) relative to \((u,v)\) is \[ c_{u,v}(f)=\max_{0\le p\le m}\max_{0\le q\le n}\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z} h^i_c\bigl(X_{\Omega'},\,u^*l_{a_p,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\otimes f^*v^*l_{b_q,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\bigr). \] The Betti numbers may equally be computed as those of the intersection of the graph of \(f\) in \(\mathbb{P}^m\times\mathbb{P}^n\) with a product of linear subspaces, for \((a_p,b_q)\) in a dense open subset of the product of the two matrix spaces. On \(X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\), the complexity of a complex is the sum of the dimensions of its cohomology groups. For \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), we write \[ c_u(A)=c_{u_d}(A)=c(u_{d,!}A). \]
nodes.statement_short: Complexity is the max over generic linear sections of the sum of Betti numbers; c_u(A)=c(u_!A).

nodes.name: Positivity of complexity
nodes.statement: \emph{Positivity} \cite[Prop.~3.4, Rem.~6.4]{SFFK23}. The complexity \(c_u(A)\) is a nonnegative integer, and \(c_u(A)=0\) if and only if \(A=0\).
nodes.origin_citation: Sawin, Forey, Fresan & Kowalski 2023, Prop. 3.4, Rem. 6.4
conclusions: The complexity \(c_u(A)\) is a nonnegative integer, and \(c_u(A)=0\) if and only if \(A=0\).

nodes.name: Complexity bounds for the six operations
nodes.statement: \emph{Six operations} \cite[Th.~6.8, estimates~(6.1), (6.2), (6.5), (6.6), (6.8)]{SFFK23}. For a morphism \(f:(X,u)\to(Y,v)\), objects \(A,B\in D^b_c(X)\), and \(C\in D^b_c(Y)\), \[ \begin{gathered} c_u(DA)\ll c(u)\,c_u(A), \qquad c_u(A\otimes B)\ll c_u(A)\,c_u(B), \qquad c_u(f^*C)\ll c_{u,v}(f)\,c_v(C),\\ c_v(Rf_!A)\ll c_{u,v}(f)\,c_u(A), \qquad c_v(Rf_*A)\ll c(u)\,c(v)\,c_{u,v}(f)\,c_u(A), \end{gathered} \] with implied constants depending only on the ambient projective dimensions.
nodes.statement_short: Complexity of duals, tensor products, pullbacks and pushforwards is bounded by products of input complexities.

nodes.name: Complexity of triangles, sums and shifts
nodes.statement: \emph{Triangles, sums, shifts} \cite[Prop.~6.14]{SFFK23}. In a distinguished triangle, the complexity of each vertex is at most the sum of the complexities of the other two. Moreover \(c_u(A\oplus B)=c_u(A)+c_u(B)\), and \(c_u(A[h])=c_u(A)\) for \(h\in\mathbb Z\). In particular, a direct summand has complexity at most that of the ambient object.

nodes.name: Complexity of external products
nodes.statement: \emph{External products} \cite[Prop.~6.12]{SFFK23}. For embedded varieties \((X,u)\) and \((Y,v)\), with \(u\boxtimes v\) the embedding of \(X\times Y\) induced by the Segre embedding and \(p_1,p_2\) the projections, \[ c_{u\boxtimes v}(A\boxtimes B) \ll c_{u\boxtimes v,u}(p_1)\,c_{u\boxtimes v,v}(p_2)\,c_u(A)\,c_v(B), \] with an implied constant depending only on the ambient projective dimensions.

nodes.name: Jordan-Holder complexity estimate
nodes.statement: \emph{Jordan--H\"older} \cite[Th.~6.15]{SFFK23}. If \((A_{i,j})_{1\le j\le n_i}\) are the Jordan--H\"older factors of \({}^pH^i(A)\), repeated with multiplicity, then \[ c_u(A)\le\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z}\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}c_u(A_{i,j})\ll c(u)\,c_u(A), \] with an implied constant depending only on the ambient projective dimension. Combined with \ref{item:C4}, this shows that every subquotient of every \({}^pH^i(A)\) has complexity at most a constant multiple of \(c(u)\,c_u(A)\).

nodes.name: Complexity of nearby and vanishing cycles
nodes.statement: \emph{Nearby and vanishing cycles} \cite[Cor.~6.18]{SFFK23}. Let \(f:(X,u)\to(S,v)\) be flat, with \(S\) a smooth irreducible curve, and let \(\sigma\in S\) be closed. Put \(S_{(\sigma)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\sigma}\), and let \[ f_{(\sigma)}:X\times_S S_{(\sigma)}\longrightarrow S_{(\sigma)} \] be the base change of \(f\). Denote by \(\Psi_f\) and \(\Phi_f\) the nearby- and vanishing-cycle functors for \(f_{(\sigma)}\), whose values on \(A\in D^b_c(X)\) are formed from the pullback of \(A\) to \(X\times_S S_{(\sigma)}\) and viewed as objects on \(X_\sigma\). If \(u_\sigma\) denotes the induced embedding of \(X_\sigma\), then \[ c_{u_\sigma}(\Psi_fA)\ll c_{u,v}(f)^2c_u(A), \qquad c_{u_\sigma}(\Phi_fA)\ll c_{u,v}(f)^2c_u(A). \] The implied constants depend only on the ambient projective dimensions.

nodes.name: Uniformity of implied constants in Omega and l
nodes.statement: The implied constants in \ref{item:C3}, \ref{item:C5}, \ref{item:C6} and \ref{item:C7} are uniform in \(\Omega\) and in \(\ell\), while \(c(u)\) and \(c_{u,v}(f)\) remain inputs.\footnote{Uniformity in \(\ell\) means that one constant serves every prime \(\ell\) invertible in \(\Omega\). This holds because the implied constants in the statements cited in \ref{item:C3}, \ref{item:C5}, \ref{item:C6} and \ref{item:C7} depend only on the ambient projective dimensions.}

nodes.name: Betti bound from equation presentation
nodes.statement: For all integers \(n_1,n_2,r,e\ge0\) there is a constant \(B_{n_1,n_2,r,e}\ge1\), independent of \(\Omega\) and of \(\ell\), with the following property. Let \(Z=Z_1\setminus Z_2\), where \(Z_1\) and \(Z_2\) are closed subschemes of \(\mathbb{P}^{n_1}_\Omega\times\mathbb{P}^{n_2}_\Omega\) defined, on each product of standard affine charts, by at most \(r\) equations of degrees at most \(e\). Then every compactly supported Betti sum of a generic linear or product-linear section of \(Z\), as in \cite[Defs.~6.3, 6.6]{SFFK23}, is at most \(B_{n_1,n_2,r,e}\).
assumptions: \(Z=Z_1\setminus Z_2\), where \(Z_1\) and \(Z_2\) are closed subschemes of \(\mathbb{P}^{n_1}_\Omega\times\mathbb{P}^{n_2}_\Omega\) defined, on each product of standard affine charts, by at most \(r\) equations of degrees at most \(e\)
conclusions: every compactly supported Betti sum of a generic linear or product-linear section of \(Z\), as in \cite[Defs.~6.3, 6.6]{SFFK23}, is at most \(B_{n_1,n_2,r,e}\)
nodes.label: lem:betti-presentation

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: A generic linear or product-linear section imposes additional linear equations and preserves the chart presentation. A finite cover by principal affine opens, realized as closed affine schemes by adjoining inverse variables, together with the \v{C}ech spectral sequence reduces the required sums to those of closed affine schemes defined by a number of equations and degrees bounded in terms of \(n_1\), \(n_2\), \(r\), and \(e\). Passing to the reduction does not change \'etale cohomology. Proposition~6.21 of \cite{SFFK23}, applied with target a point, bounds these sums by a constant depending only on the ambient dimensions and on the number and degrees of the defining equations.
nodes.statement_short: Cech reduction to affine schemes with bounded equations, then SFFK23 Prop. 6.21.

nodes.name: Sections keep presentation
nodes.statement: A generic linear or product-linear section imposes additional linear equations and preserves the chart presentation.
nodes.statement_short: Generic sections preserve the chart presentation

nodes.name: Cech reduction
nodes.statement: A finite cover by principal affine opens, realized as closed affine schemes by adjoining inverse variables, together with the \v{C}ech spectral sequence reduces the required sums to those of closed affine schemes defined by a number of equations and degrees bounded in terms of \(n_1\), \(n_2\), \(r\), and \(e\). Passing to the reduction does not change \'etale cohomology.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to closed affine schemes with bounded equations

nodes.name: Apply SFFK23 Prop. 6.21
nodes.statement: Proposition~6.21 of \cite{SFFK23}, applied with target a point, bounds these sums by a constant depending only on the ambient dimensions and on the number and degrees of the defining equations.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Betti sums by Prop. 6.21

nodes.name: Uniform complexity of the standard embeddings
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\), there is an integer \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\ge1\), depending only on \(d\), such that the complexities of the embeddings and embedded morphisms specified in \S\ref{sec:embeddings} that occur in dimensions at most \(d\), including their products with \((\mathbb{G}_m^r,u_r)\) for \(1\le r\le d\), are at most \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\) after base change to any algebraically closed field \(\Omega\). The integer \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\) is independent of every prime \(\ell\) invertible in \(\Omega\).
conclusions: there is an integer \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\ge1\), depending only on \(d\), such that the complexities of the embeddings and embedded morphisms specified in \S\ref{sec:embeddings} that occur in dimensions at most \(d\), including their products with \((\mathbb{G}_m^r,u_r)\) for \(1\le r\le d\), are at most \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\) after base change to any algebraically closed field \(\Omega\)
nodes.label: lem:standard-geometric-complexity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: For fixed \(d\), only finitely many embedded schemes and morphisms occur. By \cite[Def.~6.6]{SFFK23}, it suffices to bound the compactly supported Betti sums of generic linear sections of these schemes and generic product-linear sections of their graphs. On standard affine charts, the schemes, graphs, and boundaries are defined by a number of equations and degrees bounded in terms of \(d\). Lemma~\ref{lem:betti-presentation} bounds these sums, and taking the maximum gives \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\).
nodes.statement_short: Finitely many schemes with bounded equations; apply Lemma 2.1 and take the maximum.

nodes.name: Reduce to Betti sums
nodes.statement: For fixed \(d\), only finitely many embedded schemes and morphisms occur. By \cite[Def.~6.6]{SFFK23}, it suffices to bound the compactly supported Betti sums of generic linear sections of these schemes and generic product-linear sections of their graphs.
nodes.statement_short: Finitely many objects; reduce to Betti sums of generic sections

nodes.name: Bounded equations
nodes.statement: On standard affine charts, the schemes, graphs, and boundaries are defined by a number of equations and degrees bounded in terms of \(d\).
nodes.statement_short: Equations and degrees bounded in terms of d

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:betti-presentation} bounds these sums, and taking the maximum gives \(D_d^{\mathrm{std}}\).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.1 and max give D_d^std

nodes.name: Complexity under linear re-embedding
nodes.statement: For all integers \(0\le N\le M\), there is a constant \(E_{N,M}\ge1\), independent of \(\Omega\) and of \(\ell\), with the following property. For every locally closed embedding \(w:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\), every closed immersion \(l:\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^M_\Omega\) induced by an injective linear map \(\Omega^{N+1}\to\Omega^{M+1}\), and every \(B\in D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), \[ E_{N,M}^{-1}\,c_w(B)\le c_{l\circ w}(B)\le E_{N,M}\,c_w(B). \]
assumptions: every locally closed embedding \(w:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\), every closed immersion \(l:\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^M_\Omega\) induced by an injective linear map \(\Omega^{N+1}\to\Omega^{M+1}\), and every \(B\in D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\)
nodes.label: lem:linear-reembedding

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: View \(l\) as a morphism \((\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega,\operatorname{id})\to(\mathbb{P}^M_\Omega,\operatorname{id})\). In the formula of \ref{item:C1} for the complexity of a morphism, \(l_{a_p,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) is the constant sheaf on a linear subspace of \(\mathbb{P}^N_{\Omega'}\), and proper base change identifies \(l^*l_{b_q,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) with the constant sheaf on \(l^{-1}(\Pi)\), where \(\Pi\subseteq\mathbb{P}^M_{\Omega'}\) is the image of \(l_{b_q}\). Their tensor product is the constant sheaf on the intersection, again a linear subspace of \(\mathbb{P}^N_{\Omega'}\), whose compactly supported Betti sum is at most \(N+1\). Hence \(c_{\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id}}(l)\le N+1\). Since \(l\) is a closed immersion, one has \(c_{l\circ w}(B)=c\bigl(l_!(w_!B)\bigr)\) and \(w_!B=l^*l_!(w_!B)\). The pushforward and pullback estimates \ref{item:C3} applied to \(l\) bound each of \(c_w(B)\) and \(c_{l\circ w}(B)\) by \((N+1)\) times the other, up to implied constants depending only on \(N\) and \(M\). Taking \(E_{N,M}\) to dominate both products gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the complexity of the linear immersion by N+1, then apply pushforward and pullback estimates.

nodes.name: Complexity of l
nodes.statement: View \(l\) as a morphism \((\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega,\operatorname{id})\to(\mathbb{P}^M_\Omega,\operatorname{id})\). In the formula of \ref{item:C1} for the complexity of a morphism, \(l_{a_p,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) is the constant sheaf on a linear subspace of \(\mathbb{P}^N_{\Omega'}\), and proper base change identifies \(l^*l_{b_q,*}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) with the constant sheaf on \(l^{-1}(\Pi)\), where \(\Pi\subseteq\mathbb{P}^M_{\Omega'}\) is the image of \(l_{b_q}\). Their tensor product is the constant sheaf on the intersection, again a linear subspace of \(\mathbb{P}^N_{\Omega'}\), whose compactly supported Betti sum is at most \(N+1\). Hence \(c_{\operatorname{id},\operatorname{id}}(l)\le N+1\).
nodes.statement_short: c(l) <= N+1 via linear sections

nodes.name: Push and pull
nodes.statement: Since \(l\) is a closed immersion, one has \(c_{l\circ w}(B)=c\bigl(l_!(w_!B)\bigr)\) and \(w_!B=l^*l_!(w_!B)\). The pushforward and pullback estimates \ref{item:C3} applied to \(l\) bound each of \(c_w(B)\) and \(c_{l\circ w}(B)\) by \((N+1)\) times the other, up to implied constants depending only on \(N\) and \(M\).
nodes.statement_short: C3 bounds each complexity by (N+1) times the other

nodes.name: Choose E_{N,M}
nodes.statement: Taking \(E_{N,M}\) to dominate both products gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Take E dominating both products

nodes.name: Lissity stratification of bounded complexity
nodes.statement: For every \(N\ge0\), there is a nondecreasing function \[ H_N:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\longrightarrow\mathbb R_{\ge0} \] with the following property. Let \(w:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\) be a locally closed embedding and let \(K\in D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) satisfy \(c_w(K)\le C\). There is a stratification \[ \operatorname{Supp} K=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in I}W_\alpha \] by smooth connected locally closed subvarieties such that every \(\mathcal{H}^i(K)|_{W_\alpha}\) is lisse and \[ \#I\le H_N(C), \qquad \sum_i\operatorname{rk}\bigl(\mathcal{H}^i(K)|_{W_\alpha}\bigr)\le H_N(C) \quad(\alpha\in I). \] The function \(H_N\) is independent of \(\Omega\) and of \(\ell\).
conclusions: There is a stratification \[ \operatorname{Supp} K=\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in I}W_\alpha \] by smooth connected locally closed subvarieties such that every \(\mathcal{H}^i(K)|_{W_\alpha}\) is lisse
nodes.label: lem:lissity-complexity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: For integral \(C\), Lemma~6.26 of \cite{SFFK23} gives a lissity stratification with bounds depending only on \((C,N)\) for the degrees of its components and the complexities of their immersions. Refining into connected components preserves such a bound. The restriction estimate \ref{item:C3} and the generic-rank bound \cite[Prop.~3.4]{SFFK23} then bound the displayed rank sum on every stratum. Taking the maximum of these bounds and applying the nondecreasing-majorant convention defines \(H_N\).
nodes.statement_short: Apply SFFK23 Lemma 6.26, refine to components, bound ranks by restriction estimates.

nodes.name: Lissity stratification
nodes.statement: For integral \(C\), Lemma~6.26 of \cite{SFFK23} gives a lissity stratification with bounds depending only on \((C,N)\) for the degrees of its components and the complexities of their immersions. Refining into connected components preserves such a bound.
nodes.statement_short: SFFK23 Lemma 6.26 gives bounded strata

nodes.name: Rank bound
nodes.statement: The restriction estimate \ref{item:C3} and the generic-rank bound \cite[Prop.~3.4]{SFFK23} then bound the displayed rank sum on every stratum.
nodes.statement_short: Restriction estimate bounds ranks

nodes.name: Define H_N
nodes.statement: Taking the maximum of these bounds and applying the nondecreasing-majorant convention defines \(H_N\).
nodes.statement_short: Maximum and majorant define H_N

nodes.name: Fixed function H_N
nodes.statement: For each \(N\ge0\), fix a function \(H_N\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity}.

nodes.name: Eigenvalue strata bound
nodes.statement: Let \(w:Y\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^N_\Omega\) be a locally closed embedding, let \(K\in D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and let \(\tau\in\operatorname{Aut}_{D^b_c(Y)}(K)\). Put \[ \operatorname{Eig}_Y(K,\tau) = \bigcup_{\substack{i\in\mathbb Z\\ \bar y\to Y\ \mathrm{geometric}}} \operatorname{Eig}\bigl(\mathcal{H}^i(\tau)_{\bar y}\bigr), \] where \(\operatorname{Eig}\bigl(\mathcal{H}^i(\tau)_{\bar y}\bigr)\) denotes the set of eigenvalues on \(\mathcal{H}^i(K)_{\bar y}\). Then \[ \#\operatorname{Eig}_Y(K,\tau)\le H_N(c_w(K))^2. \]
nodes.label: lem:eigenvalue-strata

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: Choose a stratification as in Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity}. On each connected stratum, the characteristic polynomial of \(\mathcal{H}^i(\tau)_{\bar y}\) is independent of \(\bar y\) for every \(i\). The number of eigenvalues contributed by the stratum is at most the sum of the ranks of the \(\mathcal{H}^i(K)\). Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity} bounds this sum and the number of strata by \(H_N(c_w(K))\).
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic polynomials are constant on lissity strata; count strata times ranks.

nodes.name: Choose strata
nodes.statement: Choose a stratification as in Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity}. On each connected stratum, the characteristic polynomial of \(\mathcal{H}^i(\tau)_{\bar y}\) is independent of \(\bar y\) for every \(i\).
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic polynomials constant on strata

nodes.name: Eigenvalues per stratum
nodes.statement: The number of eigenvalues contributed by the stratum is at most the sum of the ranks of the \(\mathcal{H}^i(K)\).
nodes.statement_short: Per-stratum eigenvalues bounded by rank sum

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity} bounds this sum and the number of strata by \(H_N(c_w(K))\).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.4 bounds strata and ranks

nodes.name: Tame fundamental group
nodes.statement: Let \(T/\Omega\) be a torus over an algebraically closed field. Choose a smooth compactification \(T\hookrightarrow\overline T\) whose boundary is a normal-crossings divisor. SGA~1 defines tame ramification along the boundary at its generic points and defines \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T)\) as the quotient of \(\pi_1(T)\) classifying finite \'etale covers with this ramification property \cite[Exp.~XIII, 2.1.1, 2.1.3, and Rem.~2.3(c)]{SGA1}.

nodes.name: Abhyankar's lemma (independence of compactification)
nodes.statement: Abhyankar's lemma shows that this condition is independent of the choice of a smooth compactification with normal-crossings boundary \cite[Exp.~XIII, Prop.~5.2]{SGA1}, \cite[\S1.9]{GabberLoeser1996}. Consequently, the resulting quotient \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T)\) does not depend on the compactification.
conclusions: this condition is independent of the choice of a smooth compactification with normal-crossings boundary

nodes.name: Kummer sheaf
nodes.statement: When \(\Omega\) has positive characteristic, Gabber--Loeser call the rank-one lisse sheaf attached to a continuous character of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T)\) a Kummer sheaf \cite[\S\S1.3--1.4]{GabberLoeser1996}.
differentia: attached to a continuous character of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T)\)

nodes.name: Prime-to-p profinite integers
nodes.statement: When \(\operatorname{char}\Omega=p>0\), put \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}=\prod_{\ell'\ne p}\mathbb Z_{\ell'}\), where the product is over primes \(\ell'\ne p\), and in characteristic zero put \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}=\widehat{\mathbb Z}\).

nodes.name: Cocharacter lattice and isogeny [n]
nodes.statement: For \(n\) invertible in \(\Omega\), the isogeny \([n]:T\to T\) is a connected Galois cover with group \(T[n]=X_*(T)\otimes\mu_n\), where \(X_*(T)=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbb{G}_m,T)\) is the cocharacter lattice.

nodes.name: Kummer description of the tame fundamental group of a torus
nodes.statement: Kummer theory identifies \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T,1)\) with the limit of these Galois groups over the isogenies \([n]\) for which \(n\) is invertible in \(\Omega\), giving a canonical isomorphism \[ \pi_1^{\mathrm t}(T,1) \simeq X_*(T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}(1) \] \cite[\S1.3]{GabberLoeser1996}. In characteristic zero the tame fundamental group is the full \'etale fundamental group and the same identification is classical.
nodes.statement_short: pi_1^t(T,1) is canonically X_*(T) tensor the prime-to-p Tate module.

nodes.name: Tame fundamental group of G_m^d is a product
nodes.statement: The identification is functorial in homomorphisms of tori, since \(f\circ[n]=[n]\circ f\) induces \(X_*(f)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mu_n}\) on the Galois groups. The coordinate projections identify \(X_*(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) with \(\bigoplus_{j=1}^dX_*(\mathbb{G}_m)\), so they induce an isomorphism \begin{equation} \pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega,1) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \prod_{j=1}^d\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m/\Omega,1). \end{equation} In particular, \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,1)\) is abelian. In positive characteristic \(p\), it is pro-prime-to-\(p\).
nodes.statement_short: Functoriality makes the coordinate projections identify pi_1^t(G_m^d) with a product of d copies of pi_1^t(G_m), which is abelian.

nodes.name: Product formula for the tame fundamental group
nodes.statement: \pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega,1) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \prod_{j=1}^d\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m/\Omega,1).
nodes.label: eq:tame-product

nodes.name: Henselian traits at 0 and infinity
nodes.statement: We now return to the standard compactification \(j:\mathbb{G}_m/\bar k\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_{\bar k}\). For \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), write \(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\mathbb{P}^1,x}\), with generic point \(\eta_x\) and geometric generic point \(\bar\eta_x\).

nodes.name: Inertia groups I_x and tame quotient
nodes.statement: Put \[ I_x=\operatorname{Gal}(\bar\eta_x/\eta_x), \qquad I_x^{\mathrm t}=I_x/P_x, \] where the wild inertia subgroup \(P_x\) is the kernel of the action of \(I_x\) on the maximal tamely ramified extension of the fraction field of \(\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{\mathbb{P}^1,x}\).

nodes.name: Tame inertia is the prime-to-p Tate module
nodes.statement: Applied to the trait \(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}\) with the divisor \(\{x\}\), \cite[Exp.~XIII, Cor.~5.3]{SGA1} identifies \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\) canonically with \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}(1)\), through the action on compatible systems of prime-to-\(p\) roots of a uniformizer.

nodes.name: Topological generator tau_x
nodes.statement: Choose a topological generator \(\tau_x\) of \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\).

nodes.name: Decomposition I_x^t = J_x x Gamma_x
nodes.statement: The primary decomposition of \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}(1)\) gives a canonical product decomposition \[ I_x^{\mathrm t}=J_x\times\Gamma_x, \qquad \tau_x=(\tau_{x,J},\gamma_x), \] where \(J_x\) is the product of the pro-\(\ell'\) factors over the primes \(\ell'\neq p,\ell\). The factor \(\Gamma_x\) is isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\), and \(\gamma_x\) is a topological generator of \(\Gamma_x\).

nodes.name: Local component lambda_x of a character
nodes.statement: The scheme map \(\eta_x\to\mathbb{G}_m\) induces \(I_x\to\pi_1(\mathbb{G}_m,\bar\eta_x)\) and, after a choice of path from \(\bar\eta_x\) to \(1\), a homomorphism \(I_x\to\pi_1(\mathbb{G}_m,1)\). Its composite with the projection to \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1)\) is independent of the path, because the target is abelian, and factors through \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\), because the image of the pro-\(p\) group \(P_x\) in a pro-prime-to-\(p\) group is trivial. For a continuous character \(\lambda\) of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1)\), let \(\lambda_x\) denote the restriction of \(\lambda\) to \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\) along this homomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: lambda_x is the restriction of a tame character lambda of G_m to tame inertia at x, via a path-independent homomorphism.

nodes.name: Kummer local monodromy
nodes.statement: For each \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), the homomorphism \[ I_x^{\mathrm t}\longrightarrow\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1) \] just defined is an isomorphism. Consequently, restriction of characters gives an isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1),\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}^\times\bigr) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x^{\mathrm t},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}^\times), \] and the map \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda_x(\tau_x)\) is injective on continuous characters of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1)\).
conclusions: the homomorphism \[ I_x^{\mathrm t}\longrightarrow\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1) \] just defined is an isomorphism
the map \(\lambda\mapsto\lambda_x(\tau_x)\) is injective on continuous characters of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m,1)\)
nodes.label: lem:kummer-local-monodromy

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.6
nodes.statement: Apply \cite[Exp.~XIII, Cor.~2.12]{SGA1} to \(\mathbb{G}_m=\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,\infty\}\). In the local identifications of \cite[Exp.~XIII, Cor.~5.3]{SGA1}, use the uniformizers \(t\) at \(0\) and \(t^{-1}\) at \(\infty\). With respect to these identifications and the global Kummer identification above, the maps at \(0\) and \(\infty\) are the identity and inversion, respectively, on \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}(1)\). Hence both maps are isomorphisms. The assertions about characters follow because a continuous character of a procyclic group is determined by its value at a topological generator.
nodes.statement_short: Via SGA 1 the local maps are identity and inversion on the prime-to-p Tate module.

nodes.name: Apply SGA 1
nodes.statement: Apply \cite[Exp.~XIII, Cor.~2.12]{SGA1} to \(\mathbb{G}_m=\mathbb{P}^1\setminus\{0,\infty\}\). In the local identifications of \cite[Exp.~XIII, Cor.~5.3]{SGA1}, use the uniformizers \(t\) at \(0\) and \(t^{-1}\) at \(\infty\).
nodes.statement_short: Use SGA 1 identifications with uniformizers t and 1/t

nodes.name: Identity and inversion
nodes.statement: With respect to these identifications and the global Kummer identification above, the maps at \(0\) and \(\infty\) are the identity and inversion, respectively, on \(\widehat{\mathbb Z}^{(p')}(1)\). Hence both maps are isomorphisms.
nodes.statement_short: The maps are identity and inversion, hence isomorphisms

nodes.name: Characters
nodes.statement: The assertions about characters follow because a continuous character of a procyclic group is determined by its value at a topological generator.
nodes.statement_short: Procyclic characters are determined by a generator

nodes.name: Uniform complexity of Kummer sheaves
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\), there is a constant \(\kappa_d\), depending only on \(d\), such that \[ c_u(\mathcal{L})\le\kappa_d \] for every algebraically closed field \(\Omega\), every prime \(\ell\) invertible in \(\Omega\), and every rank-one lisse \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega\) whose monodromy character factors through \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega,1)\).
assumptions: every algebraically closed field \(\Omega\), every prime \(\ell\) invertible in \(\Omega\), and every rank-one lisse \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-sheaf \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega\) whose monodromy character factors through \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\Omega,1)\)
nodes.label: lem:kummer-complexity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.7
nodes.statement: Let \(\lambda\) be the monodromy character of \(\mathcal{L}\). The product formula \eqref{eq:tame-product} decomposes \(\lambda\) as \(\prod_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\circ\operatorname{pr}_j\), where each \(\lambda_j\) is a continuous character of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m/\Omega,1)\). Hence \(\mathcal{L}\simeq\boxtimes_{j=1}^d\mathcal{L}_{\lambda_j}\). Suppose that \(d=1\) and that \(\mathcal{L}\) is nontrivial. A lisse sheaf on the connected nonproper curve \(\mathbb{G}_m\) has no nonzero sections with finite support, so \(H^0_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\). Poincar\'e duality identifies \(H^2_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})\) with a Tate twist of the dual of \(H^0(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L}^\vee)\), which vanishes because \(\mathcal{L}^\vee\) is nontrivial. The restrictions of \(\lambda\) to the inertia groups \(I_0\) and \(I_\infty\) are tamely ramified. Both Swan conductors of \(\mathcal{L}\) therefore vanish, and the Grothendieck--Ogg--Shafarevich formula \cite[\textit{Sommes trigonom\'etriques}, (3.2.1)]{SGA45} gives \(\chi_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\), so \(H^1_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\) as well. The curve-complexity formula \cite[Th.~7.3(1)]{SFFK23}, applied to the degree-one embedding \(u_1\), gives \(c_u(\mathcal{L})=1\), and it gives \(c_u(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})=2\) for the trivial local system. For general \(d\), the external-product estimate \ref{item:C5}, together with the uniform bounds of Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, bounds \(c_u(\boxtimes_{j=1}^d\mathcal{L}_{\lambda_j})\) by a constant \(\kappa_d\).
nodes.statement_short: Decompose as an external product; d=1 by Euler characteristic and the curve-complexity formula, general d by C5.

nodes.name: External product decomposition
nodes.statement: Let \(\lambda\) be the monodromy character of \(\mathcal{L}\). The product formula \eqref{eq:tame-product} decomposes \(\lambda\) as \(\prod_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\circ\operatorname{pr}_j\), where each \(\lambda_j\) is a continuous character of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m/\Omega,1)\). Hence \(\mathcal{L}\simeq\boxtimes_{j=1}^d\mathcal{L}_{\lambda_j}\).
nodes.statement_short: L is an external product of rank-one Kummer sheaves

nodes.name: Case d=1
nodes.statement: Suppose that \(d=1\) and that \(\mathcal{L}\) is nontrivial. A lisse sheaf on the connected nonproper curve \(\mathbb{G}_m\) has no nonzero sections with finite support, so \(H^0_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\). Poincar\'e duality identifies \(H^2_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})\) with a Tate twist of the dual of \(H^0(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L}^\vee)\), which vanishes because \(\mathcal{L}^\vee\) is nontrivial. The restrictions of \(\lambda\) to the inertia groups \(I_0\) and \(I_\infty\) are tamely ramified. Both Swan conductors of \(\mathcal{L}\) therefore vanish, and the Grothendieck--Ogg--Shafarevich formula \cite[\textit{Sommes trigonom\'etriques}, (3.2.1)]{SGA45} gives \(\chi_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\), so \(H^1_c(\mathbb{G}_m,\mathcal{L})=0\) as well. The curve-complexity formula \cite[Th.~7.3(1)]{SFFK23}, applied to the degree-one embedding \(u_1\), gives \(c_u(\mathcal{L})=1\), and it gives \(c_u(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})=2\) for the trivial local system.
nodes.statement_short: Cohomology vanishes; curve-complexity formula gives c_u=1 or 2

nodes.name: General d
nodes.statement: For general \(d\), the external-product estimate \ref{item:C5}, together with the uniform bounds of Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, bounds \(c_u(\boxtimes_{j=1}^d\mathcal{L}_{\lambda_j})\) by a constant \(\kappa_d\).
nodes.statement_short: External-product estimate gives kappa_d

nodes.name: Character scheme and its points
nodes.statement: The character scheme is that constructed by Gabber--Loeser \cite[\S3.2]{GabberLoeser1996} and used by Forey--Fres\'an--Kowalski \cite{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points are, by construction, the continuous characters of \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,1)\). We identify a character with the corresponding \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-point of the character scheme.

nodes.name: Kummer sheaves are tame at the boundary
nodes.statement: The associated sheaf \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\) therefore has monodromy factoring through \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,1)\), and hence is tamely ramified along the boundary of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\hookrightarrow(\mathbb{P}^1)^d\).
conclusions: has monodromy factoring through \(\pi_1^{\mathrm t}(\mathbb{G}_m^d,1)\), and hence is tamely ramified along the boundary of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\hookrightarrow(\mathbb{P}^1)^d\)

nodes.name: Lang isogeny
nodes.statement: Let \(F\) denote the \(q\)-power Frobenius endomorphism of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\). After base change to \(k_n\), the Lang isogeny is \[ L_n=F^n\cdot\operatorname{inv}\colon\mathbb{G}_m^d/k_n\longrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^d/k_n, \qquad (x_1,\ldots,x_d)\longmapsto(x_1^{q^n-1},\ldots,x_d^{q^n-1}). \]

nodes.name: Kummer sheaf of a finite-field character
nodes.statement: It is a finite \'etale Galois covering with group \(\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)\). It attaches to each \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}\) a Kummer sheaf \(\mathcal{L}_{\chi,0}\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k_n\) whose \(k_n\)-trace function is \(\chi\). Its base change to \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\bar k\) is the Kummer sheaf \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\).

nodes.name: Finite-field characters embed in the character scheme
nodes.statement: The Lang covering remains connected after base change to \(\bar k\), so the geometric fundamental group of \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) surjects onto \(\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)\). Geometric base change therefore defines an injective homomorphism \[ \widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}), \qquad \chi\longmapsto[\mathcal{L}_\chi]. \]
conclusions: Geometric base change therefore defines an injective homomorphism

nodes.name: Product decomposition of character groups
nodes.statement: For \(a,b\ge1\), the standard product decomposition gives \[ \widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{a+b}(k_n)} =\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^a(k_n)}\times\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^b(k_n)}, \qquad |\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}|=q^n-1 . \] For characters \(\lambda,\eta\) of the two factors, \(\mathcal{L}_{(\lambda,\eta)}\simeq\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal{L}_\eta\).

nodes.name: Negligible perverse sheaf
nodes.statement: Following \cite[\S3.6]{GabberLoeser1996}, a perverse sheaf \(N\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) is \emph{negligible} if \(\chi(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N)=0\).\footnote{Forey--Fres\'an--Kowalski define negligibility by requiring that the set \(\bigl\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\mid\mathrm{H}^0(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)=0\bigr\}\) be generic in the sense of \S\ref{sec:equidistribution} \cite[Def.~3.4]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, for perverse sheaves defined over a finite extension of \(k\). For such \(N\) the two definitions agree. For generic \(\lambda\), generic vanishing and invariance of the Euler--Poincar\'e characteristic under Kummer twists give \(\dim\mathrm{H}^0(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\lambda)=\chi(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N)\). See \cite[Prop.~3.22(2)--(3)]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.}

nodes.name: Serre subcategory of negligible perverse sheaves
