nodes.statement: Let \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) be the Serre subcategory of negligible perverse sheaves \cite[Lem.~3.6.2]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Negligible complex
nodes.statement: A complex \(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) is \emph{negligible} if \({}^pH^i(K)\) is negligible for every \(i\).

nodes.name: Negligible complexes form a thick subcategory
nodes.statement: The negligible complexes form a thick triangulated subcategory of \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) \cite[Prop.~3.6.1(i)]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Vanishing sets N(P) and N(K)
nodes.statement: For a perverse sheaf \(P\), put \[ \mathcal N(P)=\bigl\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,P_\chi)=0\ \text{and}\ R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,P_\chi)=0\bigr\}. \] For a complex \(K\), put \[ \mathcal N(K)=\bigcap_{i\in\mathbb Z}\mathcal N({}^pH^iK). \] A character \(\chi\) lies in \(\mathcal N(K)\) exactly when both cohomologies of every perverse cohomology sheaf of \(K\) vanish at \(\chi\).\footnote{The corresponding definition in \cite[\S3.4]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, stated for negligible complexes, displays a union in place of this intersection. The union is a misprint. It would make \(\mathcal N(K)\) the full character set, because \({}^pH^iK\) vanishes for all but finitely many \(i\) and \(\mathcal N(0)\) is the full character set. The proof of \cite[Lem.~3.28]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021} uses the intersection condition.}
nodes.statement_short: N(K) is the set of characters at which both cohomologies of every perverse cohomology sheaf of K vanish.

nodes.name: Category Perv_int
nodes.statement: Following \cite[Def.-Prop.~3.7.2]{GabberLoeser1996}, let \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) be the full subcategory of perverse sheaves with no nonzero negligible subobject or quotient.

nodes.name: Perv_int is equivalent to the quotient by negligibles
nodes.statement: Localization gives an equivalence \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)/\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) \cite[Def.-Prop.~3.7.2]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Arithmetic categories Perv_neg^ari and Perv_int^ari
nodes.statement: Following \cite[\S3.8]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, let \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) and \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) be the full subcategories of \(\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) consisting of the \(M_0\) for which \(M_{0,\bar k}\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) and \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), respectively.

nodes.name: Arithmetic quotient category P^ari
nodes.statement: Put \[ \mathcal P^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k) =\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)/\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k), \] and let \(q^{\mathrm{ari}}\) be the localization functor. It induces an equivalence \[ \operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \mathcal P^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k). \]

nodes.name: Convolutions *_! and *_*
nodes.statement: Let \(T\) denote either \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k\) or \(\mathbb{G}_m^d/\bar k\), and let \(m_T\colon T\times T\to T\) be multiplication. For \(A,B\in D^b_c(T)\), we write \(A\ast_!B=R(m_T)_!(A\boxtimes B)\) and \(A\ast_*B=R(m_T)_*(A\boxtimes B)\).

nodes.name: Convolution comparison morphism c_{A,B}
nodes.statement: The transformation \eqref{eq:forget-supports} for \(m_T\) gives the canonical morphism \begin{equation} c_{A,B}=\varphi_{m_T}(A\boxtimes B)\colon A\ast_!B\longrightarrow A\ast_*B. \end{equation} For \(T=\mathbb{G}_m^d/\bar k\), its twist by \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\) is denoted \(c_{A,B,\chi}\).

nodes.name: Convolution comparison morphism
nodes.statement: c_{A,B}=\varphi_{m_T}(A\boxtimes B)\colon A\ast_!B\longrightarrow A\ast_*B.
nodes.label: eq:convolution-comparison

nodes.name: Negligibility properties of convolution
nodes.statement: If \(K\) is negligible, then \(K\ast_!A\) and \(K\ast_*A\) are negligible for every \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\). Moreover, \(\operatorname{Cone}(c_{A,B})\) is negligible for all \(A,B\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\). If \(A\) and \(B\) are perverse, then \({}^pH^i(A\ast_!B)\) and \({}^pH^i(A\ast_*B)\) are negligible for every \(i\neq0\) \cite[Prop.~3.6.4]{GabberLoeser1996}.
nodes.statement_short: Convolution with a negligible complex is negligible, Cone(c_{A,B}) is negligible, and nonzero perverse degrees of convolutions are negligible.

nodes.name: Localized derived category
nodes.statement: Let \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be the Verdier quotient of \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) by the full thick triangulated subcategory of negligible complexes.

nodes.name: Perverse t-structure on the localized category
nodes.statement: The perverse \(t\)-structure descends to this quotient, and its heart is canonically equivalent to \(\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)/\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{neg}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) \cite[Prop.~3.6.1]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Localized convolution product
nodes.statement: The products \(\ast_!\) and \(\ast_*\) induce the same \(t\)-biexact product \(\ast_{\mathrm{loc}}\) on \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_{\mathrm{loc}}\) \cite[Def.-Prop.~3.6.5]{GabberLoeser1996}. For perverse \(A\) and \(B\), this product in the heart is represented by the localization of either \({}^pH^0(A\ast_!B)\) or \({}^pH^0(A\ast_*B)\).

nodes.name: Internal convolution
nodes.statement: Transporting this product through the equivalence of \S\ref{sec:negligible} defines the \emph{internal convolution} \(\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\) on \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\).\footnote{The name follows \cite[Def.~3.11]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Gabber--Loeser call this product the intermediate convolution, and the remark closing \cite[\S3.7]{GabberLoeser1996} identifies it for \(d=1\) with Katz's middle convolution.}
nodes.origin_citation: Gabber & Loeser 1996; Forey, Fresan & Kowalski 2021, Def. 3.11

nodes.name: Intermediate extension P_int
nodes.statement: For a perverse sheaf \(P\), let \(P_{\mathrm{int}}\) denote the image of its localization under the quasi-inverse equivalence.

nodes.name: Formula for internal convolution
nodes.statement: For \(A,B\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), \[ A\ast_{\mathrm{int}}B \simeq\bigl({}^pH^0(A\ast_!B)\bigr)_{\mathrm{int}} \simeq\bigl({}^pH^0(A\ast_*B)\bigr)_{\mathrm{int}} \] canonically \cite[Def.-Prop.~3.7.3]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Arithmetic convolution tensor category
nodes.statement: Following \cite[\S3.8]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, let \(A_0,B_0\in\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). The two objects \[ q^{\mathrm{ari}}\bigl({}^pH^0(A_0\ast_!B_0)\bigr) \quad\text{and}\quad q^{\mathrm{ari}}\bigl({}^pH^0(A_0\ast_*B_0)\bigr) \] depend functorially only on \(q^{\mathrm{ari}}(A_0)\) and \(q^{\mathrm{ari}}(B_0)\), and they are canonically isomorphic. Their common product makes \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) a rigid symmetric \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-linear tensor category.

nodes.name: Arithmetic internal convolution
nodes.statement: Transporting it through the arithmetic equivalence in \S\ref{sec:negligible} defines \(\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\) on \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\).

nodes.name: Geometric base change is a symmetric tensor functor
nodes.statement: Geometric base change is a symmetric tensor functor \[ \bigl(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k),\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\bigr) \longrightarrow \bigl(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d),\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\bigr) \] \cite[\S3.8]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Convolution dual
nodes.statement: In either category, the convolution dual is \(P^\vee=\operatorname{inv}^*D(P)\) \cite[\S1.5]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Convolution powers
nodes.statement: For \(?\in\{!,*\}\) and \(A\in D^b_c(T)\), and for \(?=\mathrm{int}\) and \(A\) in either \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) or \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\), define the convolution powers recursively by \[ A^{\ast_?1}=A, \qquad A^{\ast_?(r+1)}=A^{\ast_?r}\ast_?A. \]

nodes.name: Complexity of convolution powers
nodes.statement: For every \(d,r\ge1\) and \(?\in\{!,*,\mathrm{int}\}\), there is a nondecreasing function \[ F_{d,r,?}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\longrightarrow\mathbb R_{\ge0}, \] depending only on \(d,r,?\), such that \[ c_u\bigl(A^{\ast_?r}\bigr)\le F_{d,r,?}(c_u(A)). \] Here \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) for \(?\in\{!,*\}\), and \(A\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) for \(?=\mathrm{int}\). The function is independent of the algebraically closed base field and of \(\ell\).
nodes.label: cor:convolution-complexity

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2.8
nodes.statement: By \ref{item:C3}, \ref{item:C5}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, for each \(?\in\{!,*\}\) there is a constant \(a_{d,?}\ge1\), depending only on \(d\) and \(?\), such that \[ c_u(A\ast_?B)\le a_{d,?}c_u(A)c_u(B). \] The constants are independent of the algebraically closed base field and of \(\ell\). Induction on \(r\) gives the result for \(!\) and \(*\). Internal convolution is a subquotient of \({}^pH^0(A\ast_!B)\) \cite[Def.~3.7.1, Def.-Prop.~3.7.2]{GabberLoeser1996}. Thus \ref{item:C6} gives the same bilinear estimate, with a constant depending only on \(d\), for \(\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\). A second induction on \(r\) proves the internal case.
nodes.statement_short: Bilinear complexity bound for one convolution, then induction on r; internal case via C6.

nodes.name: Bilinear bound
nodes.statement: By \ref{item:C3}, \ref{item:C5}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, for each \(?\in\{!,*\}\) there is a constant \(a_{d,?}\ge1\), depending only on \(d\) and \(?\), such that \[ c_u(A\ast_?B)\le a_{d,?}c_u(A)c_u(B). \] The constants are independent of the algebraically closed base field and of \(\ell\).
nodes.statement_short: c_u(A*B) <= a c_u(A) c_u(B)

nodes.name: Induction for ! and *
nodes.statement: Induction on \(r\) gives the result for \(!\) and \(*\).
nodes.statement_short: Induct on r

nodes.name: Internal convolution
nodes.statement: Internal convolution is a subquotient of \({}^pH^0(A\ast_!B)\) \cite[Def.~3.7.1, Def.-Prop.~3.7.2]{GabberLoeser1996}. Thus \ref{item:C6} gives the same bilinear estimate, with a constant depending only on \(d\), for \(\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\).
nodes.statement_short: C6 gives the bilinear bound for *_int

nodes.name: Second induction
nodes.statement: A second induction on \(r\) proves the internal case.
nodes.statement_short: Induct on r for *_int

nodes.name: Mellin transforms M_! and M_*
nodes.statement: Gabber--Loeser \cite[\S3.3]{GabberLoeser1996} attach to \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) two Mellin transforms \(\mathscr M_!\) and \(\mathscr M_*\), with values in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), together with a natural transformation \(\mathscr M_!\to\mathscr M_*\).

nodes.name: Point i_chi and derived restriction
nodes.statement: For \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), let \(i_\chi:\operatorname{Spec}\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\to\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) be the corresponding point and let \(Li_\chi^*\) denote derived restriction.

nodes.name: Comparison notation phi_K, phi_{K,chi}, Theta_{A,B,chi}
nodes.statement: For \(K,A,B\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) and using notation from \S\ref{sec:convolution}, we write \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \varphi_K\colon \mathscr M_!(K)\longrightarrow\mathscr M_*(K), \qquad R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi) \xrightarrow{\varphi_{K,\chi}} R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi),\\ \Theta_{A,B,\chi} :=\varphi_{A\ast_*B,\chi}\circ R\Gamma_c(c_{A,B,\chi})\colon R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_!B)_\chi\bigr) \longrightarrow R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_*B)_\chi\bigr). \end{gathered} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Comparison morphisms phi_K and Theta_{A,B,chi}
nodes.statement: \begin{gathered} \varphi_K\colon \mathscr M_!(K)\longrightarrow\mathscr M_*(K), \qquad R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi) \xrightarrow{\varphi_{K,\chi}} R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi),\\ \Theta_{A,B,\chi} :=\varphi_{A\ast_*B,\chi}\circ R\Gamma_c(c_{A,B,\chi})\colon R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_!B)_\chi\bigr) \longrightarrow R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_*B)_\chi\bigr). \end{gathered}
nodes.label: eq:comparison-notation

nodes.name: Fibres of the Mellin transforms
nodes.statement: \emph{Fibres} \cite[Cor.~3.3.2]{GabberLoeser1996}. One has \(Li_\chi^*\mathscr M_!(K)\simeq R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi)\) and \(Li_\chi^*\mathscr M_*(K)\simeq R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi)\). Under these identifications, \(Li_\chi^*(\varphi_K)=\varphi_{K,\chi}\) \cite[Prop.~3.3.4(i)]{GabberLoeser1996}.

nodes.name: Support of the cone of the Mellin comparison
nodes.statement: \emph{Support of the cone} \cite[Def.~3.3.3, Prop.~3.3.4(i)]{GabberLoeser1996}. \[ \Delta(K) =\operatorname{Supp}\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\mathscr M_!(K)\xrightarrow{\varphi_K}\mathscr M_*(K)\bigr). \] Its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points are \[ \Delta(K)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}) =\bigl\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi)\xrightarrow{\varphi_{K,\chi}} R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,K_\chi)\text{ is \emph{not} an isomorphism}\bigr\}. \]

nodes.name: Monoidality of the Mellin transforms
nodes.statement: \emph{Monoidality} \cite[Prop.~3.3.1(f)]{GabberLoeser1996}. There are canonical isomorphisms \(\mathscr M_!(A\ast_!B)\simeq\mathscr M_!(A)\otimes^L\mathscr M_!(B)\) and \(\mathscr M_*(A\ast_*B)\simeq\mathscr M_*(A)\otimes^L\mathscr M_*(B)\), natural in \(A\) and \(B\). The fibrewise compatibility of the comparison \(\mathscr M_!\to\mathscr M_*\) with convolution used below is recorded in Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-monoidal}.

nodes.name: Localization by Mellin support
nodes.statement: \emph{Localization}. The support theorem \cite[Th.~6.1.1(b)]{GabberLoeser1996} gives \[ \operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_!(K)=\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_*(K) \qquad(K\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)). \] For closed \(Z\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), let \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_Z\) be the Verdier quotient of \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) by the full triangulated subcategory of objects whose Mellin transforms are supported in \(Z\). Then \(K=0\) in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_Z\) if and only if \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_!(K)\subseteq Z\), equivalently if and only if \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_*(K)\subseteq Z\). The perverse \(t\)-structure descends to \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_Z\), and the localization functor is \(t\)-exact \cite[Prop.~3.6.1, Lem.~3.9.1]{GabberLoeser1996}. The negligible complexes form a thick triangulated subcategory of \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\).

nodes.name: Localization criterion for morphisms
nodes.statement: \emph{Localization criterion for morphisms} \cite[Prop.~3.9.2]{GabberLoeser1996}. Suppose that \(f:A\to B\) is a morphism in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) such that the composite \[ \mathscr M_!(A)\xrightarrow{\mathscr M_!(f)}\mathscr M_!(B)\longrightarrow\mathscr M_*(B) \] is an isomorphism outside a closed subset \(Z\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), then \(f\) is an isomorphism in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_Z\), and both \(\Delta(A)\) and \(\Delta(B)\) are contained in \(Z\).

nodes.name: Structure of the character scheme
nodes.statement: \emph{Character scheme} \cite[\S\S3.2.2--3.2.3, Props.~A.2.2.2, A.2.2.3]{GabberLoeser1996}. Each connected component of \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is affine, noetherian, regular, and Jacobson, and its closed points are exactly its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points.

nodes.name: Geometric base change of arithmetically semisimple objects is semisimple
nodes.statement: Let \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) be arithmetically semisimple and let \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\), which is semisimple in \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) \cite[Lem.~1.28]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Tannakian categories and tannakian groups
nodes.statement: \emph{Tannakian category} \cite[Def.~3.7.1--Th.~3.7.5]{GabberLoeser1996}, \cite[Th.~3.16]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Internal convolution makes \(\langle M\rangle\), the subcategory of \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) generated by \(M\) under \(\ast_{\mathrm{int}}\), convolution duals, direct sums, subquotients, and summands, a neutral tannakian category. Its unit object is the skyscraper sheaf \(\delta_1\) at the identity \cite[Def.-Prop.~3.6.5, Prop.~3.7.4(ii)]{GabberLoeser1996}. Let \(\langle M_0\rangle^{\mathrm{ari}}\) be the full tensor subcategory of \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) tensor-generated by \(M_0\), and write \(\langle M\rangle^{\mathrm{geo}}=\langle M\rangle\). Both categories are neutral tannakian. There are algebraic groups \(G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}\) and \(G_M^{\mathrm{geo}}\) over \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) and tensor equivalences \[ \langle M_0\rangle^{\mathrm{ari}} \simeq\operatorname{Rep}_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\bigl(G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}\bigr), \qquad \langle M\rangle^{\mathrm{geo}} \simeq\operatorname{Rep}_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\bigl(G_M^{\mathrm{geo}}\bigr). \] These are the arithmetic and geometric tannakian groups. Geometric base change is a tensor functor and induces a closed immersion \(G_M^{\mathrm{geo}}\hookrightarrow G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}\) \cite[Th.~3.30, Def.~3.31, Prop.~3.32]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.
nodes.origin_citation: Gabber & Loeser 1996, 3.7; Forey, Fresan & Kowalski 2021, Th. 3.16, 3.30
nodes.statement_short: <M> and <M_0>^ari are neutral tannakian with unit delta_1, with groups G^geo in G^ari.

nodes.name: Semisimplicity and tensor generators
nodes.statement: \emph{Semisimplicity and generators}. Since \(M\) is semisimple, its tannakian group is reductive and \(\langle M\rangle\) is semisimple \cite[Cor.~3.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. The self-dual object \(M\oplus M^\vee\) is a tensor generator, so every object of \(\langle M\rangle\) is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of its internal convolution powers \cite[Prop.~3.1]{Del82}, \cite[Prop.~1.30]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.
nodes.origin_citation: Forey, Fresan & Kowalski 2021, Cor. 3.19, Prop. 1.30; Deligne 1982

nodes.name: Arithmetic objects attached to representations
nodes.statement: \emph{Arithmetic objects and representations}. If \(M_0\) is pure of weight zero, then the category \(\langle M_0\rangle^{\mathrm{ari}}\) is semisimple. An irreducible algebraic representation \(\rho\) of \(G^{\mathrm{ari}}_M\) corresponds to an arithmetically semisimple object \(N_0=\rho(M_0)\) that is pure of weight zero \cite[Th.~3.30 and Th.~3.33]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. For some \(m(\rho)\ge1\), this object is a direct summand of \[ L_0^{\ast_{\mathrm{int}}m(\rho)}, \qquad L_0=M_0\oplus M_0^\vee, \] and its geometric base change is a direct summand of \(L^{\ast_{\mathrm{int}}m(\rho)}\), where \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\) \cite[Prop.~3.1]{Del82}, \cite[Cor.~3.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}.

nodes.name: Kunneth isomorphisms for convolution
nodes.statement: \emph{Cohomology of convolution} \cite[Lem.~1.15]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. For \(A,B\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) and \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), write \[ \begin{aligned} \kappa_!\colon R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)\otimes R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,B_\chi) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_!B)_\chi\bigr),\\ \kappa_*\colon R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)\otimes R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,B_\chi) &\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_*B)_\chi\bigr) \end{aligned} \] for the K\"unneth isomorphisms. Their compatibility with the forget-supports morphisms is Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-monoidal}.

nodes.name: Unramified characters and Frobenius conjugacy classes
nodes.statement: \emph{Unramified characters and Frobenius} \cite[Def.~3.25, Lem.~3.28, \S\S3.8--3.9]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. A character \(\chi\in X_w(M)\), where \(X_w(M)\) is as in \eqref{eq:weak-locus}, is \emph{unramified} for \(M\) if \(\omega_\chi:N\mapsto H^0(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\) is a fibre functor on \(\langle M\rangle\). We write \(X(M)\subseteq X_w(M)\) for the set of unramified characters. If \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) and \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\), define \(X(M_0)=X(M)\). For \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), let \(\alpha_1=\operatorname{id}_L\) and, for \(m\ge2\), put \[ \alpha_m =c_{L^{\ast_*(m-1)},L}\circ\bigl(\alpha_{m-1}\ast_!\operatorname{id}_L\bigr) \colon L^{\ast_!m}\longrightarrow L^{\ast_*m}, \qquad C_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha_m). \] Write \(\mu_m\colon(\mathbb{G}_m^d)^m\to\mathbb{G}_m^d\) for the \(m\)-fold multiplication, so that \(L^{\ast_!m}=R\mu_{m,!}(L^{\boxtimes m})\) and \(L^{\ast_*m}=R\mu_{m,*}(L^{\boxtimes m})\). Then \(\alpha_m=\varphi_{\mu_m}(L^{\boxtimes m})\). This holds for \(m=1\), and for \(m\ge2\) it follows by induction from Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports}(2) applied to \(\mu_m=m_T\circ(\mu_{m-1}\times\operatorname{id})\). In that identity the outer factor is \(\varphi_{m_T}\bigl(L^{\ast_*(m-1)}\boxtimes L\bigr)=c_{L^{\ast_*(m-1)},L}\), and the inner one is \(\alpha_{m-1}\ast_!\operatorname{id}_L\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(1) together with \(\varphi_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}\) from Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports}(1). The associativity constraints match the parenthesizations of the iterated convolutions compatibly with these morphisms, so \(\alpha_m\) is the canonical morphism \(L^{\ast_!m}\to L^{\ast_*m}\). Every \(C_m\) is negligible,\footnote{For \(m=2\) one has \(C_2=\operatorname{Cone}(c_{L,L})\), which is negligible by \S\ref{sec:convolution}. Suppose that \(C_{m-1}\) is negligible. The cone of \(\alpha_{m-1}\ast_!\operatorname{id}_L\) is \(C_{m-1}\ast_!L\), hence is negligible, and so is the cone of \(c_{L^{\ast_*(m-1)},L}\), again by \S\ref{sec:convolution}. The negligible complexes form a thick triangulated subcategory by \ref{item:GL4}, so the octahedral axiom applied to the definition of \(\alpha_m\) gives the assertion for \(C_m\).} so \(\mathcal N(C_m)\) in the sense of \S\ref{sec:negligible} is the set defined in \cite[\S3.4]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, where negligibility of the complex is part of the definition. Hence \cite[Lem.~3.28]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021} gives \[ X_w(M)\cap\bigcap_{m\ge2}\mathcal N(C_m)\subseteq X(M). \] Suppose that \(M_0\) is arithmetically semisimple and pure of weight zero. For \(n\ge1\) and \(\chi\in X(M_0)(k_n)\), geometric Frobenius \(\operatorname{Fr}_{k_n}\) acts on \[ \omega_\chi(N_0)=H^0(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi), \qquad N=N_{0,\bar k}, \] for every \(N_0\in\langle M_0\rangle^{\mathrm{ari}}\). Every such \(N_0\) is pure of weight zero, and \(\omega_\chi(N_0)\) with its Frobenius action is pure of weight zero \cite[Th.~3.33, \S3.9]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. These actions define a tensor automorphism of \(\omega_\chi\), hence a conjugacy class \(\operatorname{Fr}_{M_0,k_n}(\chi)\) in \(G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Using the isomorphism \(\iota\) fixed in \S\ref{sec:equidistribution}, fix a maximal compact subgroup \(K_M\subseteq G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{C})\). Following \cite[\S3.9]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, the Frobenius conjugacy class determines a unitary Frobenius conjugacy class \[ \Theta_{M_0,k_n}(\chi)\in K_M^\sharp. \] For an algebraic representation \(\rho\) of \(G_M^{\mathrm{ari}}\), put \(N_0=\rho(M_0)\) and \(N=N_{0,\bar k}\). By \cite[Lem.~3.35(2)]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}, applied over \(k_n\), the character \(\chi\) is unramified for \(N_0\). Hence \(\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)=0\) for \(i\ne0\), and the trace identity used below is \[ \operatorname{Tr}\rho\bigl(\Theta_{M_0,k_n}(\chi)\bigr) =\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\operatorname{Fr}_{k_n}\mid\mathrm{H}^0_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\bigr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Unramified characters are those where H^0 is a fibre functor; alpha_m, C_m relate them to negligibility; Frobenius gives unitary classes Theta with trace identity.

nodes.name: Kunneth compatibility of the comparison morphisms
nodes.statement: With the notation of \ref{item:T4}, the following diagram commutes for \(A,B\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) and \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). \[ \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)\otimes R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,B_\chi) \arrow[r,"\varphi_{A,\chi}\otimes\varphi_{B,\chi}"] \arrow[d,"\kappa_!"',"\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"] & R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_\chi)\otimes R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m^d,B_\chi) \arrow[d,"\kappa_*","\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"'] \\ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_!B)_\chi\bigr) \arrow[r,"\Theta_{A,B,\chi}"'] & R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(A\ast_*B)_\chi\bigr). \end{tikzcd} \]
nodes.label: lem:comparison-monoidal

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.9
nodes.statement: Write \(f\colon \mathbb{G}_m^d\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\) for the structure morphism and \(m\colon \mathbb{G}_m^d\times \mathbb{G}_m^d\to \mathbb{G}_m^d\) for multiplication. Apply \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse} with \(p=m\), \(K=A\boxtimes B\), and \(\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_\chi\). Under \(m^*\mathcal{L}_\chi\simeq\mathcal{L}_\chi\boxtimes\mathcal{L}_\chi\), its upper arrow is \(\varphi_{f\times f}(A_\chi\boxtimes B_\chi)\), and its lower composite is \(\Theta_{A,B,\chi}\). The external K\"unneth morphisms followed by \(\beta_!\) and \(\beta_*\) are the maps \(\kappa_!\) and \(\kappa_*\) of \ref{item:T4}. Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(1) therefore gives the stated diagram.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the combined compatibility (4) to multiplication, then Lemma A.2(1).

nodes.name: Apply diagram (4)
nodes.statement: Write \(f\colon \mathbb{G}_m^d\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\) for the structure morphism and \(m\colon \mathbb{G}_m^d\times \mathbb{G}_m^d\to \mathbb{G}_m^d\) for multiplication. Apply \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse} with \(p=m\), \(K=A\boxtimes B\), and \(\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_\chi\).
nodes.statement_short: Apply (4) with p=m

nodes.name: Identify arrows
nodes.statement: Under \(m^*\mathcal{L}_\chi\simeq\mathcal{L}_\chi\boxtimes\mathcal{L}_\chi\), its upper arrow is \(\varphi_{f\times f}(A_\chi\boxtimes B_\chi)\), and its lower composite is \(\Theta_{A,B,\chi}\).
nodes.statement_short: Upper arrow is phi_{fxf}, lower composite Theta

nodes.name: Identify Kunneth maps
nodes.statement: The external K\"unneth morphisms followed by \(\beta_!\) and \(\beta_*\) are the maps \(\kappa_!\) and \(\kappa_*\) of \ref{item:T4}.
nodes.statement_short: Kunneth maps with beta are kappa

nodes.name: Apply Lemma A.2(1)
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(1) therefore gives the stated diagram.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude by Lemma A.2(1)

nodes.name: Base S with embedding v
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, \(S\) is a quasi-projective \(\bar k\)-variety with a fixed locally closed embedding \begin{equation} v:S\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N_S}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Embedding of the base
nodes.statement: v:S\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N_S}.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:relative-base-embedding

nodes.name: Relative P^1_S and G_{m,S}
nodes.statement: Put \(\mathbb{P}^1_S=\mathbb{P}^1\times_{\bar k}S\) and \(\mathbb{G}_{m,S}=\mathbb{G}_m\times_{\bar k}S\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Embedding w_v of G_{m,S}
nodes.statement: Let \[ w_v:\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2N_S+1} \] be the immersion induced by \(v\) and the Segre embedding. Complexities on \(S\) and \(\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\) are denoted by \(c_v\) and \(c_{w_v}\), respectively.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Maps j_x and f_x
nodes.statement: For \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), with \(U_x\) and \(t_x\) as in \S\ref{sec:embeddings}, let \[ \begin{aligned} j_x&:\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\hookrightarrow U_x\times S,\\ f_x&=t_x\circ\operatorname{pr}_1:U_x\times S\longrightarrow\mathbb{A}^1. \end{aligned} \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Embedding v_x
nodes.statement: Equip \(U_x\times S\) with the locally closed embedding \[ v_x:U_x\times S \hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2N_S+1} \] induced by \(v\) and the Segre embedding.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Relative trait (P^1_(x))_S
nodes.statement: Via \(t_x\), identify \(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}\) with \(\mathbb{A}^1_{(0)}\), and put \((\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S=\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}\times_{\bar k}S\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Projection q_x and base change rho_x
nodes.statement: Let \[ q_x:(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S\longrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}, \qquad \rho_x:(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S\longrightarrow U_x\times S \] be the projection and the natural base-change morphism. Thus \(q_x\) identifies with the base change of \(f_x\) to \(\mathbb{A}^1_{(0)}\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Fibre maps iota_x, bar j_x and nu_x
nodes.statement: Let \[ \iota_x:S\hookrightarrow(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S, \qquad \bar j_x:\bar\eta_x\times S\longrightarrow(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S \] be the special- and geometric-generic-fibre maps, and let \(\nu_x:\eta_x\times S\to\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\) be the natural morphism.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Relative nearby cycles R Psi_x
nodes.statement: For \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_{m,S})\), put \[ R\Psi_x A:=R\Psi_{q_x}\bigl(\rho_x^*Rj_{x,*}A\bigr)\in D^b_c(S), \] where \(R\Psi_{q_x}\) is the nearby-cycle functor over the trait \(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)}\) \cite[Exp.~XIII, \S2.1]{SGA7II}.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Finiteness and inertia action on nearby cycles
nodes.statement: The complex \(R\Psi_xA\) carries its continuous \(I_x\)-action, and its cohomology sheaves are constructible \cite[\textit{Th\'eor\`emes de finitude}, Th.~3.2]{SGA45}. Consequently, Lemma~\ref{lem:eigenvalue-strata} applies to every automorphism induced by an element of \(I_x\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Strict-henselian description of relative nearby cycles
nodes.statement:
The diagram \[  egin{tikzcd}[column sep=large]  ar\eta_x	imes S \arrow[r," ar j_x"] \arrow[d] &(\mathbb{P}^1_{(x)})_S \arrow[d,"ho_x"]\ \eta_x	imes S \arrow[r] \arrow[d,"
u_x"'] &U_x	imes S\ \mathbb{G}_{m,S}\arrow[ur,"j_x"'] \end{tikzcd} \] commutes. Since \(j_x^*Rj_{x,*}A\simeq A\), it identifies the restriction of \(ho_x^*Rj_{x,*}A\) to \( ar\eta_x	imes S\) with \((
u_x^*A)|_{ ar\eta_x	imes S}\). The strict-henselian description of nearby cycles \cite[Exp.~XIII, (2.1.2.3)]{SGA7II} therefore gives an \(I_x\)-equivariant identification  egin{equation} R\Psi_x A\simeq \iota_x^*R ar j_{x,*}  igl((
u_x^*A)|_{ ar\eta_x	imes S} igr). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: The commuting diagram and the strict-henselian description identify R Psi_x A I_x-equivariantly with iota_x^* R bar j_{x,*} of the generic fibre.

nodes.name: Strict-henselian nearby cycles
nodes.statement: R\Psi_x A\simeq \iota_x^*R\bar j_{x,*} \bigl((\nu_x^*A)|_{\bar\eta_x\times S}\bigr).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:strict-henselian-nearby-cycles

nodes.name: Geometric complexity parameter D(S,v)
nodes.statement: Using the complexity notation of \ref{item:C1}, put \begin{equation} D(S,v):= \max\left\{ c(w_v),\,c(a),\,c(v_x),\,c_{w_v,v_x}(j_x),\,c_{v_x,a}(f_x) \ \middle|\ x\in\{0,\infty\} \right\}. \end{equation} Thus \(D(S,v)\) records the complexities of the embedded varieties and morphisms used to form the relative nearby cycles.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Definition of D(S,v)
nodes.statement: D(S,v):= \max\left\{ c(w_v),\,c(a),\,c(v_x),\,c_{w_v,v_x}(j_x),\,c_{v_x,a}(f_x) \ \middle|\ x\in\{0,\infty\} \right\}.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:relative-geometric-complexity

nodes.name: D(S,v) bounded for the standard bases
nodes.statement: For \(r\ge1\), Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity} bounds \(D(\mathbb{G}_m^r,u_r)\) solely in terms of \(r\). The same lemma bounds \(D(\operatorname{Spec}\bar k,\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{P}^0})\) by an absolute constant.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
conclusions: bounds \(D(\operatorname{Spec}\bar k,\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb{P}^0})\) by an absolute constant

nodes.name: Complexity of coordinate nearby cycles
nodes.statement: For every \(N,D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), there is a constant \(g_{N,D}\ge1\) such that, whenever \(N_S=N\) and \(D(S,v)\le D\), \[ c_v(R\Psi_x A)\le g_{N,D}\,c_{w_v}(A) \qquad(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_{m,S}),\ x=0,\infty). \] The constant is independent of \(\bar k\) and of \(\ell\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: lem:coordinate-nearby-complexity

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: With respect to the displayed embeddings, the six-operation estimates \ref{item:C3} bound the complexity of \(Rj_{x,*}A\) by a constant depending only on \((N,D)\) times \(c_{w_v}(A)\). The nearby-cycle estimate \ref{item:C7}, applied to the flat morphism \(f_x\) at \(0\in\mathbb{A}^1\) with input \(Rj_{x,*}A\), bounds the complexity of \(R\Psi_{q_x}\bigl(\rho_x^*Rj_{x,*}A\bigr)=R\Psi_xA\) with respect to the induced embedding of the special fibre \(\{x\}\times S\). This embedding equals \(\sigma_x\circ v\), where \(\sigma_x:\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2N_S+1}\) is the linear closed immersion obtained from the Segre embedding by fixing the first factor at \(x\). Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-reembedding} converts the resulting estimate into the asserted bound for \(c_v(R\Psi_xA)\). Taking the larger constant for \(x=0,\infty\) gives \(g_{N,D}\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Six-operation and nearby-cycle complexity estimates, then linear re-embedding (Lemma 2.3).

nodes.name: Bound Rj_*A
nodes.statement: With respect to the displayed embeddings, the six-operation estimates \ref{item:C3} bound the complexity of \(Rj_{x,*}A\) by a constant depending only on \((N,D)\) times \(c_{w_v}(A)\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: C3 bounds c(Rj_{x,*}A)

nodes.name: Nearby-cycle estimate
nodes.statement: The nearby-cycle estimate \ref{item:C7}, applied to the flat morphism \(f_x\) at \(0\in\mathbb{A}^1\) with input \(Rj_{x,*}A\), bounds the complexity of \(R\Psi_{q_x}\bigl(\rho_x^*Rj_{x,*}A\bigr)=R\Psi_xA\) with respect to the induced embedding of the special fibre \(\{x\}\times S\). This embedding equals \(\sigma_x\circ v\), where \(\sigma_x:\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2N_S+1}\) is the linear closed immersion obtained from the Segre embedding by fixing the first factor at \(x\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: C7 bounds R Psi_x A on the special fibre

nodes.name: Re-embed
nodes.statement: Lemma~\ref{lem:linear-reembedding} converts the resulting estimate into the asserted bound for \(c_v(R\Psi_xA)\). Taking the larger constant for \(x=0,\infty\) gives \(g_{N,D}\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.3 converts to c_v

nodes.name: Inertia cohomology forces an eigenvalue
nodes.statement: Fix \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), and let \(\widetilde\tau_x\in I_x\) be a lift of the topological generator \(\tau_x\in I_x^{\mathrm t}\) chosen in \S\ref{sec:tame-kummer}. Let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional continuous \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-representation of \(I_x\), and let \(\xi\) be a continuous tame character of \(I_x\), viewed also as a character of \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\). If \[ H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x,V\otimes\xi)\neq0 \] for some \(a\in\mathbb Z\), then the scalar \(\xi(\tau_x)^{-1}\) is an eigenvalue of \(\widetilde\tau_x\) on \(V\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
assumptions: \(\xi\) be a continuous tame character of \(I_x\)
conclusions: the scalar \(\xi(\tau_x)^{-1}\) is an eigenvalue of \(\widetilde\tau_x\) on \(V\)
nodes.label: lem:inertia-eigenvalue

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.2
nodes.statement: The wild inertia group \(P_x\) is pro-\(p\), and \(\xi\) is trivial on \(P_x\). Apply Hochschild--Serre to \(1\to P_x\to I_x\to I_x^{\mathrm t}\to1\). Since \(\ell\neq p\), Lemma~\ref{lem:prime-to-ell-vanishing} gives \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x,V\otimes\xi) \simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x^{\mathrm t},V^{P_x}\otimes\xi). \] Recall from \S\ref{sec:tame-kummer} the decomposition \(I_x^{\mathrm t}=J_x\times\Gamma_x\) with \(\tau_x=(\tau_{x,J},\gamma_x)\). Put \(V_0=(V^{P_x}\otimes\xi)^{J_x}\). Hochschild--Serre and Lemma~\ref{lem:prime-to-ell-vanishing}, now applied to \(1\to J_x\to I_x^{\mathrm t}\to\Gamma_x\to1\), give \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x^{\mathrm t},V^{P_x}\otimes\xi) \simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma_x,V_0). \] The complex on the right is nonzero. By Lemma~\ref{lem:zell-cohomology}, the endomorphism \(\gamma_x-1\) of the finite-dimensional vector space \(V_0\) is not invertible. Hence there is a nonzero \(u\in V_0\) fixed by \(\gamma_x\). Since \(u\) is also fixed by \(J_x\), it is fixed by \(\tau_x\) on \(V^{P_x}\otimes\xi\). Write \(u=v\otimes1\), with \(0\neq v\in V^{P_x}\). Since \(\xi\) factors through \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\), the fixed-vector equation for the chosen lift is \(\xi(\tau_x)\widetilde\tau_x v=v\), and hence \[ \widetilde\tau_x v=\xi(\tau_x)^{-1}v. \] Thus \(v\) is the required eigenvector. Since \(P_x\) fixes \(v\), every lift of \(\tau_x\) acts on \(v\) in the same way.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Hochschild-Serre twice with prime-to-l vanishing reduces to Z_l-cohomology, where a fixed vector gives the eigenvector.

nodes.name: Remove wild inertia
nodes.statement: The wild inertia group \(P_x\) is pro-\(p\), and \(\xi\) is trivial on \(P_x\). Apply Hochschild--Serre to \(1\to P_x\to I_x\to I_x^{\mathrm t}\to1\). Since \(\ell\neq p\), Lemma~\ref{lem:prime-to-ell-vanishing} gives \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x,V\otimes\xi) \simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x^{\mathrm t},V^{P_x}\otimes\xi). \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: HS and Lemma B.1 reduce to tame inertia

nodes.name: Remove J_x
nodes.statement: Recall from \S\ref{sec:tame-kummer} the decomposition \(I_x^{\mathrm t}=J_x\times\Gamma_x\) with \(\tau_x=(\tau_{x,J},\gamma_x)\). Put \(V_0=(V^{P_x}\otimes\xi)^{J_x}\). Hochschild--Serre and Lemma~\ref{lem:prime-to-ell-vanishing}, now applied to \(1\to J_x\to I_x^{\mathrm t}\to\Gamma_x\to1\), give \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(I_x^{\mathrm t},V^{P_x}\otimes\xi) \simeq R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma_x,V_0). \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: HS and Lemma B.1 reduce to Gamma_x

nodes.name: Fixed vector
nodes.statement: The complex on the right is nonzero. By Lemma~\ref{lem:zell-cohomology}, the endomorphism \(\gamma_x-1\) of the finite-dimensional vector space \(V_0\) is not invertible. Hence there is a nonzero \(u\in V_0\) fixed by \(\gamma_x\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Lemma B.2 gives a gamma_x-fixed vector

nodes.name: Eigenvalue equation
nodes.statement: Since \(u\) is also fixed by \(J_x\), it is fixed by \(\tau_x\) on \(V^{P_x}\otimes\xi\). Write \(u=v\otimes1\), with \(0\neq v\in V^{P_x}\). Since \(\xi\) factors through \(I_x^{\mathrm t}\), the fixed-vector equation for the chosen lift is \(\xi(\tau_x)\widetilde\tau_x v=v\), and hence \[ \widetilde\tau_x v=\xi(\tau_x)^{-1}v. \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Fixed vector gives eigenvalue xi(tau)^{-1}

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus \(v\) is the required eigenvector. Since \(P_x\) fixes \(v\), every lift of \(\tau_x\) acts on \(v\) in the same way.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: v is the eigenvector for every lift

nodes.name: Relative direct images B_{!,lambda} and B_{*,lambda}
nodes.statement: Let \(p:\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\to S\) and \(q:\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\to\mathbb{G}_m\) be the projections. For \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_{m,S},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) and a Kummer character \(\lambda\), define \[ B_{!,\lambda}=Rp_!(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda), \qquad B_{*,\lambda}=Rp_*(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda). \] For \(S=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\) these are \(B_{!,\lambda}=R\Gamma_c(\mathbb{G}_m,A_\lambda)\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}=R\Gamma(\mathbb{G}_m,A_\lambda)\). The transformation \eqref{eq:forget-supports} for \(p\) supplies the canonical morphism \(\varphi_p(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda)\colon B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Exceptional set E_{G_m}(A)
nodes.statement: The exceptional set of the relative Mellin transform is \begin{equation} E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A):= \{\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\ B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda} \text{ is \emph{not} an isomorphism}\} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
also_stated_at: Call \(\lambda\) \emph{exceptional} for \(A\) if the forget-supports morphism \(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) is not an isomorphism, and let \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m}\) be the set of exceptional \(\lambda\).

nodes.name: Exceptional set of the relative Mellin transform
nodes.statement: E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A):= \{\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\ B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda} \text{ is \emph{not} an isomorphism}\}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:relative-exceptional-set

nodes.name: Exceptional Kummer character
nodes.statement: A Kummer character \(\lambda\) is \emph{exceptional} for \(A\) if \(\lambda\in E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\), and \emph{non-exceptional} otherwise.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Common value B_lambda
nodes.statement: For non-exceptional \(\lambda\), write \(B_\lambda\) for the common value of the canonically isomorphic complexes \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Perverse amplitude of relative direct images
nodes.statement: If \(F\) is a perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\), then \[ Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{[0,1]}(S), \qquad Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{[-1,0]}(S). \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: lem:relative-amplitude

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.3
nodes.statement: The morphism \(p\) is affine, so Artin affine vanishing \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4} gives \(Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(S)\) and \(Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{\le0}(S)\). The fibres of \(p\) are of dimension one, so the relative-dimension estimate \cite[4.2.4]{BBDG18} gives \(Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{\le1}(S)\) and \(Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{\ge-1}(S)\). Combining the two pairs of bounds gives the claim.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Artin affine vanishing plus the relative-dimension estimate.

nodes.name: Artin vanishing
nodes.statement: The morphism \(p\) is affine, so Artin affine vanishing \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4} gives \(Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(S)\) and \(Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{\le0}(S)\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Artin vanishing gives one-sided bounds

nodes.name: Relative dimension
nodes.statement: The fibres of \(p\) are of dimension one, so the relative-dimension estimate \cite[4.2.4]{BBDG18} gives \(Rp_!F\in{}^pD^{\le1}(S)\) and \(Rp_*F\in{}^pD^{\ge-1}(S)\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Relative-dimension estimate gives the other bounds

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining the two pairs of bounds gives the claim.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: Combine both pairs

nodes.name: Projection bar p and open immersion j
nodes.statement: Let \(\bar p:\mathbb{P}^1_S\to S\) be the projection and \(j:\mathbb{G}_{m,S}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_S\) the open immersion.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Boundary inclusion i_x
nodes.statement: For \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), let \(i_x:S\simeq\{x\}\times S\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1_S\) be the boundary inclusion.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Twist A_lambda
nodes.statement: For a Kummer character \(\lambda\), put \(A_\lambda=A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Boundary description of the cone of B_! -> B_*
nodes.statement: Since \(\bar p\) is proper, \[ B_{!,\lambda}=R\bar p_*j_!A_\lambda, \qquad B_{*,\lambda}=R\bar p_*Rj_*A_\lambda , \] and, by Lemma~\ref{lem:forget-supports}(1), the forget-supports morphism \(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) is \(R\bar p_*\) applied to \(j_!A_\lambda\to Rj_*A_\lambda\). The localization triangle for the open immersion \(j\) is \[ j_!A_\lambda\longrightarrow Rj_*A_\lambda \longrightarrow i_{0,*}i_0^*Rj_*A_\lambda\oplus i_{\infty,*}i_\infty^*Rj_*A_\lambda \xrightarrow{+1}. \] Applying \(R\bar p_*\), and using \(\bar p\circ i_x=\operatorname{id}_S\), gives a canonical isomorphism in \(D^b_c(S)\) \begin{equation} \operatorname{Cone}(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}) \simeq i_0^*Rj_*A_\lambda\oplus i_\infty^*Rj_*A_\lambda . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: The localization triangle identifies the cone of B_{!,lambda} -> B_{*,lambda} with the boundary restrictions of Rj_*A_lambda at 0 and infinity.

nodes.name: Cone as boundary contributions
nodes.statement: \operatorname{Cone}(B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}) \simeq i_0^*Rj_*A_\lambda\oplus i_\infty^*Rj_*A_\lambda .
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:relative-boundary-cone

nodes.name: Boundary exceptional sets E_x(A)
nodes.statement: For \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), set \begin{equation} E_x(A):= \{\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):i_x^*Rj_*A_\lambda\neq0\}. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Boundary exceptional sets
nodes.statement: E_x(A):= \{\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):i_x^*Rj_*A_\lambda\neq0\}.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.label: eq:boundary-exceptional-set

nodes.name: E_{G_m}(A) is the union of the boundary sets
nodes.statement: Equations \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}, \eqref{eq:relative-boundary-cone}, and \eqref{eq:boundary-exceptional-set} give \[ E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)=E_0(A)\cup E_\infty(A). \]
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Uniform bound for the exceptional set
nodes.statement: Let \(v:S\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{N_S}\) be the fixed embedding \eqref{eq:relative-base-embedding}, let \(D(S,v)\) be defined by \eqref{eq:relative-geometric-complexity}, and retain the functions \(H_N\) of Lemma~\ref{lem:lissity-complexity}. For every \(N,D\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), there is a nondecreasing function \(F_{N,D}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that, if \(N_S=N\) and \(D(S,v)\le D\), then \[ \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\le F_{N,D}(c_{w_v}(A)) \qquad(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_{m,S},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})). \] Choosing \(g_{N,D}\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:coordinate-nearby-complexity}, one may take \[ F_{N,D}(t)=2H_N(g_{N,D}t)^2. \] The function \(F_{N,D}\) is independent of \(\bar k\) and of \(\ell\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base
nodes.statement_short: The number of exceptional Kummer characters is bounded by 2 H_N(g_{N,D} c_{w_v}(A))^2, uniformly in the field and l.

For each \(x\in\{0,\infty\}\), choose a lift \(\widetilde	au_x\in I_x\) of \(	au_x\). The \(I_x\)-action on \(R\Psi_x A\) makes \(\widetilde	au_x\) an automorphism of this complex. nodes.name: Dimension-one bound for Delta
nodes.statement: There is a nondecreasing function \(\Phi^\Delta_{1}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) such that, for every \(c\ge0\) and every \(B\in D^b_c((\mathbb{G}_m)_{\bar k},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) with \(c_u(B)\le c\), the set \(\Delta(B)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) is finite and \[ \#\Delta(B)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\le\Phi^\Delta_{1}(c). \] The function is independent of \(\bar k\) and of \(\ell\).
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.5
nodes.statement: Take \(S=\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\), with its standard embedding. The constituents of the parameter \(D(S,v)\) of \eqref{eq:relative-geometric-complexity} are standard embeddings and morphisms of \S\ref{sec:embeddings} in dimension at most one, so Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity} gives \(D(S,v)\le D_1^{\mathrm{std}}\). Then \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(B)=\Delta(B)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) by \ref{item:GL2}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:exceptional} gives the bound with \(\Phi^\Delta_{1}=F_{0,D_1^{\mathrm{std}}}\).

nodes.name: Base a point

nodes.name: Comparison with Katz's one-dimensional bound
nodes.statement: For perverse \(B\), this is the characteristic-uniform form of Katz's one-dimensional exceptional-character bound \cite[Ch.~1]{Katz2012}.
nodes.section: 3 The relative Mellin transform over a base

nodes.name: Relative embedding over G_m^{d-1} is u_d
nodes.statement: For \(d\ge2\), we take the base \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\), endowed with the embedding \(u_{d-1}\) of \S\ref{sec:embeddings}, and write \(\mathbb{G}_m^d=\mathbb{G}_m\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}=\mathbb{G}_{m,\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}\). The resulting embedding using the recipe in \S\ref{sec:relative-mellin} is \[ w_{u_{d-1}}:\mathbb{G}_m^d\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^{2^{d-1}-1} \hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^{2^d-1}. \] By the compatibility of the embeddings fixed in \S\ref{sec:embeddings}, this is \(u_d\). Consequently, \(c_{w_{u_{d-1}}}(A)=c_{u_d}(A)=c_u(A)\) for every \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\).

nodes.name: Coordinate projections p and q
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} p:\mathbb{G}_m^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},\qquad q:\mathbb{G}_m^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m \end{equation} be the projections to the last \(d-1\) factors and to the first factor, respectively. Under the identification \(\mathbb{G}_m^d=\mathbb{G}_{m,\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}\), these are the structural projections of \S\ref{sec:relative-mellin}. For \(A\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) and a Kummer character \(\lambda\), the complexes \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\), the exceptional set \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) of \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}, and, for non-exceptional \(\lambda\), the common value \(B_\lambda\) are taken with respect to this base.

nodes.name: Coordinate projections
nodes.statement: p:\mathbb{G}_m^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},\qquad q:\mathbb{G}_m^d\longrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m
nodes.label: eq:coordinate-projections

nodes.name: Complexity bounds F_d
nodes.statement: For every \(d\ge1\), there is a nondecreasing function \(F_{d}:\mathbb R_{\ge0}\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\), independent of the algebraically closed base field and of \(\ell\), with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] for \(M\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), with \(\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1\) the stalks at the identity, \[ \sum_ic_u({}^pH^i(M))\le F_{d}(c_u(M)),\qquad \sum_i\dim\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1\le F_{d}(c_u(M)). \] \item[(ii)] for semisimple \(M\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), \[ c_u(M\oplus M^\vee)\le F_{d}(c_u(M)). \] \item[(iii)] if \(d\ge2\), then for every perverse sheaf \(A\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and every Kummer character \(\lambda\) of the first factor, using the notation in (\ref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}) \[ \begin{gathered} \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\le F_{d}(c_u(A)),\\ c_u(B_{!,\lambda}),\ c_u(B_{*,\lambda}),\ c_u({}^pH^r(B_{!,\lambda})),\ c_u({}^pH^r(B_{*,\lambda})) \le F_{d}(c_u(A)) \qquad(r\in\mathbb Z). \end{gathered} \] \end{enumerate}
assumptions: if \(d\ge2\), then for every perverse sheaf \(A\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and every Kummer character \(\lambda\) of the first factor
if \(d\ge2\), then for every perverse sheaf \(A\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and every Kummer character \(\lambda\) of the first factor

nodes.statement_short: One nondecreasing F_d bounds perverse cohomology, identity stalks, M plus its dual, the exceptional set and the relative direct images.
nodes.label: lem:complexity-bounds

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: For (i), let \((A_{i,j})_{1\le j\le n_i}\) be the Jordan--H\"older factors of \({}^pH^i(M)\), repeated with multiplicity. The Jordan--H\"older estimate \ref{item:C6} gives \[ \sum_i\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}c_u(A_{i,j}) \ll_d c(u_d)c_u(M). \] For each \(i\), repeated application of the triangle inequality \ref{item:C4} to a Jordan--H\"older filtration gives \[ c_u({}^pH^i(M))\le\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}c_u(A_{i,j}). \] Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity} bounds \(c(u_d)\) solely in terms of \(d\), uniformly in the algebraically closed field and in \(\ell\). Summing the last inequality over \(i\) proves the first bound in (i). Let \(i_1:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^d\) be the identity section. Since the complexity of a complex on the point is the sum of the dimensions of its cohomology groups \ref{item:C1}, one has \[ c(i_1^*M)=\sum_i\dim\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1. \] The pullback estimate \ref{item:C3}, together with the uniform bound for the embedded morphism \(i_1\) in Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, proves the second bound in (i). For (ii), the duality and pullback estimates \ref{item:C3} bound \(c_u(M^\vee)\) in terms of \(c_u(M)\), since \(M^\vee=\operatorname{inv}^*D(M)\). The direct-sum identity \ref{item:C4} then bounds \(c_u(M\oplus M^\vee)\). For (iii), Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer-complexity} and the pullback estimate give a bound for \(c_u(q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda)\) independent of \(\lambda\). The tensor and pushforward estimates \ref{item:C3} then bound \[ B_{!,\lambda}=Rp_!(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda),\qquad B_{*,\lambda}=Rp_*(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda) \] and \ref{item:C4} and \ref{item:C6} bound their perverse cohomology sheaves, uniformly in \(\lambda\). Lemma~\ref{lem:exceptional}, with \((N,D)=(2^{d-1}-1,D_d^{\mathrm{std}})\), bounds \(\#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\). Take the pointwise maximum of these finitely many nondecreasing functions. Every input complexity has now been bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, so \(F_{d}\) is independent of the field, of \(\ell\), and of \(\lambda\).
nodes.statement_short: Each part from the complexity calculus C3-C6, Lemma 2.2, Lemma 2.7 and Lemma 3.4; take the maximum.

nodes.name: Part (i), perverse cohomology
nodes.statement: For (i), let \((A_{i,j})_{1\le j\le n_i}\) be the Jordan--H\"older factors of \({}^pH^i(M)\), repeated with multiplicity. The Jordan--H\"older estimate \ref{item:C6} gives \[ \sum_i\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}c_u(A_{i,j}) \ll_d c(u_d)c_u(M). \] For each \(i\), repeated application of the triangle inequality \ref{item:C4} to a Jordan--H\"older filtration gives \[ c_u({}^pH^i(M))\le\sum_{j=1}^{n_i}c_u(A_{i,j}). \] Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity} bounds \(c(u_d)\) solely in terms of \(d\), uniformly in the algebraically closed field and in \(\ell\). Summing the last inequality over \(i\) proves the first bound in (i).
nodes.statement_short: Jordan-Holder and triangle estimates

nodes.name: Part (i), identity stalks
nodes.statement: Let \(i_1:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^d\) be the identity section. Since the complexity of a complex on the point is the sum of the dimensions of its cohomology groups \ref{item:C1}, one has \[ c(i_1^*M)=\sum_i\dim\mathcal{H}^i(M)_1. \] The pullback estimate \ref{item:C3}, together with the uniform bound for the embedded morphism \(i_1\) in Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, proves the second bound in (i).
nodes.statement_short: Pullback to the identity section

nodes.name: Part (ii)
nodes.statement: For (ii), the duality and pullback estimates \ref{item:C3} bound \(c_u(M^\vee)\) in terms of \(c_u(M)\), since \(M^\vee=\operatorname{inv}^*D(M)\). The direct-sum identity \ref{item:C4} then bounds \(c_u(M\oplus M^\vee)\).
nodes.statement_short: Duality, pullback and direct sums

nodes.name: Part (iii)
nodes.statement: For (iii), Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer-complexity} and the pullback estimate give a bound for \(c_u(q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda)\) independent of \(\lambda\). The tensor and pushforward estimates \ref{item:C3} then bound \[ B_{!,\lambda}=Rp_!(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda),\qquad B_{*,\lambda}=Rp_*(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda) \] and \ref{item:C4} and \ref{item:C6} bound their perverse cohomology sheaves, uniformly in \(\lambda\). Lemma~\ref{lem:exceptional}, with \((N,D)=(2^{d-1}-1,D_d^{\mathrm{std}})\), bounds \(\#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\). Take the pointwise maximum of these finitely many nondecreasing functions. Every input complexity has now been bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-geometric-complexity}, so \(F_{d}\) is independent of the field, of \(\ell\), and of \(\lambda\).
nodes.statement_short: Kummer complexity, six operations and Lemma 3.4

nodes.name: Fixed function F_d
nodes.statement: For each \(d\), fix a function \(F_d\) as in Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}.

nodes.name: Non-exceptional fibres
nodes.statement: Let \(d\ge2\) and let \(A\) be perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\). With the notation of \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}, suppose that \(\lambda\notin E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) and write \(B_\lambda\) for the common value of the canonically isomorphic complexes \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\). Then \(B_\lambda\) is perverse and \[ c_u(B_\lambda)\le F_{d}(c_u(A)). \] One has the following equality of subsets of \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\): \[ \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):(\lambda,\eta)\in\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\} =\Delta(B_\lambda)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}). \]
nodes.label: lem:fibre

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement: Put \(K_\lambda=A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\). The sheaf \(q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is lisse of rank one, so \(K_\lambda\) is perverse. Since \(p\) is affine, Artin affine vanishing gives \[ B_{!,\lambda}=Rp_!K_\lambda\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}), \qquad B_{*,\lambda}=Rp_*K_\lambda\in{}^pD^{\le0}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}) \] \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4}. By the definition of \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) in \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}, the morphism \(\varphi_p(K_\lambda)\colon B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) is an isomorphism. Hence their common value \(B_\lambda\) belongs to the heart of the perverse \(t\)-structure. Its complexity bound follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii). Let \(f\colon\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\) be the structure morphism. Apply \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse} with \(K=K_\lambda\) and \(\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_\eta\). Identifying \(Rp_!K_\lambda\) and \(Rp_*K_\lambda\) with \(B_\lambda\) by \(\varphi_p(K_\lambda)\) gives the commutative square \[ \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}\bigr) \arrow[r,"\varphi_{A,(\lambda,\eta)}"] \arrow[d,"\beta_!"',"\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"] & R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}\bigr) \arrow[d,"\beta_*","\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"'] \\ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_\lambda)_\eta\bigr) \arrow[r,"\varphi_{B_\lambda,\eta}"'] & R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_\lambda)_\eta\bigr). \end{tikzcd} \] Here \(\beta_!\) and \(\beta_*\) are the composition and projection-formula isomorphisms in \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse}. Hence the upper horizontal morphism is an isomorphism if and only if the lower horizontal morphism is an isomorphism. The equality follows from \ref{item:GL2}.
nodes.statement_short: Artin vanishing places B_lambda in the heart; diagram (4) transfers forget-supports from G_m^d to G_m^{d-1}.

nodes.name: Perversity
nodes.statement: Put \(K_\lambda=A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\). The sheaf \(q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is lisse of rank one, so \(K_\lambda\) is perverse. Since \(p\) is affine, Artin affine vanishing gives \[ B_{!,\lambda}=Rp_!K_\lambda\in{}^pD^{\ge0}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}), \qquad B_{*,\lambda}=Rp_*K_\lambda\in{}^pD^{\le0}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}) \] \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4}. By the definition of \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) in \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}, the morphism \(\varphi_p(K_\lambda)\colon B_{!,\lambda}\to B_{*,\lambda}\) is an isomorphism. Hence their common value \(B_\lambda\) belongs to the heart of the perverse \(t\)-structure. Its complexity bound follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii).
nodes.statement_short: Artin vanishing puts B_lambda in the heart

nodes.name: Compare forget-supports
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\) be the structure morphism. Apply \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse} with \(K=K_\lambda\) and \(\mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_\eta\). Identifying \(Rp_!K_\lambda\) and \(Rp_*K_\lambda\) with \(B_\lambda\) by \(\varphi_p(K_\lambda)\) gives the commutative square \[ \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}\bigr) \arrow[r,"\varphi_{A,(\lambda,\eta)}"] \arrow[d,"\beta_!"',"\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"] & R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}\bigr) \arrow[d,"\beta_*","\rotatebox{90}{\(\sim\)}"'] \\ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_\lambda)_\eta\bigr) \arrow[r,"\varphi_{B_\lambda,\eta}"'] & R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_\lambda)_\eta\bigr). \end{tikzcd} \] Here \(\beta_!\) and \(\beta_*\) are the composition and projection-formula isomorphisms in \eqref{eq:forget-supports-composition-lisse}. Hence the upper horizontal morphism is an isomorphism if and only if the lower horizontal morphism is an isomorphism. The equality follows from \ref{item:GL2}.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram (4) and GL2 give the equality

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: \emph{Perverse sheaves.} We construct nondecreasing functions \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) satisfying the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves. For \(d=1\), take \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{1}=\Phi^\Delta_{1}\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}. Assume \(d\ge2\) and the perverse case known for \(d-1\). Let \(A\) be perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and put \(c=c_u(A)\). For each \(\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}\setminus E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)(k_n)\), Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre} and the inductive hypothesis give \[ \begin{aligned} \#\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}:(\lambda,\eta)\in\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\} &=|\Delta(B_\lambda)(k_n)|\\ &\le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}(c_u(B_\lambda))\,q^{n(d-2)}\\ &\le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1} \bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr)q^{n(d-2)}. \end{aligned} \] There are at most \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}|\le q^n\) such \(\lambda\). For the exceptional characters, the bounds \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}|\le q^{n(d-1)}\) and Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii) imply that \[ \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)(k_n)\,|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}| \le F_{d}(c)q^{n(d-1)}. \] Consequently \[ |\Delta(A)(k_n)| \le \Bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr) +F_{d}(c)\Bigr)q^{n(d-1)}. \] Define \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) to be the function in parentheses. Since \(F_{d}\) and \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\) are nondecreasing, so is \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\). This proves the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves. \emph{Arbitrary complexes.} The case \(d=1\) is Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}. Assume \(d\ge2\) and let \(M\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Induction on the perverse amplitude, using the octahedral axiom, gives a filtration of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\mathscr M_!(M)\to\mathscr M_*(M))\) whose graded pieces are \[ \operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\mathscr M_!({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\to\mathscr M_*({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\bigr)[-i],\qquad i\in\mathbb Z . \] The support of an iterated extension is contained in the union of the supports of its graded pieces, and a shift preserves support, so \ref{item:GL2} gives \[ \Delta(M)\subseteq\bigcup_{i}\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M)). \] The perverse case gives \[ |\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M))(k_n)| \le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}(c_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M)))\,q^{n(d-1)} . \] Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(i) gives \[ \sum_ic_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\le F_{d}(c_u(M)). \] Since a nonzero object has complexity at least \(1\) \ref{item:C2}, the \({}^{p}H^{i}(M)\) are nonzero for at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\) values of \(i\), and each has complexity at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\). We may therefore take \[ \Phi^\Delta_{d}(C) =F_{d}(C)\, \Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\bigl(F_{d}(C)\bigr). \] This function is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on d for perverse sheaves, splitting characters into non-exceptional (Lemma 4.2) and exceptional (Lemma 4.1(iii)); then arbitrary complexes via perverse cohomology.

nodes.name: Perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: \emph{Perverse sheaves.} We construct nondecreasing functions \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) satisfying the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves. For \(d=1\), take \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{1}=\Phi^\Delta_{1}\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}. Assume \(d\ge2\) and the perverse case known for \(d-1\). Let \(A\) be perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and put \(c=c_u(A)\). For the exceptional characters, the bounds \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}|\le q^{n(d-1)}\) and Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii) imply that \[ \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)(k_n)\,|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}| \le F_{d}(c)q^{n(d-1)}. \] Consequently \[ |\Delta(A)(k_n)| \le \Bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr) +F_{d}(c)\Bigr)q^{n(d-1)}. \] Define \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) to be the function in parentheses. Since \(F_{d}\) and \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\) are nondecreasing, so is \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\). This proves the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on d for perverse sheaves

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement: \emph{Perverse sheaves.} We construct nondecreasing functions \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) satisfying the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves. For \(d=1\), take \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{1}=\Phi^\Delta_{1}\) from Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}.
nodes.statement_short: d=1 from Corollary 3.5

nodes.name: Non-exceptional characters
nodes.statement: Assume \(d\ge2\) and the perverse case known for \(d-1\). Let \(A\) be perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and put \(c=c_u(A)\). For each \(\lambda\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}\setminus E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)(k_n)\), Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre} and the inductive hypothesis give \[ \begin{aligned} \#\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}:(\lambda,\eta)\in\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\} &=|\Delta(B_\lambda)(k_n)|\\ &\le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}(c_u(B_\lambda))\,q^{n(d-2)}\\ &\le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1} \bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr)q^{n(d-2)}. \end{aligned} \] There are at most \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}|\le q^n\) such \(\lambda\).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.2 and induction bound each fibre

nodes.name: Exceptional characters
nodes.statement: For the exceptional characters, the bounds \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}|\le q^{n(d-1)}\) and Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii) imply that \[ \#E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)(k_n)\,|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}| \le F_{d}(c)q^{n(d-1)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Trivial bound by Lemma 4.1(iii)

nodes.name: Define Phi^p_d
nodes.statement: Consequently \[ |\Delta(A)(k_n)| \le \Bigl(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr) +F_{d}(c)\Bigr)q^{n(d-1)}. \] Define \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\) to be the function in parentheses. Since \(F_{d}\) and \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d-1}\) are nondecreasing, so is \(\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\). This proves the asserted estimate for perverse sheaves.
