nodes.name: Arbitrary complexes
nodes.statement: \emph{Arbitrary complexes.} The case \(d=1\) is Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}. Assume \(d\ge2\) and let \(M\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Induction on the perverse amplitude, using the octahedral axiom, gives a filtration of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\mathscr M_!(M)\to\mathscr M_*(M))\) whose graded pieces are \[ \operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\mathscr M_!({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\to\mathscr M_*({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\bigr)[-i],\qquad i\in\mathbb Z . \] The support of an iterated extension is contained in the union of the supports of its graded pieces, and a shift preserves support, so \ref{item:GL2} gives \[ \Delta(M)\subseteq\bigcup_{i}\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M)). \] The perverse case gives \[ |\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M))(k_n)| \le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}(c_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M)))\,q^{n(d-1)} . \] Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(i) gives \[ \sum_ic_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\le F_{d}(c_u(M)). \] Since a nonzero object has complexity at least \(1\) \ref{item:C2}, the \({}^{p}H^{i}(M)\) are nonzero for at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\) values of \(i\), and each has complexity at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\). We may therefore take \[ \Phi^\Delta_{d}(C) =F_{d}(C)\, \Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\bigl(F_{d}(C)\bigr). \] This function is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to perverse cohomology sheaves

nodes.name: Case d=1
nodes.statement: \emph{Arbitrary complexes.} The case \(d=1\) is Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one}.
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 3.5

nodes.name: Filtration of the cone
nodes.statement: Assume \(d\ge2\) and let \(M\in D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Induction on the perverse amplitude, using the octahedral axiom, gives a filtration of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\mathscr M_!(M)\to\mathscr M_*(M))\) whose graded pieces are \[ \operatorname{Cone}\bigl(\mathscr M_!({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\to\mathscr M_*({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\bigr)[-i],\qquad i\in\mathbb Z . \] The support of an iterated extension is contained in the union of the supports of its graded pieces, and a shift preserves support, so \ref{item:GL2} gives \[ \Delta(M)\subseteq\bigcup_{i}\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M)). \]
nodes.statement_short: Delta(M) inside union of Delta(pH^i M)

nodes.name: Bound the pieces
nodes.statement: The perverse case gives \[ |\Delta({}^{p}H^{i}(M))(k_n)| \le\Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}(c_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M)))\,q^{n(d-1)} . \] Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(i) gives \[ \sum_ic_u({}^{p}H^{i}(M))\le F_{d}(c_u(M)). \] Since a nonzero object has complexity at least \(1\) \ref{item:C2}, the \({}^{p}H^{i}(M)\) are nonzero for at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\) values of \(i\), and each has complexity at most \(F_{d}(c_u(M))\).
nodes.statement_short: Perverse case and Lemma 4.1(i)

nodes.name: Define Phi^Delta_d
nodes.statement: We may therefore take \[ \Phi^\Delta_{d}(C) =F_{d}(C)\, \Phi^{\mathrm p}_{d}\bigl(F_{d}(C)\bigr). \] This function is nondecreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Take Phi_d = F_d Phi^p_d(F_d)

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.2
nodes.statement:
We use the notation of \eqref{eq:cohomology-jump-loci}. We argue by induction on \(d\). For \(i=0\), \(|\mathcal V_{d,0}(A)(k_n)|\le|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}|\le q^{nd}\), so we may assume \(1\le i\le d\). We use repeatedly that, for every \(d'\ge1\), a perverse sheaf \(P\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'}\), and a Kummer character \(\eta\), Artin affine vanishing and its Verdier dual give \(\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(a<0\) and \(\mathrm{H}^a(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(a>0\) \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4}. The cohomological amplitude of a perverse sheaf on a \(d'\)-dimensional variety gives \(\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=\mathrm{H}^a(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(|a|>d'\). \emph{Base case \(d=1\).} For \(i=1\), \(\mathcal V_{1,1}(A)\subseteq\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) by Artin vanishing on \(\mathbb{G}_m\), so Corollary~ef{cor:d-one} gives \(|\mathcal V_{1,1}(A)(k_n)|\le\Phi^\Delta_{1}(c_u(A))\). Together with the constant \(1\) covering the case \(i=0\), we may take \(\Psi_{1}=\Phi^\Delta_{1}+1\). \emph{Inductive step.} Let \(d\ge2\), assume the theorem for \(d-1\), and use the projections \(p\) and \(q\) of \eqref{eq:coordinate-projections}. For a Kummer character \(\lambda\), the complex \(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is a perverse sheaf, and \(B_{!,\lambda}\), \(B_{*,\lambda}\), \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) are as in \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}. Put \(c=c_u(A)\) and \(E=E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\). Lemma~ef{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii) gives \(\#E\le F_{d}(c)\). The projection formula and Lemmas~ef{lem:forget-supports}(2) and~ef{lem:forget-supports-products}(2) give, for all Kummer characters \(\lambda,\eta\) and every \(j\), \[ \mathrm{H}^j_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}) \simeq\mathrm{H}^j_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},B_{!,\lambda}\otimes\mathcal{L}_\eta), \qquad \mathrm{H}^j(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}) \simeq\mathrm{H}^j(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},B_{*,\lambda}\otimes\mathcal{L}_\eta). \] \emph{Non-exceptional \(\lambda\).} If \(\lambda
otin E\), then \(B_{!,\lambda}\simeq B_{*,\lambda}=B_\lambda\) is perverse and satisfies \(c_u(B_\lambda)\le F_{d}(c)\) by Lemma~ef{lem:fibre}. The identifications give \[ \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):(\lambda,\eta)\in\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)\} =\mathcal V_{d-1,i}(B_\lambda) \] for \(0\le i\le d-1\). The set on the left is empty for \(i=d\). For \(1\le i\le d-1\), the inductive hypothesis and \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}|\le q^n\) give \[ \Bigl|\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)(k_n)\cap  igl((\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}\setminus E(k_n))	imes\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)} igr)\Bigr| \le \Psi_{d-1} igl(F_{d}(c) igr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] For \(i=d\), the left-hand side is zero. \emph{Exceptional \(\lambda\).} The sheaf \(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is perverse, so Lemma~ef{lem:relative-amplitude} gives \(B_{!,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[0,1]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[-1,0]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\), with \(c_u(B_{!,\lambda}),c_u(B_{*,\lambda})\le F_{d}(c)\) by Lemma~ef{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii). Write \(P^r={}^pH^r(B_{!,\lambda})\) for \(r=0,1\). These sheaves are perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\), with \(c_u(P^r)\le F_{d}(c)\) by the same lemma. For \(\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the perverse spectral sequence \[ E_2^{a,r}=\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^r)_\eta) \Rightarrow\mathrm{H}^{a+r}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta) \] and Artin vanishing for \(P^0\) and \(P^1\) give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a<0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i-1}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^1)_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The first set on the right lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i}(P^0)\), and the second lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i-1}(P^1)\) if \(i>1\). For \(i=1\), the second is contained in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}\). The inductive hypothesis therefore gives \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] For ordinary cohomology, put \(Q^r={}^pH^r(B_{*,\lambda})\) for \(r=-1,0\). These sheaves have complexity at most \(F_{d}(c)\). The analogous spectral sequence and Artin vanishing give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a>0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i+1}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^{-1})_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The same inductive estimates apply to \(Q^0\) and \(Q^{-1}\). Hence \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] Multiplying the sum of the two bounds above for \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) by \(\#E\le F_{d}(c)\), the exceptional contribution is at most \[ 2F_{d}(c) \Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] Combining the non-exceptional and exceptional estimates, we may take \[  egin{aligned} \Psi_{d}(c) ={}&1+\Psi_{d-1} igl(F_{d}(c) igr)\ &+2F_{d}(c) \Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1} igl(F_{d}(c) igr)+1\Bigr). \end{aligned} \] The term \(1\) gives the estimate for \(i=0\). Since \(F_{d}\) and \(\Psi_{d-1}\) are nondecreasing, so is \(\Psi_{d}\). This completes the induction.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on d through the first-coordinate projection: non-exceptional fibres reduce to dimension d-1 (Lemma 4.2); exceptional fibres use perverse amplitude (Lemma 3.3) and the perverse spectral sequence, shifting degree i to i-1.

nodes.name: Notation
nodes.statement: We use the notation of \eqref{eq:cohomology-jump-loci}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the cohomology-jump loci

nodes.name: Induction and vanishing facts
nodes.statement: We argue by induction on \(d\). For \(i=0\), \(|\mathcal V_{d,0}(A)(k_n)|\le|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k_n)}|\le q^{nd}\), so we may assume \(1\le i\le d\). We use repeatedly that, for every \(d'\ge1\), a perverse sheaf \(P\) on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'}\), and a Kummer character \(\eta\), Artin affine vanishing and its Verdier dual give \(\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(a<0\) and \(\mathrm{H}^a(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(a>0\) \cite[Th.~4.1.1, Cor.~4.1.2]{BBDG18}, \cite[Exp.~XIV, 3.1]{SGA4}. The cohomological amplitude of a perverse sheaf on a \(d'\)-dimensional variety gives \(\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=\mathrm{H}^a(\mathbb{G}_m^{d'},P_\eta)=0\) for \(|a|>d'\).
nodes.statement_short: Induct on d; dispose of i=0; recall Artin vanishing

nodes.name: Base case d=1
nodes.statement: \emph{Base case \(d=1\).} For \(i=1\), \(\mathcal V_{1,1}(A)\subseteq\Delta(A)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\) by Artin vanishing on \(\mathbb{G}_m\), so Corollary~\ref{cor:d-one} gives \(|\mathcal V_{1,1}(A)(k_n)|\le\Phi^\Delta_{1}(c_u(A))\). Together with the constant \(1\) covering the case \(i=0\), we may take \(\Psi_{1}=\Phi^\Delta_{1}+1\).
nodes.statement_short: Corollary 3.5

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement: \emph{Inductive step.} Let \(d\ge2\), assume the theorem for \(d-1\), and use the projections \(p\) and \(q\) of \eqref{eq:coordinate-projections}. For a Kummer character \(\lambda\), the complex \(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is a perverse sheaf, and \(B_{!,\lambda}\), \(B_{*,\lambda}\), \(E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\) are as in \eqref{eq:relative-exceptional-set}. Put \(c=c_u(A)\) and \(E=E_{\mathbb{G}_m}(A)\). Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii) gives \(\#E\le F_{d}(c)\). The projection formula and Lemmas~\ref{lem:forget-supports}(2) and~\ref{lem:forget-supports-products}(2) give, for all Kummer characters \(\lambda,\eta\) and every \(j\), \[ \mathrm{H}^j_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}) \simeq\mathrm{H}^j_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},B_{!,\lambda}\otimes\mathcal{L}_\eta), \qquad \mathrm{H}^j(\mathbb{G}_m^d,A_{(\lambda,\eta)}) \simeq\mathrm{H}^j(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},B_{*,\lambda}\otimes\mathcal{L}_\eta). \]
nodes.statement_short: Projection formula identifies twisted cohomology

nodes.name: Non-exceptional lambda
nodes.statement: \emph{Non-exceptional \(\lambda\).} If \(\lambda\notin E\), then \(B_{!,\lambda}\simeq B_{*,\lambda}=B_\lambda\) is perverse and satisfies \(c_u(B_\lambda)\le F_{d}(c)\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:fibre}. The identifications give \[ \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):(\lambda,\eta)\in\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)\} =\mathcal V_{d-1,i}(B_\lambda) \] for \(0\le i\le d-1\). The set on the left is empty for \(i=d\). For \(1\le i\le d-1\), the inductive hypothesis and \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}|\le q^n\) give \[ \Bigl|\mathcal V_{d,i}(A)(k_n)\cap \bigl((\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m(k_n)}\setminus E(k_n))\times\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}\bigr)\Bigr| \le \Psi_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] For \(i=d\), the left-hand side is zero.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.2 and induction

nodes.name: Exceptional lambda
nodes.statement:
\emph{Exceptional \(\lambda\).} The sheaf \(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is perverse, so Lemma~ef{lem:relative-amplitude} gives \(B_{!,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[0,1]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[-1,0]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\), with \(c_u(B_{!,\lambda}),c_u(B_{*,\lambda})\le F_{d}(c)\) by Lemma~ef{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii). Write \(P^r={}^pH^r(B_{!,\lambda})\) for \(r=0,1\). These sheaves are perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\), with \(c_u(P^r)\le F_{d}(c)\) by the same lemma. For \(\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the perverse spectral sequence \[ E_2^{a,r}=\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^r)_\eta) \Rightarrow\mathrm{H}^{a+r}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta) \] and Artin vanishing for \(P^0\) and \(P^1\) give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a<0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i-1}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^1)_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The first set on the right lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i}(P^0)\), and the second lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i-1}(P^1)\) if \(i>1\). For \(i=1\), the second is contained in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}\). The inductive hypothesis therefore gives \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] For ordinary cohomology, put \(Q^r={}^pH^r(B_{*,\lambda})\) for \(r=-1,0\). These sheaves have complexity at most \(F_{d}(c)\). The analogous spectral sequence and Artin vanishing give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a>0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i+1}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^{-1})_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The same inductive estimates apply to \(Q^0\) and \(Q^{-1}\). Hence \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \] Multiplying the sum of the two bounds above for \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) by \(\#E\le F_{d}(c)\), the exceptional contribution is at most \[ 2F_{d}(c) \Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Perverse spectral sequences for B_! and B_*

nodes.name: Compact supports
nodes.statement:
\emph{Exceptional \(\lambda\).} The sheaf \(A\otimes q^*\mathcal{L}_\lambda\) is perverse, so Lemma~ef{lem:relative-amplitude} gives \(B_{!,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[0,1]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\in{}^pD^{[-1,0]}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1})\), with \(c_u(B_{!,\lambda}),c_u(B_{*,\lambda})\le F_{d}(c)\) by Lemma~ef{lem:complexity-bounds}(iii). Write \(P^r={}^pH^r(B_{!,\lambda})\) for \(r=0,1\). These sheaves are perverse on \(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}\), with \(c_u(P^r)\le F_{d}(c)\) by the same lemma. For \(\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the perverse spectral sequence \[ E_2^{a,r}=\mathrm{H}^a_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^r)_\eta) \Rightarrow\mathrm{H}^{a+r}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta) \] and Artin vanishing for \(P^0\) and \(P^1\) give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a<0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{i-1}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(P^1)_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The first set on the right lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i}(P^0)\), and the second lies in \(\mathcal V_{d-1,i-1}(P^1)\) if \(i>1\). For \(i=1\), the second is contained in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}\). The inductive hypothesis therefore gives \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}_c(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{!,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound jumps of B_{!,lambda} via P^0, P^1

nodes.name: Ordinary cohomology
nodes.statement:
For ordinary cohomology, put \(Q^r={}^pH^r(B_{*,\lambda})\) for \(r=-1,0\). These sheaves have complexity at most \(F_{d}(c)\). The analogous spectral sequence and Artin vanishing give \(\mathrm{H}^{a}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)=0\) for \(a>0\), together with the inclusion \[  egin{aligned} &\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}): \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad\subseteq \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^0)_\eta)
eq0\}\ &\qquad{}\cup \{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}):\mathrm{H}^{-i+1}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(Q^{-1})_\eta)
eq0\}. \end{aligned} \] The same inductive estimates apply to \(Q^0\) and \(Q^{-1}\). Hence \[ \#\Bigl\{\eta\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1}(k_n)}: \substack{\mathrm{H}^i(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0\ \,	ext{or}\ \mathrm{H}^{-i}(\mathbb{G}_m^{d-1},(B_{*,\lambda})_\eta)
eq0}\Bigr\} \le\Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Bound jumps of B_{*,lambda} via Q^0, Q^{-1}

nodes.name: Exceptional total
nodes.statement: Multiplying the sum of the two bounds above for \(B_{!,\lambda}\) and \(B_{*,\lambda}\) by \(\#E\le F_{d}(c)\), the exceptional contribution is at most \[ 2F_{d}(c) \Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}(F_{d}(c))+1\Bigr)q^{n(d-i)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Multiply by #E

nodes.name: Define Psi_d
nodes.statement: Combining the non-exceptional and exceptional estimates, we may take \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi_{d}(c) ={}&1+\Psi_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr)\\ &+2F_{d}(c) \Bigl(2\Psi_{d-1}\bigl(F_{d}(c)\bigr)+1\Bigr). \end{aligned} \] The term \(1\) gives the estimate for \(i=0\). Since \(F_{d}\) and \(\Psi_{d-1}\) are nondecreasing, so is \(\Psi_{d}\). This completes the induction.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to define Psi_d

nodes.name: Comparison with Bonolis-Kowalski-Woo
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} should be compared with the recent uniform variants of the Katz--Laumon and Fouvry--Katz stratification theorems proved by Bonolis, Kowalski, and Woo \cite{BonolisKowalskiWoo2026} for exponential sums in families. Those results concern stratifications of the additive Fourier parameter space. Here the parameter space is the Gabber--Loeser character scheme and the estimate counts its finite-field Kummer characters. The estimate is uniform over perverse sheaves of bounded complexity while the characteristic and \(\ell\) vary. This is the form used in \S\ref{sec:unramified} to prove Corollary~\ref{cor:equidistribution}.

nodes.name: Self-dual object L = M + M^vee
nodes.statement: We use the unramified locus \(X(M_0)\) of \ref{item:T5} in \S\ref{sec:tannakian} and let \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\).

nodes.name: Properties of L
nodes.statement: Then \(L\) is perverse, self-dual, and lies in \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\), with \(c_u(L)\le F_{d}(c_u(M))\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(ii).

nodes.name: Twisted comparison alpha_{m,chi}
nodes.statement: Let \(\alpha_m\) and \(C_m\) be as in \ref{item:T5}. The twist of \(\alpha_m\) by \(\mathcal{L}_\chi\) is denoted \(\alpha_{m,\chi}\).

nodes.name: Weakly unramified implies unramified
nodes.statement: Let \(M_0\in\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{ari}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d/k)\) be arithmetically semisimple, let \(M=M_{0,\bar k}\), and let \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\). Then \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\).
nodes.label: lem:weakly-unramified-inclusion

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement:
With the Mellin transforms of \Sef{sec:mellin}, write \(\gamma_m\colon\mathscr M_!(L^{\ast_!m})	o\mathscr M_*(L^{\ast_*m})\) for the morphism induced by \(\alpha_m\) and the transformation \(\mathscr M_!	o\mathscr M_*\). \emph{Fibres of \(\gamma_m\).} For \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), let \(\Theta_{m,\chi}=Li_\chi^*\gamma_m\), viewed through ef{item:GL1} as \[ R\Gamma_c igl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_!m})_\chi igr) \xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma_c(\alpha_{m,\chi})\ }R\Gamma_c igl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_*m})_\chi igr) \longrightarrow R\Gamma igl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_*m})_\chi igr), \] where the second morphism forgets supports. Put \(\Theta_{1,\chi}=\varphi_{L,\chi}\). Naturality of the K"unneth isomorphisms and Lemma~ef{lem:comparison-monoidal} give \[ \Theta_{m,\chi}=\Theta_{m-1,\chi}\otimes\varphi_{L,\chi}. \] Thus \(\Theta_{m,\chi}=\varphi_{L,\chi}^{\otimes m}\) under the iterated K"unneth identifications. \emph{Support of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\).} The complex \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) is coherent because the Mellin transforms take values in coherent complexes (\Sef{sec:mellin}). Since \(Li_\chi^*\) is triangulated, one has \(Li_\chi^*\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(\Theta_{m,\chi})\). For \(\chi
otin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the morphism \(\varphi_{L,\chi}\), hence \(\Theta_{m,\chi}\), is an isomorphism, so the derived fibre of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) vanishes at every character outside \(\Delta(L)\). Put \(U=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\setminus\Delta(L)\) and \(Q_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)|_U\). By ef{item:GL6}, each connected component of \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The components are open, and both properties are local, so \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is locally noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The open subscheme \(U\) is therefore Jacobson, and its closed points are closed in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), hence are characters outside \(\Delta(L)\) \cite[Tag~005X]{stacks-project}. Let \(\chi\) be a closed point of \(U\), write \(A_\chi=\mathcal O_{U,\chi}\), and let \((Q_m)_\chi\) denote the stalk of \(Q_m\) at \(\chi\), viewed as a complex of \(A_\chi\)-modules. Write \(k(\chi)\) for the residue field of \(A_\chi\). There is a canonical identification \[ Li_\chi^*Q_m\simeq (Q_m)_\chi\otimes^L_{A_\chi}k(\chi). \] The left-hand side vanishes by the two preceding paragraphs. If \((Q_m)_\chi\) were nonzero, there would be a largest integer \(r\) with \(H^r((Q_m)_\chi)
eq0\), because \((Q_m)_\chi\) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology modules over the noetherian local ring \(A_\chi\). In the hyper-Tor spectral sequence \[ E_2^{-a,b}=\mathrm{Tor}^{A_\chi}_a igl(H^b((Q_m)_\chi),k(\chi) igr) \Longrightarrow H^{b-a} igl(Li_\chi^*Q_m igr), \] the only possibly nonzero term in total degree \(r\) is \(H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)\). Nakayama's lemma then gives \(H^r(Li_\chi^*Q_m)\simeq H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)
eq0\), a contradiction. Hence \((Q_m)_\chi=0\) at every closed point \(\chi\) of \(U\). The support of \(Q_m\) is a finite union of supports of coherent cohomology sheaves, hence closed in \(U\). A nonempty closed subset of the Jacobson scheme \(U\) contains a closed point, so \(Q_m=0\). Therefore \[ \operatorname{Supp}\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\subseteq\Delta(L). \] \emph{Localization.} The morphism \(\gamma_m\) is an isomorphism outside \(\Delta(L)\), so ef{item:GL5} applied to \(\alpha_m\) shows that \(\alpha_m\) is an isomorphism in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_{\Delta(L)}\). Equivalently, \(C_m=0\) there, that is, by ef{item:GL4}, \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_!(C_m)\) and \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_*(C_m)\) are contained in \(\Delta(L)\). Since the localization functor is perverse \(t\)-exact, the image of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) in the localized heart is zero. By ef{item:GL4}, both Mellin transforms of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) are therefore supported in \(\Delta(L)\). Fix \(\chi
otin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). The preceding support statement and ef{item:GL1} give \[ R\Gamma_c igl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi igr) =R\Gamma igl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi igr)=0 \qquad(m\ge2,\ j\in\mathbb Z). \] By \eqref{eq:weak-locus}, every \(\chi\in X_w(L)\) lies outside \(\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Since \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), one also has \(X_w(L)\subseteq X_w(M)\). Fix \(\chi\in X_w(L)\). The vanishing above and the definitions of \Sef{sec:negligible} give \(\chi\in\mathcal N({}^pH^jC_m)\) for all \(j\) and hence \(\chi\in\mathcal N(C_m)\) for all \(m\ge2\). Thus \(\chi\in X_w(M)\cap igcap_{m\ge2}\mathcal N(C_m)\), and ef{item:T5} shows that \(\chi\) is unramified for \(M\). Hence \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: Fibres of the Mellin comparison are tensor powers of phi_{L,chi}; Nakayama on the Jacobson character scheme shows the cone is supported in Delta(L), and the localization criterion GL5 then gives unramifiedness via T5.

nodes.name: Define gamma_m
nodes.statement: With the Mellin transforms of \S\ref{sec:mellin}, write \(\gamma_m\colon\mathscr M_!(L^{\ast_!m})\to\mathscr M_*(L^{\ast_*m})\) for the morphism induced by \(\alpha_m\) and the transformation \(\mathscr M_!\to\mathscr M_*\).
nodes.statement_short: Mellin comparison of alpha_m

nodes.name: Fibres of gamma_m
nodes.statement: \emph{Fibres of \(\gamma_m\).} For \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), let \(\Theta_{m,\chi}=Li_\chi^*\gamma_m\), viewed through \ref{item:GL1} as \[ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_!m})_\chi\bigr) \xrightarrow{\ R\Gamma_c(\alpha_{m,\chi})\ }R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_*m})_\chi\bigr) \longrightarrow R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,(L^{\ast_*m})_\chi\bigr), \] where the second morphism forgets supports. Put \(\Theta_{1,\chi}=\varphi_{L,\chi}\). Naturality of the K\"unneth isomorphisms and Lemma~\ref{lem:comparison-monoidal} give \[ \Theta_{m,\chi}=\Theta_{m-1,\chi}\otimes\varphi_{L,\chi}. \] Thus \(\Theta_{m,\chi}=\varphi_{L,\chi}^{\otimes m}\) under the iterated K\"unneth identifications.

nodes.name: Support of the cone
nodes.statement:
\emph{Support of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\).} The complex \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) is coherent because the Mellin transforms take values in coherent complexes (\Sef{sec:mellin}). Since \(Li_\chi^*\) is triangulated, one has \(Li_\chi^*\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(\Theta_{m,\chi})\). For \(\chi
otin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the morphism \(\varphi_{L,\chi}\), hence \(\Theta_{m,\chi}\), is an isomorphism, so the derived fibre of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) vanishes at every character outside \(\Delta(L)\). Put \(U=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\setminus\Delta(L)\) and \(Q_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)|_U\). By ef{item:GL6}, each connected component of \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The components are open, and both properties are local, so \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is locally noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The open subscheme \(U\) is therefore Jacobson, and its closed points are closed in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), hence are characters outside \(\Delta(L)\) \cite[Tag~005X]{stacks-project}. eq0\), because \((Q_m)_\chi\) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology modules over the noetherian local ring \(A_\chi\). In the hyper-Tor spectral sequence \[ E_2^{-a,b}=\mathrm{Tor}^{A_\chi}_a igl(H^b((Q_m)_\chi),k(\chi) igr) \Longrightarrow H^{b-a} igl(Li_\chi^*Q_m igr), \] the only possibly nonzero term in total degree \(r\) is \(H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)\). Nakayama's lemma then gives \(H^r(Li_\chi^*Q_m)\simeq H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)
eq0\), a contradiction. Hence \((Q_m)_\chi=0\) at every closed point \(\chi\) of \(U\). The support of \(Q_m\) is a finite union of supports of coherent cohomology sheaves, hence closed in \(U\). nodes.statement_short: Cone of gamma_m supported in Delta(L)

nodes.name: Fibres vanish
nodes.statement: \emph{Support of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\).} The complex \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) is coherent because the Mellin transforms take values in coherent complexes (\S\ref{sec:mellin}). Since \(Li_\chi^*\) is triangulated, one has \(Li_\chi^*\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(\Theta_{m,\chi})\). For \(\chi\notin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the morphism \(\varphi_{L,\chi}\), hence \(\Theta_{m,\chi}\), is an isomorphism, so the derived fibre of \(\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\) vanishes at every character outside \(\Delta(L)\). Put \(U=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\setminus\Delta(L)\) and \(Q_m=\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)|_U\).
nodes.statement_short: Derived fibres vanish off Delta(L)

nodes.name: Jacobson
nodes.statement: By \ref{item:GL6}, each connected component of \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The components are open, and both properties are local, so \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\) is locally noetherian and Jacobson, and its closed points are its \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-points. The open subscheme \(U\) is therefore Jacobson, and its closed points are closed in \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}\), hence are characters outside \(\Delta(L)\) \cite[Tag~005X]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: U is Jacobson with closed points characters

nodes.name: Nakayama
nodes.statement: Let \(\chi\) be a closed point of \(U\), write \(A_\chi=\mathcal O_{U,\chi}\), and let \((Q_m)_\chi\) denote the stalk of \(Q_m\) at \(\chi\), viewed as a complex of \(A_\chi\)-modules. Write \(k(\chi)\) for the residue field of \(A_\chi\). There is a canonical identification \[ Li_\chi^*Q_m\simeq (Q_m)_\chi\otimes^L_{A_\chi}k(\chi). \] The left-hand side vanishes by the two preceding paragraphs. If \((Q_m)_\chi\) were nonzero, there would be a largest integer \(r\) with \(H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\neq0\), because \((Q_m)_\chi\) is bounded with finitely generated cohomology modules over the noetherian local ring \(A_\chi\). In the hyper-Tor spectral sequence \[ E_2^{-a,b}=\mathrm{Tor}^{A_\chi}_a\bigl(H^b((Q_m)_\chi),k(\chi)\bigr) \Longrightarrow H^{b-a}\bigl(Li_\chi^*Q_m\bigr), \] the only possibly nonzero term in total degree \(r\) is \(H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)\). Nakayama's lemma then gives \(H^r(Li_\chi^*Q_m)\simeq H^r((Q_m)_\chi)\otimes_{A_\chi}k(\chi)\neq0\), a contradiction. Hence \((Q_m)_\chi=0\) at every closed point \(\chi\) of \(U\). The support of \(Q_m\) is a finite union of supports of coherent cohomology sheaves, hence closed in \(U\). A nonempty closed subset of the Jacobson scheme \(U\) contains a closed point, so \(Q_m=0\). Therefore \[ \operatorname{Supp}\operatorname{Cone}(\gamma_m)\subseteq\Delta(L). \]
nodes.statement_short: Nakayama forces the stalks and Q_m to vanish

nodes.name: Localization
nodes.statement: \emph{Localization.} The morphism \(\gamma_m\) is an isomorphism outside \(\Delta(L)\), so \ref{item:GL5} applied to \(\alpha_m\) shows that \(\alpha_m\) is an isomorphism in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_{\Delta(L)}\). Equivalently, \(C_m=0\) there, that is, by \ref{item:GL4}, \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_!(C_m)\) and \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_*(C_m)\) are contained in \(\Delta(L)\). Since the localization functor is perverse \(t\)-exact, the image of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) in the localized heart is zero. By \ref{item:GL4}, both Mellin transforms of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) are therefore supported in \(\Delta(L)\). Fix \(\chi\notin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). The preceding support statement and \ref{item:GL1} give \[ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi\bigr) =R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi\bigr)=0 \qquad(m\ge2,\ j\in\mathbb Z). \] By \eqref{eq:weak-locus}, every \(\chi\in X_w(L)\) lies outside \(\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Since \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), one also has \(X_w(L)\subseteq X_w(M)\). Fix \(\chi\in X_w(L)\). The vanishing above and the definitions of \S\ref{sec:negligible} give \(\chi\in\mathcal N({}^pH^jC_m)\) for all \(j\) and hence \(\chi\in\mathcal N(C_m)\) for all \(m\ge2\). Thus \(\chi\in X_w(M)\cap\bigcap_{m\ge2}\mathcal N(C_m)\), and \ref{item:T5} shows that \(\chi\) is unramified for \(M\). Hence \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: GL5 and T5 give unramifiedness

nodes.name: Apply GL5
nodes.statement: \emph{Localization.} The morphism \(\gamma_m\) is an isomorphism outside \(\Delta(L)\), so \ref{item:GL5} applied to \(\alpha_m\) shows that \(\alpha_m\) is an isomorphism in \(D^b_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d)_{\Delta(L)}\). Equivalently, \(C_m=0\) there, that is, by \ref{item:GL4}, \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_!(C_m)\) and \(\operatorname{Supp}\mathscr M_*(C_m)\) are contained in \(\Delta(L)\). Since the localization functor is perverse \(t\)-exact, the image of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) in the localized heart is zero. By \ref{item:GL4}, both Mellin transforms of \({}^pH^j(C_m)\) are therefore supported in \(\Delta(L)\).
nodes.statement_short: C_m vanishes in the localized category

nodes.name: Cohomology vanishes
nodes.statement: Fix \(\chi\notin\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). The preceding support statement and \ref{item:GL1} give \[ R\Gamma_c\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi\bigr) =R\Gamma\bigl(\mathbb{G}_m^d,({}^pH^jC_m)_\chi\bigr)=0 \qquad(m\ge2,\ j\in\mathbb Z). \]
nodes.statement_short: GL1 gives vanishing cohomology

nodes.name: Unramified
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:weak-locus}, every \(\chi\in X_w(L)\) lies outside \(\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Since \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\), one also has \(X_w(L)\subseteq X_w(M)\). Fix \(\chi\in X_w(L)\). The vanishing above and the definitions of \S\ref{sec:negligible} give \(\chi\in\mathcal N({}^pH^jC_m)\) for all \(j\) and hence \(\chi\in\mathcal N(C_m)\) for all \(m\ge2\). Thus \(\chi\in X_w(M)\cap\bigcap_{m\ge2}\mathcal N(C_m)\), and \ref{item:T5} shows that \(\chi\) is unramified for \(M\). Hence \(X_w(L)\subseteq X(M_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: T5 gives chi unramified

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement: By \eqref{eq:weak-locus} and Lemma~\ref{lem:weakly-unramified-inclusion}, \(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_0)\subseteq\Delta(L)(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), and Theorem~\ref{thm:delta-count} applied to \(L\) gives \[ |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_0))(k_n)| \le|\Delta(L)(k_n)| \le\Phi^\Delta_{d}(c_u(L))\,q^{n(d-1)} \le\Phi^\Delta_{d}\bigl(F_{d}(c_u(M))\bigr)q^{n(d-1)}. \] We may therefore take \[ \Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C) =\Phi^\Delta_{d}\bigl(F_{d}(C)\bigr).\qedhere \]
nodes.statement_short: Complement of X(M_0) lies in Delta(L); apply Theorem 1.1 to L.

nodes.name: Identity stalk of a semisimple perverse sheaf
nodes.statement: For \(x\in\mathbb{G}_m^d\), let \(\delta_x\) denote the skyscraper sheaf at \(x\), and let \(1\in\mathbb{G}_m^d\) be the identity. Let \(P\) be a semisimple perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\), and suppose that \(\delta_1\) is not a direct summand of \(P\). Then \[ \mathcal{H}^j(P)_1=0\qquad(j\ge0). \]
assumptions: \(P\) be a semisimple perverse sheaf on \(\mathbb{G}_m^d\)
\(\delta_1\) is not a direct summand of \(P\)
nodes.label: lem:identity-stalk

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider a simple summand \(Q\) of \(P\). If \(Q\) is punctual, then \(Q\simeq\delta_x\) for some \(x\neq 1\), so its stalk at \(1\) vanishes. Suppose that \(\dim\operatorname{Supp} Q>0\). The perverse support condition gives \(\mathcal{H}^j(Q)=0\) for \(j>0\). If \(\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1\neq0\), the adjunction morphism for the inclusion \(i_1:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and truncation give a nonzero morphism of perverse sheaves \[ Q\longrightarrow i_{1,*}i_1^*Q \longrightarrow i_{1,*}\tau^{\ge0}i_1^*Q =\delta_1\otimes_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1. \] Since \(Q\) is simple, this morphism is a monomorphism. Hence \(\operatorname{Supp} Q\subseteq\{1\}\), a contradiction. Thus \(\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1=0\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a simple summand; punctual case trivial, otherwise a nonzero map to delta_1 contradicts simplicity.

nodes.name: Reduce to simple
nodes.statement: It suffices to consider a simple summand \(Q\) of \(P\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to a simple summand Q

nodes.name: Punctual case
nodes.statement: If \(Q\) is punctual, then \(Q\simeq\delta_x\) for some \(x\neq 1\), so its stalk at \(1\) vanishes.
nodes.statement_short: Q = delta_x with x != 1

nodes.name: Positive-dimensional case
nodes.statement: Suppose that \(\dim\operatorname{Supp} Q>0\). The perverse support condition gives \(\mathcal{H}^j(Q)=0\) for \(j>0\). If \(\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1\neq0\), the adjunction morphism for the inclusion \(i_1:\{1\}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{G}_m^d\) and truncation give a nonzero morphism of perverse sheaves \[ Q\longrightarrow i_{1,*}i_1^*Q \longrightarrow i_{1,*}\tau^{\ge0}i_1^*Q =\delta_1\otimes_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1. \] Since \(Q\) is simple, this morphism is a monomorphism. Hence \(\operatorname{Supp} Q\subseteq\{1\}\), a contradiction. Thus \(\mathcal{H}^0(Q)_1=0\).
nodes.statement_short: Nonzero map to delta_1 contradicts simplicity

nodes.name: Weyl criterion
nodes.statement: Let \(G\) be reductive and let \(K_G\) be a maximal compact subgroup of \(G(\mathbb C)\). Families of conjugacy classes \(\theta_j(x)\in K_G^\sharp\), indexed by finite sets \(X_j\), are \(\mu_G^\sharp\)-equidistributed if and only if \[ \frac{1}{|X_j|}\sum_{x\in X_j}\operatorname{Tr}\rho\bigl(\theta_j(x)\bigr)\longrightarrow0 \] for every nontrivial irreducible algebraic representation \(\rho\) of \(G\).
equivalent_conditions: Families of conjugacy classes \(\theta_j(x)\in K_G^\sharp\), indexed by finite sets \(X_j\), are \(\mu_G^\sharp\)-equidistributed
assumptions: Let \(G\) be reductive and let \(K_G\) be a maximal compact subgroup of \(G(\mathbb C)\).

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 1.4
nodes.statement:
The argument follows the proof of \cite[Th.~4.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Put \(C=\sup_jc_u(M_j)\), and for every \(j\) write \(q_j=\#k_j\). Since \(\#k_j	o\infty\), there is \(j_0\) such that \(X_j

By ef{item:T5}, one has \(	au_i(\chi)=0\) for \(i

eq0\}\). By the definition of complexity ef{item:C1}, the tensor-product estimate ef{item:C3}, and Lemma~ef{lem:kummer-complexity}, there is a constant \(B_ho\), independent of \(j\) and of \(k_j\), such that \[ \dim\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\le c_u(N_\chi)\le B_ho \qquad(i\in\mathbb Z,\ \chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})). \] We use the following three estimates.  egin{enumerate} \item[(a)] \(\mathcal A_i\subseteq\mathcal V_{d,|i|}(N)\), so Theorem~ef{thm:stratified} gives \(|\mathcal A_i|\le\Psi_{d}(C_ho)\,q^{d-|i|}\). \item[(b)] As \(N_0\) is pure of weight zero, \(\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\) has weights \(\le i\) \cite[3.3.1]{Del80}, \cite[5.1.13]{BBDG18}, so \(|	au_i(\chi)|\le B_ho\,q^{i/2}\). \item[(c)] \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X|\le\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)q^{d-1}\) by \eqref{eq:cor-unram}. \end{enumerate} For \(i
eq0\), the function \(	au_i\) is supported on \(\mathcal A_i\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X\). Hence \[  egin{aligned}  rac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in X}	au_0(\chi) =\ & rac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}}\sum_{|i|\le d}(-1)^i	au_i(\chi) - rac{1}{|X|}\sum_{0<|i|\le d}(-1)^i\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal A_i}	au_i(\chi)\ &- rac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X}	au_0(\chi). \end{aligned} \] By the Grothendieck--Lefschetz trace formula \(\sum_{|i|\le d}(-1)^i	au_i(\chi)=\sum_{x\in \mathbb{G}_m^d(k)} t_{N_0}(x;k)\,\chi(x)\), where \(t_{N_0}\) denotes the trace function of the arithmetic object \(N_0\). Summing over \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\) and using \(\sum_\chi\chi(x)=|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}|\) for \(x=1\) and \(\sum_\chi\chi(x)=0\) otherwise, the first term equals \((|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}|/|X|)\,t_{N_0}(1;k)\). Since \(G^{\mathrm{ari}}_M=G^{\mathrm{geo}}_M=G\) and \(ho\) is nontrivial and irreducible, \(\operatorname{Hom}(\delta_1,N)=0\) in \(\langle Mangle\). Both inclusions \(\langle Mangle\subseteq\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\subseteq\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) are full, so \(N\) has no direct summand isomorphic to \(\delta_1\). The trivial representation gives average one, so the Weyl criterion yields the equidistribution of the classes \(\Theta_{M_0,k}(\chi)\), \(\chi\in X(M_0)(k)\), in \(K_G^\sharp\) for the measure \(\mu_G^\sharp\) as \(\#k_j	o\infty\).
nodes.statement_short: Weyl criterion: express the Weyl sum by the trace formula and bound the identity term (Lemma 5.2, weights), the non-zero-degree terms (Theorem 1.2) and the omitted characters (Theorem 1.3). The key step is that the identity stalk of rho(M) has only negative-degree cohomology.

nodes.name: Unramified sets are large
nodes.statement: The argument follows the proof of \cite[Th.~4.19]{ForeyFresanKowalski2021}. Put \(C=\sup_jc_u(M_j)\), and for every \(j\) write \(q_j=\#k_j\). Theorem~\ref{thm:unram-count}, applied to \(M_{j,0}\), gives \begin{equation} |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_{j,0}))(k_j)| \le\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)\,q_j^{d-1}, \end{equation} so \(|X_j|=(q_j-1)^d+O(q_j^{d-1})\), with constants depending only on \(d\) and \(C\). Since \(\#k_j\to\infty\), there is \(j_0\) such that \(X_j\neq\varnothing\) and \(|X_j|\asymp q_j^d\) for every \(j\ge j_0\). The finitely many \(j<j_0\) do not affect the limit and are omitted below.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.3 gives |X_j| ~ q_j^d

nodes.name: Bound on characters outside X(M_{j,0})
nodes.statement: |(\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\setminus X(M_{j,0}))(k_j)| \le\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)\,q_j^{d-1},
nodes.label: eq:cor-unram

nodes.name: Fix j
nodes.statement: Fix \(j\ge j_0\), and write \(k=k_j\), \(\bar k=\bar k_j\), \(q=q_j\), \(M_0=M_{j,0}\), \(M=M_j\), and \(X=X_j\). By \S\ref{sec:tannakian}, \(M\) is semisimple in \(\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\).
nodes.statement_short: Abbreviate notation

nodes.name: Reduce to Weyl sums
nodes.statement: Apply the Weyl criterion just recalled to the sets \(X_j\) and the unitary Frobenius conjugacy classes \(\theta_j(\chi)=\Theta_{M_{j,0},k_j}(\chi)\) of \ref{item:T5}. It suffices to show that, for every nontrivial irreducible algebraic representation \(\rho\) of the common reductive group \(G\), the sums in the criterion tend to zero. We prove the stronger estimate \begin{equation} \frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in X}\operatorname{Tr}\rho\bigl(\Theta_{M_0,k}(\chi)\bigr)\ll_\rho q^{-1/2}, \end{equation} with an implied constant independent of \(k\).
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the estimate (16)

nodes.name: Weyl-sum estimate O(q^{-1/2})
nodes.statement: \frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in X}\operatorname{Tr}\rho\bigl(\Theta_{M_0,k}(\chi)\bigr)\ll_\rho q^{-1/2},
nodes.label: eq:cor-weyl

nodes.name: Complexity of N
nodes.statement: For the remainder of the proof, constants may also depend on \(G\) and on \(\rho\), but not on \(j\). By \ref{item:T3}, the object \(N_0=\rho(M_0)\) is arithmetically semisimple and pure of weight zero. Its geometric base change \(N\) is a direct summand of \(L^{\ast_{\mathrm{int}}m(\rho)}\), where \(L=M\oplus M^\vee\) and \(m(\rho)\ge1\) depends only on \(\rho\) and \(G\). Put \[ C_\rho= F_{d,m(\rho),\mathrm{int}}\bigl(F_{d}(C)\bigr), \] with \(F_{d,m(\rho),\mathrm{int}}\) the convolution-power bound of Corollary~\ref{cor:convolution-complexity} and \(F_{d}\) the function of Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}. The direct-summand estimate \ref{item:C4} and Corollary~\ref{cor:convolution-complexity} give \(c_u(N)\le C_\rho\). This constant is independent of \(j\) and of \(k_j\).
nodes.statement_short: c_u(N) <= C_rho

nodes.name: Frobenius traces
nodes.statement: Write \(\tau_i(\chi)=\operatorname{Tr}(\operatorname{Fr}_k\mid \mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi))\), with \(\operatorname{Fr}_k\) the geometric Frobenius of \(k\). By \ref{item:T5}, one has \(\tau_i(\chi)=0\) for \(i\neq0\) and \(\operatorname{Tr}\rho(\Theta_{M_0,k}(\chi))=\tau_0(\chi)\) for every \(\chi\in X\).
nodes.statement_short: Trace of rho equals tau_0 on X

nodes.name: Sets A_i and B_rho
nodes.statement: For \(0<|i|\le d\) put \(\mathcal A_i=\{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}:\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\neq0\}\). By the definition of complexity \ref{item:C1}, the tensor-product estimate \ref{item:C3}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:kummer-complexity}, there is a constant \(B_\rho\), independent of \(j\) and of \(k_j\), such that \[ \dim\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\le c_u(N_\chi)\le B_\rho \qquad(i\in\mathbb Z,\ \chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d}(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})). \] We use the following three estimates.
nodes.statement_short: Define A_i and the dimension bound

nodes.name: Estimate (a)
nodes.statement: [(a)] \(\mathcal A_i\subseteq\mathcal V_{d,|i|}(N)\), so Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified} gives \(|\mathcal A_i|\le\Psi_{d}(C_\rho)\,q^{d-|i|}\).
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.2 bounds A_i

nodes.name: Estimate (b)
nodes.statement: [(b)] As \(N_0\) is pure of weight zero, \(\mathrm{H}^i_c(\mathbb{G}_m^d,N_\chi)\) has weights \(\le i\) \cite[3.3.1]{Del80}, \cite[5.1.13]{BBDG18}, so \(|\tau_i(\chi)|\le B_\rho\,q^{i/2}\).
nodes.statement_short: Weights bound tau_i

nodes.name: Estimate (c)
nodes.statement: [(c)] \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X|\le\Phi^{\mathrm{ur}}_{d}(C)q^{d-1}\) by \eqref{eq:cor-unram}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.3 bounds the complement

nodes.name: Decompose the Weyl sum
nodes.statement: For \(i\neq0\), the function \(\tau_i\) is supported on \(\mathcal A_i\subseteq\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X\). Hence \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in X}\tau_0(\chi) =\ &\frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}}\sum_{|i|\le d}(-1)^i\tau_i(\chi) -\frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{0<|i|\le d}(-1)^i\sum_{\chi\in\mathcal A_i}\tau_i(\chi)\\ &-\frac{1}{|X|}\sum_{\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\setminus X}\tau_0(\chi). \end{aligned} \] By the Grothendieck--Lefschetz trace formula \(\sum_{|i|\le d}(-1)^i\tau_i(\chi)=\sum_{x\in \mathbb{G}_m^d(k)} t_{N_0}(x;k)\,\chi(x)\), where \(t_{N_0}\) denotes the trace function of the arithmetic object \(N_0\). Summing over \(\chi\in\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}\) and using \(\sum_\chi\chi(x)=|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}|\) for \(x=1\) and \(\sum_\chi\chi(x)=0\) otherwise, the first term equals \((|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}|/|X|)\,t_{N_0}(1;k)\).
nodes.statement_short: Trace formula and orthogonality

nodes.name: Identity contribution
nodes.statement: It remains to bound the identity contribution \(t_{N_0}(1;k)\). By \ref{item:T1}, the tannakian unit is the skyscraper sheaf \(\delta_1\) at the identity. Since \(G^{\mathrm{ari}}_M=G^{\mathrm{geo}}_M=G\) and \(\rho\) is nontrivial and irreducible, \(\operatorname{Hom}(\delta_1,N)=0\) in \(\langle M\rangle\). Both inclusions \(\langle M\rangle\subseteq\operatorname{Perv}_{\mathrm{int}}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\subseteq\operatorname{Perv}(\mathbb{G}_m^d)\) are full, so \(N\) has no direct summand isomorphic to \(\delta_1\). By \ref{item:T3} and \S\ref{sec:tannakian}, \(N\) is semisimple. Lemma~\ref{lem:identity-stalk} therefore gives \(\mathcal{H}^j(N)_1=0\) for \(j\ge0\). Thus only degrees \(j\le-1\) contribute to \(t_{N_0}(1;k)\). Since \(N_0\) is pure of weight zero, the Frobenius eigenvalues on \(\mathcal{H}^j(N)_1\) have weights at most \(j\) \cite[1.2]{Del80}, \cite[5.1.8]{BBDG18} and therefore have absolute value at most \(q^{-1/2}\) in these degrees. Consequently, \[ |t_{N_0}(1;k)| \le q^{-1/2}\sum_{j\le-1}\dim\mathcal{H}^j(N)_1 \le F_{d}(C_\rho)q^{-1/2}, \] because \[ \sum_{j\le-1}\dim\mathcal{H}^j(N)_1 \le F_{d}(c_u(N)) \le F_{d}(C_\rho), \] where the first inequality is Lemma~\ref{lem:complexity-bounds}(i) and the second is monotonicity.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 and weights give O(q^{-1/2})

nodes.name: Bound the three terms
nodes.statement: As \(|\widehat{\mathbb{G}_m^d(k)}|\asymp|X|\), the first term is \(\ll_\rho q^{-1/2}\). By (a) and (b) the second term is \[ \ll_\rho\frac{1}{q^d}\sum_{1\le i\le d}q^{d-i}\,q^{i/2}\ll_\rho q^{-1/2}, \] the terms with \(i<0\) vanishing by Artin affine vanishing. By (b) and (c) the third term is \(\ll_\rho q^{d-1}\cdot B_\rho/q^d\ll_\rho q^{-1}\). This proves \eqref{eq:cor-weyl}.
nodes.statement_short: All three terms are O(q^{-1/2})

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: The trivial representation gives average one, so the Weyl criterion yields the equidistribution of the classes \(\Theta_{M_0,k}(\chi)\), \(\chi\in X(M_0)(k)\), in \(K_G^\sharp\) for the measure \(\mu_G^\sharp\) as \(\#k_j\to\infty\).
nodes.statement_short: Weyl criterion gives equidistribution

nodes.name: Kunneth isomorphism kappa_! for external products
nodes.statement: For \(f:X\to S\), \(g:Y\to T\), \(K\in D^b_c(X)\), and \(K'\in D^b_c(Y)\), let \[ \kappa_!:Rf_!K\boxtimes Rg_!K'\xrightarrow{\sim}R(f\times g)_!(K\boxtimes K') \] be the K\"unneth isomorphism \cite[Exp.~XVII, Th.~5.4.3]{SGA4}.
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation

nodes.name: Kunneth morphism kappa_*
nodes.statement: Let \[ \kappa_*:Rf_*K\boxtimes Rg_*K'\longrightarrow R(f\times g)_*(K\boxtimes K') \] be the morphism adjoint to the product of the counits.
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation

nodes.name: Forget-supports: independence and composition
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item The transformation \(\varphi_f\) does not depend on the compactification. Under the canonical identifications, \(\varphi_f=\operatorname{id}\) for \(f\) proper, and \(\varphi_f=\varphi_j\) for \(f=j\) an open immersion. \item For \(p\colon X\to Y\) and \(r\colon Y\to Z\), under the canonical isomorphisms \(R(rp)_!\simeq Rr_!\,Rp_!\) and \(R(rp)_*\simeq Rr_*\,Rp_*\), \[ \varphi_{rp}(K)=\varphi_r\bigl(Rp_*K\bigr)\circ Rr_!\bigl(\varphi_p(K)\bigr). \] \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
conclusions: The transformation \(\varphi_f\) does not depend on the compactification.
nodes.label: lem:forget-supports

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.1
nodes.statement: For an open immersion \(j\), the morphism \(\varphi_j(K)\) is characterized by \(j^*\varphi_j(K)=\operatorname{id}_K\). We use this characterization throughout. (1) Let \((j_i,\bar f_i)\), \(i=1,2\), be two compactifications of \(f\), and let \(\bar X_3\) be the closure of the image of \((j_1,j_2)\colon X\to\bar X_1\times_Y\bar X_2\). Write \(j_3\colon X\to\bar X_3\) for the induced map and \(r_i\colon\bar X_3\to\bar X_i\) for the proper projections. Since \(\bar X_{3-i}\to Y\) is separated, the graph of \(j_{3-i}\circ j_i^{-1}\) is closed over \(j_i(X)\), so \(r_i^{-1}(j_i(X))=j_3(X)\). Thus \(j_3\) is an open immersion with dense image, and \(\bar X_3\) is a third compactification. It remains to compare \((j',\bar f\circ q)\) with \((j,\bar f)\), where \(q\) is proper, \(q\circ j'=j\), and \(q^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)\). Proper base change gives a canonical isomorphism \[ j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rq_*j'_!K. \] Under this isomorphism and \(Rq_*Rj'_*=Rj_*\), the morphism \(Rq_*(\varphi_{j'}(K))\) pulls back along \(j\) to \(\operatorname{id}_K\), and therefore equals \(\varphi_j(K)\). Applying \(R\bar f_*\) proves independence. If \(f\) is proper, take \(j=\operatorname{id}\). If \(f=j\) is an open immersion, the transformation just constructed pulls back along \(j\) to the identity and hence equals \(\varphi_j\) by the characterization at the start of the proof. (2) Choose compactifications \(p=\bar p\circ j\) and \(r=\bar r\circ j'\), and choose a compactification \[ \bar X\xrightarrow{\ j''\ }\bar X''\xrightarrow{\ q\ }\bar Y' \] of \(j'\circ\bar p\colon\bar X\to\bar Y'\), with \(j''\) an open immersion with dense image and \(q\) proper \cite[Tag~0ATU]{stacks-project}. Since \(\bar X\) is proper over \(Y\) and \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))\) is separated over \(Y\), the induced morphism \(\bar X\to q^{-1}(j'(Y))\) is proper. Its image \(j''(\bar X)\) is therefore closed. It is also dense because \(j''(\bar X)\) is dense in \(\bar X''\). Thus \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))=j''(\bar X)\). Then \(rp=(\bar r\circ q)\circ(j''\circ j)\) is a compactification of \(rp\). The characterization above gives \[ \varphi_{j''j}(K)=\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\circ j''_!(\varphi_j(K)). \] For \(M\in D^b_c(\bar X)\), proper base change and the equality \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))=j''(\bar X)\) give a natural isomorphism \[ j'_!R\bar p_*M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rq_*j''_!M. \] Under this isomorphism and \(Rq_*Rj''_*=Rj'_*R\bar p_*\), the characterization of \(\varphi_{j'}\) gives \[ Rq_*(\varphi_{j''}(M))=\varphi_{j'}(R\bar p_*M). \] Apply \(R(\bar r\circ q)_*\) to the first identity and use the naturality of the intervening isomorphism. The composition isomorphisms of \cite[Exp.~XVII, \S5.1]{SGA4} then give \[ \varphi_{rp}(K) =R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\bigr] \circ R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*j''_!(\varphi_j(K))\bigr] =\varphi_r(Rp_*K)\circ Rr_!(\varphi_p(K)). \]
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement_short: Characterize phi_j by restriction to the identity; dominate two compactifications by a third and compose compactifications.

nodes.name: Characterization
nodes.statement: For an open immersion \(j\), the morphism \(\varphi_j(K)\) is characterized by \(j^*\varphi_j(K)=\operatorname{id}_K\). We use this characterization throughout.
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement_short: phi_j characterized by j^* phi_j = id

nodes.statement_short: Proper base change and the characterization

nodes.name: Part (2)
nodes.statement: (2) Choose compactifications \(p=\bar p\circ j\) and \(r=\bar r\circ j'\), and choose a compactification \[ \bar X\xrightarrow{\ j''\ }\bar X''\xrightarrow{\ q\ }\bar Y' \] of \(j'\circ\bar p\colon\bar X\to\bar Y'\), with \(j''\) an open immersion with dense image and \(q\) proper \cite[Tag~0ATU]{stacks-project}. The characterization above gives \[ \varphi_{j''j}(K)=\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\circ j''_!(\varphi_j(K)). \] For \(M\in D^b_c(\bar X)\), proper base change and the equality \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))=j''(\bar X)\) give a natural isomorphism \[ j'_!R\bar p_*M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rq_*j''_!M. \] Under this isomorphism and \(Rq_*Rj''_*=Rj'_*R\bar p_*\), the characterization of \(\varphi_{j'}\) gives \[ Rq_*(\varphi_{j''}(M))=\varphi_{j'}(R\bar p_*M). \] Apply \(R(\bar r\circ q)_*\) to the first identity and use the naturality of the intervening isomorphism. The composition isomorphisms of \cite[Exp.~XVII, \S5.1]{SGA4} then give \[ \varphi_{rp}(K) =R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\bigr] \circ R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*j''_!(\varphi_j(K))\bigr] =\varphi_r(Rp_*K)\circ Rr_!(\varphi_p(K)). \]
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement_short: Composition formula

nodes.name: Compactify the composite
nodes.statement: (2) Choose compactifications \(p=\bar p\circ j\) and \(r=\bar r\circ j'\), and choose a compactification \[ \bar X\xrightarrow{\ j''\ }\bar X''\xrightarrow{\ q\ }\bar Y' \] of \(j'\circ\bar p\colon\bar X\to\bar Y'\), with \(j''\) an open immersion with dense image and \(q\) proper \cite[Tag~0ATU]{stacks-project}. Since \(\bar X\) is proper over \(Y\) and \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))\) is separated over \(Y\), the induced morphism \(\bar X\to q^{-1}(j'(Y))\) is proper. Its image \(j''(\bar X)\) is therefore closed. It is also dense because \(j''(\bar X)\) is dense in \(\bar X''\). Thus \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))=j''(\bar X)\). Then \(rp=(\bar r\circ q)\circ(j''\circ j)\) is a compactification of \(rp\). The characterization above gives \[ \varphi_{j''j}(K)=\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\circ j''_!(\varphi_j(K)). \]
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement_short: Build a compactification of rp

nodes.name: Compose
nodes.statement: For \(M\in D^b_c(\bar X)\), proper base change and the equality \(q^{-1}(j'(Y))=j''(\bar X)\) give a natural isomorphism \[ j'_!R\bar p_*M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rq_*j''_!M. \] Under this isomorphism and \(Rq_*Rj''_*=Rj'_*R\bar p_*\), the characterization of \(\varphi_{j'}\) gives \[ Rq_*(\varphi_{j''}(M))=\varphi_{j'}(R\bar p_*M). \] Apply \(R(\bar r\circ q)_*\) to the first identity and use the naturality of the intervening isomorphism. The composition isomorphisms of \cite[Exp.~XVII, \S5.1]{SGA4} then give \[ \varphi_{rp}(K) =R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*\varphi_{j''}(Rj_*K)\bigr] \circ R\bar r_*\bigl[Rq_*j''_!(\varphi_j(K))\bigr] =\varphi_r(Rp_*K)\circ Rr_!(\varphi_p(K)). \]
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.statement_short: Proper base change and composition isomorphisms

nodes.name: Forget-supports: external products and lisse projection formula
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item For \(f:X\to S\), \(g:Y\to T\), \(K\in D^b_c(X)\), and \(K'\in D^b_c(Y)\), one has \[ \varphi_{f\times g}(K\boxtimes K')\circ\kappa_! =\kappa_*\circ\bigl(\varphi_f(K)\boxtimes\varphi_g(K')\bigr). \] \item Let \(p:X\to Y\), let \(\mathcal{L}\) be a lisse \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-sheaf on \(Y\), and let \(K\in D^b_c(X,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\). Under this isomorphism and the projection-formula identification for \(Rp_!\), the morphism \(\varphi_p(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L})\) identifies with \(\varphi_p(K)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{L}}\). \end{enumerate}
nodes.section: A Compatibilities of the forget-supports transformation
nodes.label: lem:forget-supports-products

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.2
nodes.statement: (1) Compactify \(f=\bar f\circ j_X\) and \(g=\bar g\circ j_Y\). Then \(f\times g=(\bar f\times\bar g)\circ j\) with \(j=j_X\times j_Y\) an open immersion and \(\bar f\times\bar g\) proper. Under the canonical identification \(j_!(K\boxtimes K')\simeq j_{X!}K\boxtimes j_{Y!}K'\), let \(c\colon Rj_{X*}K\boxtimes Rj_{Y*}K'\to Rj_*(K\boxtimes K')\) be the morphism adjoint to the identity after pullback by \(j\). The characterization of the forget-supports transformation for an open immersion gives \[ \varphi_j(K\boxtimes K') =c\circ\bigl(\varphi_{j_X}K\boxtimes\varphi_{j_Y}K'\bigr). \] Apply \(R(\bar f\times\bar g)_*\) and the K\"unneth isomorphism for the proper morphisms \(\bar f,\bar g\) \cite[Exp.~XVII, Th.~5.4.3]{SGA4}. The left side becomes \(\varphi_{f\times g}(K\boxtimes K')\circ\kappa_!\), while \(c\) induces \(\kappa_*\). This gives~(1). (2) We first prove the formula for \(Rp_*\). Since \(\mathcal{L}\) is lisse of finite rank, it is dualizable. Write \(\mathcal{L}^\vee\) for its dual. For every \(M\in D^b_c(Y,\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), duality for \(\mathcal{L}\) and \(p^*\mathcal{L}\), together with the adjunction \(p^*\dashv Rp_*\), gives natural isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Hom}_Y(M,Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}) &\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_Y(M\otimes\mathcal{L}^\vee,Rp_*K)\\ &\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_X(p^*M\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}^\vee,K)\\ &\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_X(p^*M,K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L})\\ &\simeq \operatorname{Hom}_Y(M,Rp_*(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L})). \end{aligned} \] By Yoneda, these give an isomorphism \[ Rp_*K\otimes\mathcal{L}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp_*(K\otimes p^*\mathcal{L}). \] Its adjoint is the tensor product of the counit \(p^*Rp_*K\to K\) with \(\operatorname{id}_{p^*\mathcal{L}}\), so this is the usual natural morphism. Choose a compactification \(p=\bar p\circ j\) in the definition of \(\varphi_p\), so that \(\varphi_p=R\bar p_*(\varphi_j)\), and put \(\mathcal{M}=\bar p^*\mathcal{L}\). The \(!\)-projection formula and the formula for \(Rj_*\) just proved give \[ j_!K\otimes\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j_!(K\otimes j^*\mathcal{M}), \qquad Rj_*K\otimes\mathcal{M}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rj_*(K\otimes j^*\mathcal{M}). \] Under these isomorphisms, both \(\varphi_j(K\otimes j^*\mathcal{M})\) and \(\varphi_j(K)\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal{M}}\) pull back to the identity, and hence they agree. Apply \(R\bar p_*\) and the proper projection formula \cite[Exp.~XVII, Prop.~5.2.9]{SGA4}, \cite[Prop.~A.1.5(ii)]{GabberLoeser1996} to obtain~(2).

nodes.name: Pushforward commutes with constant tensor factors
nodes.statement: Let \(f\colon X\to Y\) be any morphism of schemes and let \(V\) be a finite-dimensional \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-vector space. For \(Z=X,Y\), let \(V_Z\) be the constant sheaf on \(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}\) associated with \(V\). The tensor products below are derived tensor products of \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-sheaves. For \(K\in D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell})\), the natural morphism \begin{equation} \theta_{K,V}\colon Rf_*K\otimes_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}V_Y \longrightarrow Rf_*(K\otimes_{\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}}V_X) \end{equation} is an isomorphism, naturally in \(K\) and in \(V\).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma A.3

nodes.name: Prime-to-l continuous cohomology vanishes
nodes.statement: Let \(H\) be a profinite group all of whose finite quotients have order prime to \(\ell\), and let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional continuous \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-representation of \(H\). Then continuous cohomology is concentrated in degree \(0\). \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,M)\simeq M^H, \qquad H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,M)=0\quad(a>0). \] The same conclusion holds when \(M\) is a finite discrete \(H\)-module of \(\ell\)-power order.
nodes.section: B Continuous cohomology of inertia groups
assumptions: \(H\) be a profinite group all of whose finite quotients have order prime to \(\ell\)
nodes.label: lem:prime-to-ell-vanishing

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.1
nodes.statement: Choose a finite extension \(E/\mathbb Q_\ell\) over which \(M\) is defined (\S\ref{sec:sheaves}), a uniformizer \(\varpi\) of \(E\), and an \(H\)-stable \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice \(\Lambda\subset M\). Continuous cochains with values in \(\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\) factor through finite quotients \(Q\) of \(H\). The order of every such \(Q\) is prime to \(\ell\), hence is invertible on \(\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\), and the norm idempotent \[ e_Q=\frac{1}{\lvert Q\rvert}\sum_{g\in Q}g \] projects onto \(Q\)-invariants. Thus \(Q\)-invariants are exact on these modules. Passing over the finite quotients gives \[ H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)=0 \qquad(a>0). \] Let \[ K_n=\ker\bigl(\Lambda/\varpi^{n+1}\Lambda\longrightarrow\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\bigr). \] The same argument gives \(H^1_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,K_n)=0\). The long exact sequence therefore shows that the transition maps on \(H^0_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)=(\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)^H\) are surjective. In Jannsen's exact sequence \cite[(2.1)]{Jannsen88} \[ 0\to{\varprojlim_n}^{1}\,H^{a-1}_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda) \to H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda) \to\varprojlim_n H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)\to0, \] the right term vanishes for \(a>0\). If \(a>1\), the left term vanishes by the same cohomology vanishing. If \(a=1\), it is \({\varprojlim_n}^{1}(\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda)^H\), which vanishes because the transition maps are surjective. Extending scalars to \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) proves the assertion. For a finite discrete module \(M\) of \(\ell\)-power order, continuous cochains factor through finite quotients of \(H\), and the norm idempotent gives the same conclusion.
nodes.section: B Continuous cohomology of inertia groups
nodes.statement_short: Norm idempotents kill higher cohomology at finite level; Jannsen's sequence passes to the limit.

nodes.statement: Choose a finite extension \(E/\mathbb Q_\ell\) over which \(M\) is defined (\S\ref{sec:sheaves}), a uniformizer \(\varpi\) of \(E\), and an \(H\)-stable \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice \(\Lambda\subset M\). nodes.name: Continuous cohomology of Z_l
nodes.statement: Let \(\Gamma\simeq\mathbb Z_\ell\) with topological generator \(\gamma\), and let \(M\) be a finite-dimensional continuous \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\)-representation of \(\Gamma\). Then \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma,M) \simeq \bigl[M\xrightarrow{\gamma-1}M\bigr], \] where the first copy of \(M\) in the two-term complex on the right is in degree \(0\). The same description holds when \(M\) is instead a finite discrete \(\Gamma\)-module of \(\ell\)-power order.
nodes.section: B Continuous cohomology of inertia groups
nodes.label: lem:zell-cohomology

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma B.2
nodes.statement: Choose an \(E\)-model \(M_E\) of \(M\), for a finite extension \(E/\mathbb Q_\ell\) with uniformizer \(\varpi\), and a \(\Gamma\)-stable \(\mathcal O_E\)-lattice \(\Lambda\subset M_E\) (\S\ref{sec:sheaves}). Put \(\Lambda_n=\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda\). For every \(n\), the completed group algebra satisfies \[ (\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)[[\Gamma]]\simeq(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)[[T]], \qquad \gamma\longmapsto1+T, \] and the augmentation identifies the trivial module \(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n\) with the quotient by \(T=\gamma-1\). Multiplication by \(T\) is injective in a formal power-series ring, so \[ 0\longrightarrow(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)[[\Gamma]] \xrightarrow{\ \gamma-1\ }(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)[[\Gamma]] \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{aug}\ }(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)\longrightarrow0 \] is a free resolution of the trivial module. Applying continuous module homomorphisms into \(\Lambda_n\) gives, functorially and compatibly in \(n\), \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma,\Lambda_n) \simeq \bigl[\Lambda_n\xrightarrow{\gamma-1}\Lambda_n\bigr]. \] For the identification of the cohomology of this two-term complex with continuous cohomology at each finite level see \cite[Prop.~1.7.7]{NSW2008}. The transition maps of these two-term complexes are termwise surjective, so the derived inverse limit is the termwise inverse limit, and the definition in \S\ref{sec:sheaves} gives \[ R\Gamma_{\mathrm{cts}}(\Gamma,M_E) \simeq \bigl[M_E\xrightarrow{\gamma-1}M_E\bigr]. \] Extending scalars to \(\ol\mathbb{Q}_{\ell}\) proves the assertion. For a finite discrete \(\Gamma\)-module \(A\) of \(\ell\)-power order, choose \(n\) with \(\ell^nA=0\). The same free resolution over \((\mathbb Z/\ell^n)[[\Gamma]]\) applies directly.
nodes.section: B Continuous cohomology of inertia groups
nodes.statement_short: Free resolution of the trivial module over the Iwasawa algebra, then pass to the limit.

nodes.statement_short: Same resolution over Z/l^n
